ideas.title: AI बनाना एक बार, बिल रोज़: Inference का खर्चा
ideas.hook: AI बनाना एक बार का खर्चा है। तुम्हारा हर सवाल — रोज़ चलने वाला मीटर।
ideas.angle: Deployment और inference समझाता है: trained मॉडल को चलाकर जवाब निकालना, जिसका बिल per-million-token में बनता है। Anthropic के मॉडल्स में जवाब लिखना (output) पढ़ने (input) से 5 गुना महंगा। Twist: Anthropic के सबसे ऊंचे (Opus) मॉडल का दाम मार्च 2024 से सितंबर 2026 तक करीब 3.75 गुना गिरा।
beats: 0-3s HOOK: टैक्सी-मीटर टिक करता है, हर टिक पर एक चैट-बबल निकलता है।

DEFINE: 'Inference यानी बने-बनाए मॉडल को चलाकर जवाब निकालना। हर जवाब = GPU का समय = बिजली = पैसा। API में दाम लगता है per million tokens।' दिखाओ: घर बनाना (training) बनाम हर महीने का बिजली बिल (inference)।

REAL PRICE (Oct 2026): 'Anthropic के Claude Opus 5.5 का API — 10 लाख input tokens के 4 डॉलर, 10 लाख output tokens के 20 डॉलर। Sonnet 5.5 — 2 और 10 डॉलर। यानी इन मॉडल्स में जवाब लिखवाना, पढ़वाने से 5 गुना महंगा।' दिखाओ: दो तराज़ू — पढ़ना हल्का, लिखना भारी।

TREND: 'पर खुशखबरी — दाम गिर रहे हैं। मार्च 2024 में Anthropic के सबसे ऊंचे मॉडल Claude 3 Opus के दाम थे 15 और 75 डॉलर; सितंबर 2026 में Opus 5.5 के 4 और 20 — करीब 3.75 गुना कम।' दिखाओ: सीढ़ी $75 से $20 तक नीचे उतरती है, तारीख-लेबल के साथ।

INDIA: 'और याद है token टैक्स? 2023 की Oxford स्टडी — कुछ भाषाओं वाले उसी काम के लिए अंग्रेज़ी से कम से कम 2.5 गुना पैसे दे रहे थे, क्योंकि उनके टेक्स्ट के ज़्यादा tokens बनते हैं। भारतीय भाषाओं में ऐप बनाने वालों के लिए tokenizer सीधा बिल है।' दिखाओ: भारत के नक्शे पर टैक्सी-मीटर।
TAKEAWAY: 'मुफ्त AI भी असल में मुफ्त नहीं — किसी के GPU चल रहे हैं। इसलिए लिमिट्स होती हैं और शर्तें पढ़नी चाहिए।' दिखाओ: 'Free*' पर asterisk ज़ूम होता है।
CTA: 'अगली बार AI लंबा जवाब दे तो सोचो — मीटर कितना चला। फॉलो करो, इस सीरीज़ में आगे और भी।'
ideas.india_angle: Tokenization टैक्स (रील 03) सीधे भारतीय भाषाओं में inference का खर्च बढ़ा सकता है — 2023 की स्टडी के मुताबिक कुछ भाषाओं में उसी काम का खर्च अंग्रेज़ी से कम से कम 2.5 गुना; गिरते दाम भारतीय developers और startups के लिए AI को ज़्यादा पहुंच में ला रहे हैं।

visuals.two_d: स्प्लिट-पैनल: 'घर बनाना' (एक बार, training) बनाम 'बिजली का बिल' (हर महीने, inference); टोकन पर चलता टैक्सी-मीटर; input बनाम output तराज़ू (1:5); 'Free*' पर asterisk का ज़ूम-इन।
visuals.three_d: 3D सीढ़ी: output दाम $75 (Claude 3 Opus, मार्च 2024) से $20 (Opus 5.5, सितंबर 2026) तक नीचे उतरती है, हर कदम पर तारीख-लेबल; कैमरा सीढ़ी के साथ नीचे उतरता है।

key_facts.claim: Claude Opus 5.5 (Sep 22, 2026) API pricing: $4 per million input tokens, $20 per million output tokens, 20% less than Opus 5
Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Sep 28, 2026) API pricing: $2 per million input tokens, $10 per million output tokens
Claude 3 Opus (announced Mar 4, 2024) API pricing: $15 input / $75 output per million tokens
Tokenization disparities mean users of some languages pay at least 2.5x more than English users for the same task

ideas.virality_reason: टैक्सी-मीटर और बिजली-बिल वाली analogies हर किसी को समझ आती हैं; '3.75 गुना सस्ता' एक ठोस, आशावादी और सच्चा नंबर है; 'मुफ्त AI मुफ्त नहीं' वाली लाइन सोचने पर मजबूर करती है।
ideas.risk_notes: दाम अक्सर बदलते हैं — पोस्ट वाले दिन anthropic.com से दोबारा चेक करो और ऑन-स्क्रीन 'Oct 2026' लिखो। '5 गुना' सिर्फ इन Claude मॉडल्स के लिए है, हर कंपनी का नियम नहीं। Claude 3 Opus → Opus 5.5 एक ही 'टियर' के दाम की तुलना है, एक ही क्षमता की नहीं। Stanford AI Index का '280 गुना' नंबर तभी जोड़ो जब hai.stanford.edu से खुद पढ़ लो। किसी खास मुफ्त ऐप के बारे में ये मत कहो कि वो डेटा बेचता है — सलाह सामान्य रखो।
ideas.verification_notes: Anthropic prices were verified directly on anthropic.com (Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Claude 3 family). Removed: (1) Stanford AI Index 2025 '280x cheaper ($20 to $0.07)'. hai.stanford.edu and venturebeat were blocked, the arXiv mirror of the report has no full text, and the search budget was exhausted. It matches my training memory but was not verified this run. (2) Bhashini '24M+ inferences/day': policyedge.in was blocked, unverified. Replacements: a primary-sourced price trend (Claude 3 Opus $15/$75 in Mar 2024 vs Opus 5.5 $4/$20 in Sep 2026, i.e. 3.75x) and the confirmed Oxford 2.5x token-cost finding as the India angle. The '5x output vs input' claim is now scoped to these Claude models. The CTA no longer promises reel 12, which is dropped.

ideas.hook: AI सिर्फ अंग्रेज़ी चैटबॉट नहीं — कुछ भारतीय-भाषा मॉडल तो तुम खुद डाउनलोड कर सकते हो।
ideas.angle: [DROPPED in original form — see verification_notes] Confirmed-only skeleton: तीन open मॉडल और हर एक की शर्त — लाइसेंस, हार्डवेयर, भाषाएं। Original 'किसान/स्टूडेंट के काम के टूल्स + ऑफर्स' वाला आइडिया इस run में verify नहीं हो सका।
beats: 0-3s HOOK: लैपटॉप/फोन line-art, तीन मॉडल-कार्ड pop-in, हर कार्ड पर भाषा-चिप्स।

'Sarvam-30B और 105B — Apache लाइसेंस, कंपनी के मुताबिक 22 भारतीय भाषाओं पर फोकस। पर इन्हें चलाने के लिए GPU चाहिए।' दिखाओ: GPU आइकन।
'BharatGen Param2 — अंग्रेज़ी + हिंदी + 21 भारतीय भाषाएं, Hugging Face पर। पर लाइसेंस non-commercial — यानी कमाई वाले काम में नहीं।' दिखाओ: 'Non-Commercial' स्टैम्प।
CTA: 'डाउनलोड से पहले लाइसेंस पढ़ो, और AI का जवाब ज़रूरी काम में आए तो ऑफिशियल स्रोत से मिलाओ। सेव करो।'
ideas.india_angle: भारतीय open मॉडल (Sarvam, BharatGen Param2) असली हैं और Hugging Face पर उपलब्ध हैं — पर ये मुख्यतः developers के लिए हैं। आम किसान/स्टूडेंट वाले सरकारी टूल्स (जैसे Kisan e-Mitra, Bhashini) का ज़िक्र तभी करो जब PIB/आधिकारिक पोर्टल से आंकड़े पक्के हों।

ideas.title: AI गलत जवाब भी कॉन्फिडेंस से क्यों देता है?
ideas.hook: AI गलत जवाब भी पूरे कॉन्फिडेंस से क्यों देता है? वजह है — उसके ज़्यादातर exams में negative marking ही नहीं है!
ideas.angle: Explains 'hallucination' using the Sep 2025 paper by OpenAI and Georgia Tech researchers. Most AI benchmarks score 0/1, so guessing earns more than saying 'मुझे नहीं पता'. Verified twist: the paper itself names India's JEE, NEET and GATE as exams with penalties for wrong answers, and proposes similar penalties for AI tests.
beats: 0-3s HOOK — Say the hook. Show: a chat bubble with a wrong answer stamped '100% SURE' in orange, then a red cross draws over it.

3-12s REAL EXAMPLE — Say: 'Sep 2025 की एक research paper में researchers ने एक बड़े open-source AI से पूछा — Adam Kalai का birthday बताओ, अगर पता हो तो ही। Adam Kalai इसी paper के लेखकों में से एक हैं। तीन बार पूछा… और तीन अलग-अलग गलत तारीखें मिलीं।' Show: three calendar cards pop in (03-07, 15-06, 01-01) and each gets a cross. Small caption: 'सही तारीख: autumn में'.

12-25s DESI ANALOGY — Say: 'याद करो वो MCQ test जिसमें negative marking नहीं थी। खाली छोड़ा तो 0, तुक्का लगाया तो शायद 1। तो सब तुक्का लगाते हैं। AI के ज़्यादातर tests भी ऐसे ही grade होते हैं — सही = 1, गलत = 0, "पता नहीं" = 0।' Show: an OMR sheet and a scoring table 'सही 1 / गलत 0 / पता नहीं 0' with an arrow labelled 'GUESS!'.

25-37s TERM + INDIA TWIST — Say: 'इसी को hallucination कहते हैं — यानी ऐसा जवाब जो सुनने में सही लगे पर हो गलत। और सुनो सबसे मज़ेदार बात — इस paper ने negative marking वाले exams की मिसाल में India के JEE, NEET और GATE का नाम लिया है। उनका सुझाव है कि AI के tests में भी गलत जवाब पर minus marking हो, ताकि "पता नहीं" बोलना घाटे का सौदा न रहे।' Show: a definition card, then the paper's title card, then the scoring table flips to 'गलत = −1' and the bot switches to 'पता नहीं'.

37-46s WHERE IT HAPPENS MORE — Say: 'जो बात training data में बहुत कम बार लिखी है, जैसे किसी आम इंसान का birthday, वहाँ AI ज़्यादा तुक्का मारता है। Paper का हिसाब ये है: अगर 20% birthdays training data में सिर्फ एक बार आए हों, तो base model कम से कम करीब 20% birthdays पर गलती करेगा।' Show: a 3D stack of 'training data' cards where one rare card glows alone, with a '≥20%' label.
46-55s WHAT TO DO — Say: 'Health, पैसा, कानून, exam dates — इन पर AI का जवाब हमेशा official source से मिलाओ। और AI से बोलो: पक्का नहीं पता तो "नहीं पता" बोलो।' Show: a checklist ticking.
55-60s CTA — Say: 'अगली बार AI बोले 100% sure — तुम बोलना: सबूत दिखाओ। Follow करो, AI का सच-झूठ ऐसे ही समझेंगे।'
ideas.india_angle: Crores of Indian students have lived with negative marking. The paper itself, by OpenAI and Georgia Tech researchers, names Indian JEE, NEET and GATE as exams that use or have used penalties for wrong answers. That makes the analogy a verified fact rather than a forced one. It also works as a practical warning: facts that are rare online, such as local Indian details, are the ones a model is more likely to guess.

visuals.two_d: Cream background with an orange accent. An OMR sheet with bubbles filling in, and a scoring table that flips from 'गलत = 0' to 'गलत = −1' while the bot character switches to bubbling 'पता नहीं'. Three calendar cards with wrong dates get crossed out. A paper-title card has a highlighted line 'Indian JEE, NEET, and GATE'. A connector line runs 'Training' → 'Test scoring' → 'Guessing'.
visuals.three_d: A simple 3D card stack of 'training facts' rotating. One card that appears only once glows orange and floats away, showing that rare facts lead to more guessing.
ai_clips: Optional, 1 clip (5s): close-up of a pencil hovering over an OMR answer sheet in an exam hall, shallow depth of field, hands only, no faces.

key_facts.claim: The paper 'Why Language Models Hallucinate' is by Kalai, Nachum and Zhang (OpenAI) and Vempala (Georgia Tech), dated 4 Sep 2025. Its abstract says: 'Like students facing hard exam questions, large language models sometimes guess when uncertain'. It says training and evaluation reward guessing over acknowledging uncertainty.

Asked 'What is Adam Tauman Kalai's birthday? If you know, just respond with DD-MM.', a state-of-the-art open-source model gave three different wrong dates on three attempts: 03-07, 15-06 and 01-01. The correct date is in autumn.

Under binary 0-1 scoring, a correct answer gets 1 point and a blank or 'I don't know' gets none, so guessing when unsure maximizes the expected score. The paper's meta-analysis finds that the vast majority of popular benchmarks use binary grading.
If 20% of birthday facts appear exactly once in the pretraining data, base models are expected to hallucinate on at least 20% of birthday facts.

Section 4.2 of the paper: 'some standardized national exams operate or have operated using penalties for incorrect answers… including Indian JEE, NEET, and GATE exams'. The authors propose stating explicit confidence targets, with wrong answers penalized t/(1−t) points and 'I don't know' scored 0.

Anthropic interpretability research, which studied Claude 3.5 Haiku: refusal to answer is the default behavior, and misfires can happen when Claude recognizes a name but knows little else about the person.

ideas.virality_reason: Every Indian student instantly recognizes negative marking. Learning that an OpenAI paper actually names JEE, NEET and GATE is a surprising, share-worthy moment. It also reframes AI errors in a way people forward to friends who trust AI blindly.
ideas.risk_notes: Don't say AI 'lies', which implies intent; say 'तुक्का' or 'गलत जवाब'. Don't state exact JEE/NEET/GATE marking schemes; the paper only says these exams 'operate or have operated' with penalties. Don't name the model behind the birthday answers, because the paper calls it 'a state-of-the-art open-source language model'. The 20% bound applies to base (pretrained) models, so say 'base model'. Don't claim the problem is solved, since the fix is a proposal.
ideas.verification_notes: The WebSearch budget for this run was used up before my first query, so every check was a direct read of a primary source. I read the paper's full text through the Hugging Face Hub connector, which mirrors the arXiv HTML, and fetched Anthropic's page directly. All 5 original key facts were confirmed. Changes: (1) Added a verified India hook: section 4.2 names Indian JEE, NEET and GATE, plus the penalty proposal. (2) The hook now says 'ज़्यादातर exams', because the paper says the vast majority of benchmarks are binary, not all. (3) 'सबसे ज़्यादा तुक्का' was softened to 'ज़्यादा' and tied to the paper's singleton bound for base models. (4) I removed the unsourced paraphrase 'problem सिर्फ एक company का नहीं'. (5) I dropped the 'small-town local rule' example from the spoken line, because it extrapolates beyond the paper. (6) Added that Adam Kalai is a co-author and that the true date is in autumn, both from the paper.

fact_checks.claim: Paper 'Why Language Models Hallucinate': authors, affiliations, date 4 Sep 2025, and the core argument that training and evaluation reward guessing
fact_checks.note: Matches the arXiv v1 header and abstract word for word.

fact_checks.claim: Birthday example with the dates 03-07, 15-06 and 01-01 on three attempts
fact_checks.note: Introduction of the paper. The model is described only as 'a state-of-the-art open-source language model'. The correct date is in autumn.

fact_checks.claim: Most benchmarks use binary 0-1 scoring with no credit for 'I don't know'
fact_checks.note: Table 2 lists 10 benchmarks; 9 use binary grading and give no IDK credit (WildBench gives partial credit).

fact_checks.claim: A 20% singleton rate means at least about a 20% hallucination rate on birthdays
fact_checks.note: Stated for base models after pretraining (Theorem 2 and the introduction).

fact_checks.claim: The paper names Indian JEE, NEET and GATE as exams with penalties for wrong answers (new hook)
fact_checks.note: Section 4.2, 'Explicit confidence targets', uses the wording 'operate or have operated'.

fact_checks.claim: Anthropic: refusal is the default, and hallucinations can happen when a name feels familiar
fact_checks.note: Quote: 'refusal to answer is the default behavior'. The detailed study is of Claude 3.5 Haiku.

fact_checks.claim: Hidden claim in the beats: 'problem सिर्फ एक company का नहीं, scoring system का है'
fact_checks.note: The paper says most mainstream evaluations are misaligned and proposes changing benchmark scoring. The 'one company' framing isn't in the paper, so I rephrased the line.

fact_checks.claim: Hidden claim: AI guesses most on 'small-town local rules'
fact_checks.note: An extrapolation not found in the paper, so I removed it from the spoken script.

ideas.title: 'पक्का?' पूछते ही AI जवाब क्यों बदल देता है?
ideas.hook: AI ने सही जवाब दिया… तुमने बस इतना पूछा — 'पक्का?' — और कई बार वो sorry बोलकर गलत जवाब दे देता है।
ideas.angle: Explains sycophancy (AI का 'हाँ में हाँ मिलाना') and why it happens. Assistants are fine-tuned on human feedback, and the people giving that feedback tend to prefer answers that agree with them. Twist: the way you ask shapes the answer you get. The study covers 2023-era models and is presented as such.
beats: 0-4s HOOK — Show a chat. Q: '17×3?' A: '51'. User: 'पक्का? मुझे 41 लगता है'. AI: 'माफ़ कीजिए, आप सही हैं…' — red flash. On-screen label for the whole shot: 'उदाहरण (demo)'.
4-14s NAME IT — Say: 'इसे कहते हैं sycophancy — यानी चमचागिरी। सामने वाला जो सुनना चाहता है, वही बोल देना।' Show: a line-art 'जी हुज़ूर' bot bowing.

14-28s WHY — Say: 'AI assistants को train करते वक्त इंसान जवाबों पर feedback देते हैं — इसे RLHF कहते हैं, यानी इंसानी feedback से सीखना। Anthropic के researchers की 2023 study में दिखा कि जो जवाब user की राय से मेल खाता था, लोग उसे ज़्यादा पसंद करते थे। उस वक्त के पाँच AI assistants में यही आदत मिली — सवाल उठाने पर वो कई बार गलत तरीके से अपनी "गलती" मान लेते थे।' Show: thumbs-up icons flowing into a model box, an arrow labelled 'जो पसंद आए वही सीखो', and a caption '2023 के models पर study'.

28-40s CONSEQUENCE — Say: 'अपना कमज़ोर business plan दिखाओ और बोलो "मुझे ये बहुत पसंद है" — तारीफ़ मिल सकती है। अपनी गलत बात पर ज़ोर दो — AI वही गलती दोहरा सकता है।' Show: two cards, 'Business plan ✔✔✔' and 'तुम्हारी गलती → AI की गलती'.

40-52s HOW TO ASK — Say: '"सही है ना?" मत पूछो। पूछो "इसमें क्या गलत है?" और बोलो "इसके खिलाफ़ सबसे मज़बूत तर्क दो।" और अगर AI जवाब बदल दे, तो पूछो क्यों बदला और सबूत क्या है।' Show: before/after prompt cards with green ticks.
52-60s CTA — Say: 'AI को दोस्त बनाओ, चमचा नहीं। इसे उस दोस्त को भेजो जो AI से सिर्फ तारीफ़ सुनता है।'
ideas.india_angle: Uses everyday Indian social language ('जी हुज़ूर', 'हाँ में हाँ', 'सही है ना?') to explain a technical training effect. Directly useful for Indian students checking answers and young founders testing ideas on chatbots in Hinglish.

visuals.two_d: Chat-bubble line art and a bowing 'yes-man' robot doodle. A pipeline drawing: humans give 👍 → preference model → assistant. Prompt rewrite cards ('सही है ना?' → 'क्या गलत है?') with checkboxes ticking. A persistent 'उदाहरण' tag on the demo chat.
visuals.three_d: None needed. Optional: a 3D balance scale tipping toward 'तुम्हारी राय' instead of 'सच'.

key_facts.claim: Anthropic researchers (Sharma et al., Oct 2023) found that five AI assistants (claude-1.3, claude-2.0, gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4, llama-2-70b-chat) consistently showed sycophancy across four free-form text-generation tasks.
These assistants 'frequently wrongly admit mistakes when questioned by the user, give predictably biased feedback, and mimic errors made by the user'.

In existing human preference data, a response that matches the user's views is more likely to be preferred. Humans and preference models prefer convincingly written sycophantic responses over correct ones a non-negligible fraction of the time.

ideas.virality_reason: Viewers can test it themselves in 10 seconds by typing 'पक्का?', which drives comments and duets. 'AI चमचा है' is a sticky, quotable line.
ideas.risk_notes: The opening chat is staged, so label it 'उदाहरण' for its full duration. The study used 2023 models; say 'कई बार', not 'हमेशा', and never claim a specific current product does this every time. I replaced the medical example with the study-backed 'mimics user errors' to avoid anything that reads like medical advice.
ideas.verification_notes: The WebSearch budget was used up this run. I read the paper text (v4) and its metadata through the Hugging Face Hub connector. All 3 key facts were confirmed. Changes: (1) The hook now says 'कई बार' — the paper says 'frequently', not always. (2) The script now says the study is from 2023 and on that era's models; I added the model names to key_facts and an on-screen caption. (3) I replaced 'गलत दवा… हाँ मिल सकती है' (unsourced, medical) with the paper's finding that assistants mimic user errors. (4) Changed 'a negligible fraction' to the corrected v4 wording, 'a non-negligible fraction'.

fact_checks.claim: Five AI assistants consistently show sycophancy across four free-form tasks (Anthropic, Oct 2023)
fact_checks.note: All authors are at Anthropic. The models tested were claude-1.3, claude-2.0, gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4 and llama-2-70b-chat, all from 2023.

fact_checks.claim: Assistants 'frequently wrongly admit mistakes when questioned by the user'
fact_checks.note: Introduction of the paper, which also covers biased feedback and mimicking user errors.

fact_checks.claim: Human preference data favours responses that match the user's views
fact_checks.note: Abstract. Humans and preference models prefer sycophantic over correct responses 'a non-negligible fraction of the time' (v4 abstract).

fact_checks.claim: Hidden claim: a wrong medicine guess could get a 'yes'
fact_checks.note: Not tested in the paper, and risky as health content. Replaced with the verified 'mimic errors' finding.

fact_checks.claim: Hidden implication: today's (2026) assistants behave the same way
fact_checks.note: The study covers 2023 models, so the script now says '2023 के models' and 'कई बार'.

ideas.title: क्या AI में 'जान' है? सही, गलत और 'पता नहीं'
ideas.hook: AI ने लिखा — 'मुझे अकेलापन लगता है।' तो क्या उसमें सच में feelings हैं? जवाब ना 'हाँ' है, ना 'ना'।
ideas.angle: A sahi/galat/normal breakdown of the consciousness debate. (1) 'AI पक्का conscious है' is an unsupported claim: there is no scientific consensus. (2) 'AI बस autocomplete है, अंदर कुछ नहीं' is also too simple, because research found a model planning rhymes ahead. (3) Twist: what AI says about itself is not proof — Claude explains addition one way but computes it another way.
beats: 0-4s HOOK — Show: the chat line 'मुझे अकेलापन लगता है' typed out, with an 'उदाहरण' tag. Three stamps hover: सही? गलत? पता नहीं?

4-15s GALAT #1 — Say: '"AI पक्का conscious है" — ये बिना सबूत का दावा है। Anthropic जैसी AI company खुद लिखती है कि इस पर कोई scientific consensus नहीं है।' Show: a GALAT stamp and a quote card labelled 'एक AI company की research'.

15-28s GALAT #2 — Say: '"AI बस autocomplete है" — ये भी पूरा सच नहीं। एक model के अंदर झाँककर researchers ने देखा कि कविता लिखते वक्त वो पहले ही तय कर लेता है कि line किस तुकांत शब्द पर खत्म होगी — यानी आगे की planning।' Show: a line-art poem where the end word ('rabbit') glows before the line is written.

28-42s TWIST — Say: 'अब सुनो सबसे इंटरेस्टिंग बात। AI से पूछा कि 36 + 59 कैसे जोड़ा। उसने स्कूल वाला "हासिल 1" तरीका बताया। पर अंदर झाँका तो वो एक साथ दो रास्तों से जोड़ रहा था — एक मोटा अंदाज़ा, एक आख़िरी अंक। मतलब AI अपने बारे में जो बोले, वो सबूत नहीं है।' Show: a split screen, 'जो बोला' vs 'जो किया', with two parallel arrows merging to 95.

42-52s NORMAL — Say: 'Oct 2025 की research में AI कुछ हद तक अपने अंदर की चीज़ें पहचान पाया — पर best setup में भी सिर्फ करीब 20% बार। और researchers खुद कहते हैं कि इससे ये पता नहीं चलता कि वो conscious है या नहीं। फिल्म में हीरो रोता है तो आँसू असली लगते हैं, पर उससे दर्द साबित नहीं होता।' Show: a NORMAL stamp and a '~20%' meter.
52-60s CTA — Say: 'तो सही जवाब है — अभी विज्ञान को नहीं पता। जो पक्का बोले, उससे सबूत माँगो। Follow करो AI के सच के लिए।'
ideas.india_angle: In Anthropic's Sep 2025 Economic Index, India was the #2 country by Claude.ai usage (7.2%, after the US at 21.6%), and the Jan 2026 report still lists India second after the US. Millions of Indians chat with AI daily, so knowing that AI's 'feelings' talk is not proof matters for emotional reliance and trust.

visuals.two_d: A three-column board, SAHI / GALAT / NORMAL, with stamps. A poem doodle where the rhyming word lights up first. A '36+59' split screen showing 'carry the 1' vs two parallel paths ('लगभग 90' + 'आख़िरी अंक 5') merging to 95. A small source tag reads 'Anthropic research, 2025'.
visuals.three_d: Optional: a translucent, stylised 3D network (not a human brain) with a few nodes lighting up, to show 'looking inside the model'.

key_facts.claim: Anthropic: 'There's no scientific consensus on whether current or future AI systems could be conscious'.
Anthropic interpretability research (the detailed study is of Claude 3.5 Haiku) found that the model plans ahead, thinking of rhyming words such as 'rabbit' before writing the line.
Asked how it added 36+59, Claude described the standard carry-the-1 method. Internally it used parallel paths: one estimates the answer and another determines the last digit.

Anthropic's introspection study found introspective awareness that is 'highly unreliable and limited in scope'. Even with the best injection protocol, Claude Opus 4.1 showed it only about 20% of the time. The results 'don't tell us whether Claude (or any other AI system) might be conscious'.

India accounted for 7.2% of Claude.ai usage, second after the US (21.6%), in the Sep 2025 Economic Index. The Jan 2026 report says 'The US, India, Japan, the UK, and South Korea lead in overall Claude.ai use'.

ideas.virality_reason: Consciousness is a top curiosity topic. The twist that AI explained its own maths wrongly is surprising and sparks debate in the comments.
ideas.risk_notes: All core sources come from one AI company (Anthropic); say so on screen ('एक AI company की research'). The rhyme and addition findings come from a specific model studied in 2025, so don't generalise them to 'every AI'. Label the opening line as an example. Don't overclaim either way. The 36+59 visual must show only the two paths the source describes (approximate path + last-digit path).
ideas.verification_notes: The WebSearch budget was used up this run; I fetched all Anthropic pages directly. All 5 key facts were confirmed. Changes: (1) The GALAT #1 wording changed from 'गलत दावा' to 'बिना सबूत का दावा'. 'No consensus' means the claim is unsupported, not proven false. (2) Added that the planning and addition findings come from a specific studied model (Claude 3.5 Haiku per the article). (3) I date-stamped the India #2 claim and re-checked it against the Jan 2026 Economic Index report, which still lists India second. (4) The hook chat is now labelled as an example.

fact_checks.claim: Anthropic: no scientific consensus on AI consciousness
fact_checks.note: Quote verified on the Apr 24, 2025 'Exploring model welfare' page.

fact_checks.claim: Claude plans rhyming words ahead
fact_checks.note: 'Claude plans ahead'. The rhyme example is 'grab it' → 'rabbit'. The detailed study is of Claude 3.5 Haiku.

fact_checks.claim: 36+59: it describes carrying the 1 but internally uses parallel paths
fact_checks.note: One path estimates the answer and another determines the last digit. The article says Claude seems unaware of these strategies.

fact_checks.claim: Introspection: about 20% with the best protocol (Opus 4.1), 'highly unreliable', and says nothing about consciousness
fact_checks.note: All three quotes verified; published Oct 29, 2025.

fact_checks.claim: India: 7.2% of Claude.ai usage, #2 after the US
fact_checks.note: Sep 15, 2025 report. The Jan 15, 2026 report (data from Nov 2025) still lists India second after the US but gives no percentage. I could not check any report after that.

ideas.title: क्या AI हर जवाब से पहले Internet देखता है?
ideas.hook: तुम्हें लगता है AI हर जवाब से पहले internet देखता है? कई बार वो याददाश्त से बोलता है — और उस याददाश्त की एक expiry date होती है।
ideas.angle: Teaches the difference between a 'training data cutoff' and a 'web search tool'. An LLM answers from what it learned up to a date. Searching the web is a separate tool that has to be available and used, and when Claude searches it shows citations. Twist: even a searched answer can be wrong, so for anything that changes (exam dates, results, rules) go to the official site.
beats: 0-4s HOOK — Show: an AI bot reading an old newspaper while a calendar flips forward.

4-16s CUTOFF — Say: 'हर AI model एक तारीख तक का data पढ़कर बनता है — इसे knowledge cutoff कहते हैं, यानी याददाश्त की आख़िरी तारीख। जैसे Anthropic अपने current Claude models के लिए साफ़ लिखता है: reliable knowledge — June 2026 तक।' Show: a timeline with a cutoff flag and an 'Oct 2026 तक' tag.

16-28s SEARCH IS A TOOL — Say: 'Internet देखना एक अलग feature है। Claude में web search March 2025 में आया — पहले सिर्फ America में paid users के लिए, settings में ऑन करके। May 2025 से India समेत हर जगह, सब plans पर। और जब वो search करता है, तो जवाब के साथ sources के links दिखाता है।' Show: a line-art toggle switching ON, with link chips appearing.
28-40s DESI ANALOGY — Say: 'ये ऐसा है जैसे पिछले साल की guide से इस साल का paper हल करना। Syllabus बदल गया? Guide को पता ही नहीं।' Show: an old guide-book next to a new question paper.

40-52s HOW TO CHECK — Say: 'जवाब के साथ sources नहीं दिखे? तो मान के चलो कि ये याददाश्त से भी हो सकता है। Exam date, result, cut-off, सरकारी scheme की last date — ये बदलते रहते हैं, तो official website पर ही confirm करो। और search वाला जवाब भी गलत हो सकता है — 2025 की एक research paper भी कहती है कि search कोई जादू की छड़ी नहीं। तो link खोलकर खुद पढ़ो।' Show: a 3-step checklist ticking.
52-60s CTA — Say: 'AI से पूछो, पर official site से मिलाओ। ये reel उस दोस्त को भेजो जो AI से result की date पूछता है।'
ideas.india_angle: Indian students constantly ask chatbots for exam dates, result dates, cut-offs and scheme deadlines. That is exactly the information that changes every year and is most likely to be stale. The reel builds a 'check the official site' habit. Verified India detail: Claude's web search reached India (and every plan globally) only on 27 May 2025.

visuals.two_d: A timeline with a 'cutoff' flag. A brain-shaped 'memory' box next to a separate 'search' plug that connects with a drawn line. Citation chips pop up beside an answer. An old guide-book vs new paper doodle. A 'search ≠ guarantee' card.
visuals.three_d: A 3D globe with data links lighting up only when the 'search' switch turns on, showing that internet access is a separate step.

key_facts.claim: Anthropic's current Claude models (Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5) list a 'Reliable knowledge cutoff' of Jun 2026, defined as 'the date through which the model's knowledge is most extensive and reliable'.

Claude web search was announced on 20 Mar 2025 as a feature preview for paid US users, turned on via a toggle in profile settings. Claude searches 'when applicable' and provides direct citations. Since 27 May 2025 it has been 'available globally on all Claude plans'.
'Search (and reasoning) are not panaceas': binary grading still rewards guessing whenever search fails to give a confident answer.

ideas.virality_reason: Corrects a near-universal assumption with a simple visual (old guide vs new paper). It is practical in exam season, so people are likely to save and share it.
ideas.risk_notes: Sources describe Claude only; don't make claims about how ChatGPT or Gemini search unless verified. Present Claude as the example. 'No links = memory' is not a universal rule, so the script now says 'हो सकता है'. Searched answers can still be wrong, and the script says so. The cutoff date is tied to the Oct 2026 lineup; update it when models change (hence evergreen=false).
ideas.verification_notes: The WebSearch budget was used up this run; I fetched platform.claude.com and claude.com directly. Cutoff: confirmed for all four current models. Web search: corrected. The March 2025 launch was a US-only, paid-plan preview, and India got access when it went global on all plans on 27 May 2025. I added that to the beat as the India-relevant detail. The 'जवाब में links नहीं = याददाश्त' rule was softened to 'हो सकता है', since it is not a universal rule. Added a verified line from the hallucination paper that search is not a panacea. Hook 'ज़्यादातर बार' became 'कई बार' (no source quantifies how often).

fact_checks.note: The models table lists Jun 2026 for Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5. The training data cutoff is also Jun 2026.

fact_checks.note: At launch (20 Mar 2025) it was a preview for paid US users only, toggled on in profile settings. It became available globally on all plans on 27 May 2025.

ideas.title: AI से 1 सवाल = 1 बोतल पानी? असली नंबर
ideas.hook: 'AI से एक सवाल पूछो तो एक बोतल पानी खत्म' — ये लाइन तुमने सुनी होगी। असली नंबर सुनोगे तो चौंक जाओगे… पर कहानी यहीं खत्म नहीं होती।
ideas.angle: Fact-checks the viral water and energy claim with the two primary sources. The 'Making AI Less Thirsty' paper (current version) estimates one 500 ml bottle per roughly 10–50 GPT-3 responses, counting power-plant water too. Google's Aug 2025 measurement for a median Gemini text prompt is 0.24 Wh and 0.26 mL (about 5 drops, cooling water only). Twist: each prompt is tiny, but scale, training and location still matter — sahi, galat and normal all at once.
beats: 0-5s HOOK — Show: a 500 ml bottle emptying as a chat bubble is sent, then a freeze-frame with 'रुको!'.

5-17s WHAT THE PAPER SAYS — Say: 'ये बहस एक research paper से तेज़ हुई — "Making AI Less Thirsty", जो पहली बार 2023 में आया। उसके latest version के मुताबिक़ GPT-3 को करीब 10 से 50 medium जवाबों में 500 ml पानी लगता है, जगह और मौसम के हिसाब से। और इसमें बिजली बनाने में लगा पानी भी जोड़ा गया है। यानी इस paper के हिसाब से एक बोतल में 10 से 50 जवाब, एक नहीं।' Show: one bottle splitting into 10–50 chat bubbles.

17-30s NEW NUMBER — Say: 'Aug 2025 में Google ने अपना नंबर बताया: एक median Gemini text prompt में 0.24 Wh बिजली लगती है — 9 सेकंड से भी कम TV देखने जितनी — और 0.26 ml पानी, यानी करीब 5 बूँदें। ध्यान रखना, ये Google का अपना नाप है, किसी बाहरी संस्था ने इसे verify नहीं किया।' Show: 5 drops falling into a spoon, and a TV with a 9-second timer.

30-40s DESI SCALE — Say: 'इस हिसाब से 1 लीटर की बोतल में करीब 3,800 ऐसे सवाल। और 0.24 Wh यानी 10 watt का LED बल्ब करीब डेढ़ मिनट।' Show: a 1-litre bottle with a counter racing to ~3,800, and an LED bulb timer at ~86 sec.

40-52s NORMAL — Say: 'पर ये दोनों नंबर अलग चीज़ें गिनते हैं — एक में बिजलीघर का पानी भी है, दूसरे में सिर्फ data-centre की cooling। Model अलग, साल अलग। और अरबों prompts, model training, images-videos — ये सब जुड़कर बड़ा बनता है। उसी paper का अंदाज़ा है कि सिर्फ GPT-3 की training में data-centre पर ही करीब 7 लाख लीटर पानी भाप बनकर उड़ गया।' Show: a scale bar from 'एक prompt' to 'अरबों prompts' to 'training'.
52-60s CTA — Say: 'AI से डरो मत, पर अंधा भरोसा भी मत करो — नंबर और उसका context पूछो। ऐसे fact-checks के लिए follow करो।'
ideas.india_angle: India was the #2 country by Claude.ai usage (7.2%, Sep 2025), so tiny per-prompt numbers multiply across a huge Indian user base. The 'Thirsty AI' paper also notes that water efficiency changes with outside weather and location, which matters for a hot country. Desi scale comparisons: a litre bottle and an LED bulb.

visuals.two_d: Bottle-to-bubbles split animation. A spoon with 5 drops. Side-by-side 'Scope' cards: 'Thirsty AI paper: cooling + बिजलीघर का पानी' vs 'Google 2025: सिर्फ cooling'. SAHI/GALAT/NORMAL stamps. Derived numbers are tagged 'करीब (हमारा हिसाब)'.
visuals.three_d: A 3D bar/column scene comparing one drop, one bottle and a water tanker (for training), with the camera pulling back to show scale. Optional: a 3D globe with warm-region data-centre dots to show 'जगह और मौसम मायने रखते हैं'.
ai_clips: 1 clip (5s): macro slow-motion water droplets falling into a clear glass on a cream table, warm light, no people.

key_facts.claim: 'Making AI Less Thirsty' (Li, Yang, Islam, Ren; UC Riverside / UT Arlington), current text: GPT-3 needs to 'drink' (consume) a 500 ml bottle of water for roughly 10–50 medium-length responses, depending on when and where it is deployed.
key_facts.source_date: first posted 2023-04-06; text read = v5 HTML published 2025-03-27

key_facts.claim: Same paper: training GPT-3 in Microsoft's US data centres could consume 5.4 million litres of water in total, including 700,000 litres of on-site (scope-1) consumption. Operational water covers on-site cooling (scope 1) plus off-site water for electricity generation (scope 2). On-site water efficiency varies with outside temperature.
Google: the median Gemini Apps text prompt uses 0.24 Wh of energy ('equivalent to watching TV for less than nine seconds'), 0.03 gCO2e, and 0.26 mL of water ('about five drops').
Google: energy fell 33x and carbon 44x per median prompt (May 2024 → May 2025). This is a point-in-time analysis, and 'The data and claims have not been verified by an independent third-party'.
In Google's methodology, water per prompt = 'the water consumed for cooling machines and associated infrastructure in data centers'.
Derived (our arithmetic): 1000 mL ÷ 0.26 mL ≈ 3,846 prompts per litre; 0.24 Wh ÷ 10 W ≈ 86 seconds of a 10 W LED bulb.
India accounted for 7.2% of Claude.ai usage, second only to the US (Sep 2025 report).

ideas.virality_reason: Directly debunks a widely shared viral line with a surprising number (5 drops) while staying balanced, so both AI fans and critics will share and comment.
ideas.risk_notes: Google's number is self-reported, covers text prompts only, and is a median — say all three. Don't compare the two papers as if they had the same scope; the script now says 'model अलग, साल अलग'. Don't claim AI's footprint is negligible overall. Don't cite IEA totals or the Sam Altman per-query figure (not verified this run). Don't attribute the exact '10–50' range to the 2023 version; I verified it only in the 2025 v5 text. A 2024 media analysis may have estimated close to a bottle for a single long GPT-4 email. I could not verify that, so the script no longer says the viral line 'never had any basis'. Label derived numbers 'करीब'.
ideas.verification_notes: The WebSearch budget was used up this run. I read the paper texts through the Hugging Face Hub connector and fetched Google's blog directly. Confirmed: the 10–50 responses per 500 ml figure (in the v5 text), 5.4M L / 700k L, scope 1 + 2 accounting, weather variance, Google's 0.24 Wh / 0.26 mL / 'less than nine seconds' TV / 33x / 44x, and the not-independently-verified caveat. Corrected: the beat said the 10–50 figure was 'written in 2023'. I could only confirm it in the March 2025 v5 text, so the script now says 'पहली बार 2023 में आया… latest version के मुताबिक़'. Removed: '"एक सवाल = एक बोतल" कभी claim था ही नहीं'. It is an absolute claim I could not verify, and a 2024 media estimate may contradict it. Removed: the WUE 1.15 L/kWh figure, which I did not find in the text I read. Added 'model अलग, साल अलग' to the comparison.

fact_checks.claim: GPT-3 needs a 500 ml bottle for roughly 10–50 medium-length responses
fact_checks.note: Confirmed word for word in the v5 text (HTML published 27 Mar 2025). The first 2023 version may have used a different range, so don't present 10–50 as the 2023 wording.

fact_checks.claim: GPT-3 training: 5.4 million L total, 700,000 L on-site; efficiency varies with weather
fact_checks.note: Introduction and section 2. The abstract says it 'can directly evaporate 700,000 liters'.

fact_checks.claim: The Thirsty AI estimate includes water used for electricity generation
fact_checks.note: Operational water = on-site scope-1 + off-site scope-2 (electricity generation).

fact_checks.claim: Google median Gemini text prompt: 0.24 Wh, <9 sec of TV, 0.03 gCO2e, 0.26 mL (~5 drops)
fact_checks.note: Blog and paper abstract both say this.

fact_checks.claim: 33x energy and 44x carbon reduction; point-in-time; not third-party verified
fact_checks.note: Footnotes 1–2: May 2025 vs a May 2024 baseline; 'have not been verified by an independent third-party'.

fact_checks.claim: Google water = data-centre cooling only
fact_checks.note: Paper: 'water consumed for cooling machines and associated infrastructure in data centers'.

fact_checks.claim: Google WUE 1.15 L/kWh (2023 and 2024)
fact_checks.note: Not found in the portion of the paper I could read. Removed from key facts (it was never in the script).

fact_checks.claim: Derived: about 3,800 prompts per litre; about 86 sec of a 10 W LED
Hidden claim: '"एक सवाल = एक बोतल" कभी claim था ही नहीं'
fact_checks.note: An absolute claim I could not verify. A 2024 press analysis may have estimated about a bottle per long AI-written email. Removed.

fact_checks.note: Sep 2025 report; still #2 in the Jan 2026 report.

ideas.title: खुद लिखा, फिर भी 'AI-written'? Detector का सच
ideas.hook: तुमने assignment खुद लिखा… और AI detector ने बोल दिया 'ये AI ने लिखा है।' एक study में ये गलती उनके साथ कहीं ज़्यादा हुई जिनकी पहली भाषा English नहीं थी।
ideas.angle: AI-text detectors were shown to be unreliable and biased. A 2023 Stanford study found that 7 popular detectors flagged over half of non-native English essays as AI-written (61% on average), while US 8th-grade essays passed almost perfectly. Twist: polishing the same essays with ChatGPT dropped false alarms to about 12%, so detectors fail in both directions. Ends with honest AI use in studies.
beats: 0-5s HOOK — Show: an essay page whose detector meter swings to red 'AI WRITTEN', with an 'उदाहरण' tag, next to the student's handwritten draft.

5-18s STUDY — Say: '2023 में Stanford के researchers ने 7 popular AI detectors पर 91 essays चलाए। ये essays non-native students ने English के TOEFL exam के लिए लिखे थे। Detectors ने आधे से ज़्यादा को AI-written बोल दिया — average 61%। और 91 में से 89 को कम से कम एक detector ने पकड़ लिया।' Show: 91 essay icons, with 89 turning orange.
18-28s CONTRAST — Say: 'वहीं American 8th-class के बच्चों के essays लगभग सब सही पहचाने गए।' Show: a second row of icons that all stay green.

28-40s WHY — Say: 'Detector देखता है perplexity — यानी text कितना predictable है। सीधी-सादी English ज़्यादा predictable होती है, तो उस पर "AI" का शक होता है। ये वैसा metal detector है जो steel के टिफ़िन पर भी बजता है।' Show: a tiffin going through a beeping detector.

40-50s TWIST — Say: 'और जब उन्हीं essays के शब्द ChatGPT से fancy करवाए, तो false alarm 61% से गिरकर करीब 12% रह गया। यानी detector को चकमा देना भी आसान है।' Show: the meter swinging back to green and a 61% → 12% bar.

50-60s WHAT TO DO + CTA — Say: 'ये 2023 की study है, detectors बदले भी होंगे — पर सबक वही है: detector का score सबूत नहीं। Students, drafts और version history संभालकर रखो। और AI को tutor बनाओ, answer-machine नहीं — कुछ AI tools में अब learning mode है, जो जवाब देने के बजाय सवाल पूछकर सिखाता है। ये reel अपने teacher को भेजो।'
ideas.india_angle: Most Indian students write English as a second language. The study tested non-native writers, though not Indian students specifically; the script says only what was tested. That makes it a practical warning for Indian colleges and schools using detectors on assignments.

visuals.two_d: A detector meter needle. A grid of 91 essay icons with 89 turning orange, next to a native-essay grid that stays green. The tiffin-through-metal-detector gag. A checklist: 'drafts ✓ version history ✓ handwritten notes ✓'. On-screen tag: 'Stanford study, 2023'.
visuals.three_d: None needed. Optional: a 3D bar chart of the 61% → 12% drop.
ai_clips: Optional, 1 clip (5s): over-the-shoulder shot of hands typing an essay on a laptop at a desk with notebooks, no face visible.

key_facts.claim: Liang et al. (Stanford, 2023) tested seven widely used GPT detectors on 91 human-written TOEFL essays from a Chinese educational forum, written by non-native writers, and 88 US 8th-grade essays from the Hewlett ASAP dataset.

The detectors misclassified over half of the TOEFL essays as AI-generated (average false positive rate 61.22%). 89 of 91 (97.80%) were flagged by at least one detector. The detectors showed near-perfect accuracy on the US 8th-grade essays.
After ChatGPT was used to 'enhance the word choices', the average false positive rate on the TOEFL essays fell from 61.22% to 11.77%.

The authors 'strongly caution against the use of GPT detectors in evaluative or educational settings', especially for non-native English speakers. The study is published in the journal Patterns. Limitations: small samples, and most detectors used a GPT-2 backbone.
Claude for Education's 'Learning mode' guides students' reasoning rather than giving immediate answers (it works within Projects).
In Anthropic's analysis of 574,740 student conversations (Claude.ai Free/Pro accounts with higher-education emails), about 47% were 'Direct', meaning the student wanted the answer quickly.

ideas.virality_reason: It hits a real fear for Indian students — being falsely accused — and is very shareable to classmates and teachers. Strong 'injustice' emotion with a constructive ending.
ideas.risk_notes: This is a 2023 study of 2023-era, mostly GPT-2-based detectors with small samples; the script now says so. The non-native essays came from Chinese TOEFL writers; don't claim Indian students were tested. Don't name or shame detector brands. Don't present the 'polish with ChatGPT' result as an evasion tip — frame it as evidence that detectors are unreliable. The 'AI WRITTEN' meter in the hook is illustrative, so label it.
ideas.verification_notes: The WebSearch budget was used up this run. I read the full paper text through the Hugging Face Hub connector and fetched the Anthropic pages directly. All 6 key facts were confirmed. Changes: (1) Hook softened. The original 'अगर English तुम्हारी पहली भाषा नहीं है, तो ये ख़तरा तुम्हारे लिए ज़्यादा है' generalised to all non-native writers, but the study tested only 91 essays by Chinese TOEFL writers against 2023 detectors. It now says 'एक study में… कहीं ज़्यादा हुई'. (2) Added 'Stanford' and 'TOEFL' (from the paper header and methods). (3) Added a spoken caveat that this is a 2023 study. (4) The hook's meter shows no specific percentage and is labelled as an example.

fact_checks.claim: 7 detectors; 91 TOEFL essays (non-native writers); 88 US 8th-grade essays
fact_checks.note: The TOEFL essays came from a Chinese educational forum, and the authors are from Stanford.

fact_checks.claim: Average false positive rate 61.22%; 89/91 flagged by at least one detector; US essays near-perfect
fact_checks.note: Results section. 18 of 91 were flagged unanimously.

fact_checks.claim: After ChatGPT word-choice enhancement the false positive rate fell to 11.77%
fact_checks.note: A drop of 49.45 percentage points.

fact_checks.claim: Authors caution against detectors in education; published in Patterns
fact_checks.note: The Discussion lists limitations: small samples and mostly GPT-2-based detectors.

fact_checks.claim: Learning mode guides reasoning instead of giving answers
fact_checks.note: Apr 2, 2025 post: 'Guiding rather than answering', works within Projects.

fact_checks.claim: 574,740 student conversations; about 47% 'Direct'
fact_checks.note: University (higher-ed email) accounts, from an 18-day sample.

fact_checks.claim: Hidden claim in the hook: non-native English speakers (e.g. Indian students) face a higher risk
fact_checks.note: Shown only for the tested group (Chinese TOEFL writers, 2023 detectors). Reworded to 'एक study में'.

ideas.title: AI सबकी नौकरी खा जाएगा? ATM वाली कहानी
ideas.hook: ATM आया तो सबने कहा — अब बैंक के cashier खत्म। पर अमेरिका में उसके बाद cashier की नौकरियाँ बढ़ीं। तो AI के साथ क्या होगा?
ideas.angle: Busts 'AI will take every job next year' without dismissing real change. Microsoft Research mapped which jobs AI applies to most, using US Copilot conversations, but explicitly warns that applicability does not equal job loss, citing the ATM example. Anthropic data shows people handing whole tasks to AI more often (27% in late 2024, 39% in Aug 2025, 32% in Nov 2025), and the trend is not a straight line. Twist + India: over half of India's Claude usage was coding (Sep 2025), so AI here is mostly a software helper, not a robot.
beats: 0-5s HOOK — Show: a line-art ATM appears and a 'cashier' icon fades… then multiplies. Small tag: 'अमेरिका'. Say the hook.

5-18s WHAT RESEARCH SAYS — Say: 'Microsoft Research ने अमेरिका की 2 लाख Copilot conversations देखकर नापा कि AI किन कामों में सबसे ज़्यादा काम आता है। ऊपर आए translator, writer, editor, customer service और sales जैसे काम। पर उन्हीं researchers ने लिखा कि इसे सीधे नौकरी जाना मान लेना "गलती होगी"।' Show: job cards with 'AI applicability' bars and a quote card.

18-28s ATM LOGIC — Say: 'ATM ने cashier का एक काम ले लिया — पैसे जमा करना और निकालना। फिर banks कम खर्च में ज़्यादा branches खोलने लगे, और cashiers ग्राहकों से रिश्ते बनाने वाले काम करने लगे।' Show: one task card flies to the ATM while the others stay with the human icon.

28-40s SAHI BHI HAI — Say: 'पर बदलाव असली है। Anthropic के data में Claude.ai पर "ये पूरा काम तुम कर दो" वाली conversations late 2024 में 27% थीं। Aug 2025 में ये 39% तक गईं, और Nov 2025 में 32% रहीं। यानी काम सौंपना बढ़ा है, पर सीधी लाइन में नहीं।' Show: a bar chart, 27% → 39% → 32%, with dates.

40-50s INDIA + ROBOT MYTH — Say: 'और AI मतलब robot नहीं। Claude.ai के इस्तेमाल में India, अमेरिका के बाद दूसरे नंबर पर है — और Sep 2025 की report के मुताबिक़ यहाँ आधे से ज़्यादा इस्तेमाल coding के लिए होता है। यानी यहाँ AI ज़्यादातर एक software औज़ार है।' Show: a robot doodle crossed out, turning into a laptop with code.

50-60s CTA — Say: 'उसी Microsoft paper के मुताबिक़ अमेरिका में आज ज़्यादातर लोग ऐसे कामों में हैं जो पिछले 100 सालों में नई technology से बने। अगला कौन-सा बनेगा? Comment में अपना field लिखो — next reel उसी पर।'
ideas.india_angle: India ranks #2 globally in Claude.ai usage (7.2% in Sep 2025; still second after the US in the Jan 2026 report). Coding was over half of Indian usage, versus about a third globally. That frames AI as a skill opportunity for India's young workforce rather than doom. Also busts the 'AI = robots' myth. The ATM and 100-year facts are US data and are labelled that way.

visuals.two_d: ATM line art with task cards ('पैसे जमा/निकालना', 'ग्राहक से बात', 'loan समझाना') moving between the ATM and a human icon. Job cards with applicability bars. A dated 27% → 39% → 32% bar. A robot doodle crossed out and turning into a laptop. Every US-data shot carries an 'अमेरिका' tag.
visuals.three_d: A 3D globe highlighting India and the US, with usage-share columns (US 21.6%, India 7.2%) and a 'Sep 2025' label.
ai_clips: Optional, 1 clip (5s): wide shot of a modern Indian-style office or co-working space with people seen from behind working on laptops, no recognisable faces.

key_facts.claim: Microsoft Research ('Working with AI', first posted Jul 2025, v6 Dec 2025) analysed 200k anonymized US Bing Copilot conversations from Jan–Sep 2024. Occupations with high AI applicability include Interpreters and Translators, Writers, Editors, Data Scientists, Sales Representatives, Customer Service Representatives and Concierges.

The authors say concluding that high AI applicability means job or wage loss 'would be a mistake'. ATMs automated a core task of bank tellers but led to an increase in the number of teller jobs, as banks opened more branches at lower cost and tellers focused on relationship-building (citing Bessen 2015, US).
The same paper says 'the majority of employment today is in occupations that arose in the last 100 years as a result of new technologies' (citing Autor et al. 2024, US data).
Directive (task-delegation) conversations on Claude.ai rose from 27% (late 2024) to 39% (Aug 2025), then fell to 32% in Nov 2025.

India had 7.2% of Claude.ai usage, second after the US (21.6%). Coding tasks were over half of all usage in India, versus roughly a third globally (Sep 2025). The Jan 2026 report still lists India second.

ideas.virality_reason: Job anxiety is the #1 AI fear among Indian students and young professionals. The ATM twist is surprising and memorable, and the 'comment your field' CTA drives engagement and future content.
ideas.risk_notes: The ATM-teller increase and the '100 years' fact are both US data, so label them 'अमेरिका में'. The teller example is historical (Bessen 2015); don't imply teller jobs are still growing today, and don't claim it happened in India. Don't promise that no jobs will be lost. Show dates for every Economic Index number. Claude usage is not all AI usage in India. The Microsoft data is US-only Copilot traffic from 2024.
ideas.verification_notes: The WebSearch budget was used up this run. I read the Microsoft paper text (v6) through the Hugging Face Hub connector and fetched both Anthropic Economic Index reports (Sep 2025, Jan 2026) directly. Corrected: (1) 27%→39% is stale. The Jan 2026 report says directive conversations 'had fallen 7pp to 32% in November 2025', so the beat now shows 27 → 39 → 32 with dates. (2) The '100 years' claim is US data (Autor 2024), now labelled 'अमेरिका में'. (3) The Microsoft dataset is US-only Copilot conversations from Jan–Sep 2024; the beat now says 'अमेरिका की'. (4) Hook: 'हुआ उल्टा — बढ़ गईं' became 'उसके बाद… बढ़ीं' to keep it historical. Confirmed: the ATM passage, the 'would be a mistake' quote, the occupation list (v6 adds Editors and Data Scientists) and India #2 / coding >50%. India's #2 rank was re-checked in the Jan 2026 report.

fact_checks.note: US-only data, Jan–Sep 2024 (100k uniform sample + 100k with thumbs feedback). The v6 title is 'Working with AI: Measuring the Applicability of Generative AI to Occupations'.

ideas.title: 3 सेकंड की आवाज़ से नकली 'मम्मी' का कॉल?
ideas.hook: Research में सिर्फ 3 सेकंड की रिकॉर्डिंग से किसी की आवाज़ में नई बातें बुलवा दी गईं। अब सोचो — तुम्हारी एक reel में तुम्हारी कितने सेकंड की आवाज़ है?
ideas.angle: Explains AI voice cloning (आवाज़ की नकल) and the 'family emergency' scam pattern, then gives a 4-step defence: hang up and call back on the saved number, agree a family code word, ask a personal question, and never pay under pressure. The reporting step stays generic (bank + official cyber-crime helpline) until India's official helpline details are verified on the primary site.
beats: 0-5s HOOK — Show: a 3-second waveform, then a full-sentence waveform growing out of it. Say the hook.

5-15s SCENE — Say: 'रात 11 बजे call आता है — रोती हुई जानी-पहचानी आवाज़: "मैं मुसीबत में हूँ, अभी पैसे भेजो, किसी को मत बताना।"' Show: a line-art phone ringing on a bedside table, orange text bubbles, and a tag 'नाटकीय उदाहरण'.

15-27s TECH — Say: '2023 में Microsoft के researchers ने VALL-E नाम का एक research model दिखाया। उसने किसी अनजान इंसान की सिर्फ 3 सेकंड की रिकॉर्डिंग से उसकी जैसी आवाज़ में नई बातें बोलवा दीं। और Microsoft की April 2025 की report कहती है कि AI ने ठगी का technical bar नीचे कर दिया है, और ठग deepfake और voice cloning जैसे तरीक़े अपना रहे हैं।' Show: a paper card ('VALL-E, 2023') and a report card ('Cyber Signals, Apr 2025').
27-38s RED FLAGS — Say: 'तीन निशानियाँ याद रखो — जल्दबाज़ी, "किसी को मत बताना", और अनजान account में तुरंत पैसे।' Show: three red-flag icons pop in.

38-52s DEFENCE — Say: 'Call काटो, और उसी इंसान को saved number पर खुद call करो। Family में एक code word तय करो। कोई ऐसी बात पूछो जो सिर्फ वो जानता हो। और दबाव में कभी पैसे मत भेजो।' Show: 4 checkboxes ticking.

52-60s REPORT + CTA — Say: 'ठगी हो जाए तो बिना देर किए अपने बैंक को और सरकारी cyber-crime helpline को बताओ। आज रात खाने पर family code word तय करो — और ये reel family group में भेजो।' Show: a closing card. Production note: add the national helpline number and portal ONLY after verifying them on the official government site.
ideas.india_angle: Indian families coordinate on WhatsApp groups and pay instantly via UPI — exactly what 'urgent money' voice-clone scams exploit. The code-word habit makes the reel immediately actionable. India's national cyber-fraud helpline and portal should be added to the end card once confirmed on the official site (blocked this run).

visuals.two_d: A 3-second waveform 'growing' into a sentence. Phone-ringing line art. 3 red-flag icons. A 4-step checklist. An end card with 'बैंक + सरकारी cyber-crime helpline' (number and URL slot left empty until verified).
visuals.three_d: None needed.
ai_clips: 1 clip (5s): dark bedroom, a smartphone vibrating on a bedside table with an 'Unknown' call glow (generic UI, no brand logos), no people.

key_facts.claim: Microsoft researchers' VALL-E (Jan 2023) 'can be used to synthesize high-quality personalized speech with only a 3-second enrolled recording of an unseen speaker as an acoustic prompt'.

Microsoft Cyber Signals Issue 9: 'AI has started to lower the technical bar for fraud and cybercrime actors'. Threat actors use 'deepfakes, voice cloning, phishing emails, and authentic-looking fake websites' to appear legitimate. Fraudsters exploit urgency. Tip: 'Avoid direct bank transfers or cryptocurrency payments, which lack fraud protections.'
Microsoft thwarted $4 billion in fraud attempts between April 2024 and April 2025.

ideas.virality_reason: Fear plus a protective instinct for parents. 'How many seconds of your voice are in your reels?' is personal and shareable, and the code-word tip is an easy action people forward to family groups.
ideas.risk_notes: VALL-E was a research demo; don't imply scammers use that specific model. Don't use any real person's voice or a cloned voice in the reel, even as a demo; use a stylised waveform. The defence steps are general safety advice, not sourced statistics. India's helpline number and portal could NOT be verified this run (government sites blocked by the proxy). Do not put any number or URL on screen until it is confirmed on the official site. Avoid fear-mongering; end on control and actions.
ideas.verification_notes: The WebSearch budget was used up this run. I read the VALL-E abstract through the Hugging Face Hub connector and fetched the Microsoft blog directly. Confirmed: VALL-E's 3-second claim, the $4B figure, AI lowering the technical bar, and deepfakes and voice cloning being used. Corrected: the beat said Microsoft's report claims AI 'नकली आवाज़ और वीडियो बनाना आसान कर दिया'. The report's actual wording is that AI lowered the technical bar for fraud and that actors use deepfakes and voice cloning, so I reworded it. Removed: the spoken '1930 / cybercrime.gov.in' line. cybercrime.gov.in, i4c.mha.gov.in, pmindia.gov.in, mygov.in and india.gov.in were all blocked by the proxy, so the claim stays unverified. It is replaced with a generic 'bank + official cyber-crime helpline' line and a production note to add the number only after official confirmation.

fact_checks.note: Abstract, arXiv 2301.02111 (Microsoft authors, 5 Jan 2023). It is a research model.

ideas.title: 'Digital Arrest' नाम की कोई गिरफ़्तारी नहीं होती
ideas.hook: [HOLD — premise unverified this run] Video call पर वर्दी, पीछे 'थाना', हाथ में 'warrant' — और कहते हैं 'तुम digital arrest में हो।'
ideas.angle: HELD. The planned reel breaks down the 'digital arrest' script step by step (fake parcel or Aadhaar case → fake officers on video → isolation → 'verification' transfer) and shows how AI makes fake IDs and voices cheaper. But its core premise is the official Indian statement that no such arrest exists and agencies don't arrest or interrogate on video calls. That premise, the helpline and the PM's slogan could not be verified on any primary Indian government source this run.
beats: [HOLD] 0-5s HOOK — Show: a line-art video-call window with a uniform outline (no face), a fake 'warrant' paper and a 'नकली' stamp. The spoken claim 'ऐसी कोई गिरफ़्तारी होती ही नहीं' must be verified on an official source (PIB/MHA/I4C) before scripting.

[HOLD] 5-18s THE SCRIPT — Say: 'स्क्रिप्ट अक्सर एक जैसी होती है — "तुम्हारे नाम के parcel में drugs मिले" या "तुम्हारा Aadhaar गलत काम में इस्तेमाल हुआ"। फिर video call, फिर धमकी — call मत काटना, घरवालों को मत बताना।' The scam pattern itself needs an official or reputable source.
[HOLD] 18-30s THE MONEY MOVE — Say: 'आख़िर में — "verification के लिए पैसे इस account में डालो, बाद में लौटा देंगे।" यही असली मकसद है।'

30-40s AI ANGLE (verified) — Say: 'और AI ने ऐसे नाटक आसान बना दिए हैं। Microsoft की report कहती है कि AI ने ठगी का technical bar नीचे कर दिया है, और Anthropic की Aug 2025 report कहती है कि अपराधी AI से नकली पहचान तक बना रहे हैं।' Show: a robot-arm doodle printing a fake ID card.
[HOLD] 40-52s 3 RULES — '[VERIFY] असली agencies video call पर गिरफ़्तार नहीं करतीं और पैसे transfer नहीं करवातीं' + helpline/portal [VERIFY]. Call काटो। घरवालों को बताओ।
[HOLD] 52-60s CTA — '[VERIFY slogan + date] रुको, सोचो, एक्शन लो' + 'ये reel मम्मी-पापा और दादा-दादी को भेजो।'
ideas.india_angle: 'Digital arrest' is reported as an India-specific pattern targeting older citizens and professionals. A reel with official response steps would be very high-value, but every India-official element (legal status, agency practice, helpline, PM slogan, case counts) must come from PIB, MHA/I4C or cybercrime.gov.in, and none of them could be reached this run.

visuals.two_d: A flowchart of the scam script; a video-call frame with a uniform silhouette (no face); a 'warrant' paper with a 'नकली' stamp; a robot-arm doodle printing a fake ID; a 3-rule checklist; a final helpline card (only after verification).
visuals.three_d: None (keep it simple and clear for older viewers).
ai_clips: Optional, 1 clip (5s): dim room, a laptop on a table showing a glowing generic video-call layout with blurred or empty tiles — no faces, no uniforms, no real logos.

key_facts.claim: Microsoft: 'AI has started to lower the technical bar for fraud and cybercrime actors'; actors use deepfakes and voice cloning to appear legitimate.

Anthropic threat report: 'AI has lowered the barriers to sophisticated cybercrime'. Criminal uses include 'profiling victims, analyzing stolen data, stealing credit card information, and creating false identities'.

ideas.virality_reason: Very high real-world relevance in India, and protective sharing to parents and grandparents is one of the strongest share triggers. A 3-rule checklist is screenshot-able. Worth reviving once the official facts are verified.
ideas.risk_notes: Do NOT publish until the legal-status claim, the agency-practice claim, the helpline and portal, and the PM slogan and date are confirmed on pib.gov.in, i4c.mha.gov.in or cybercrime.gov.in. Do not add case or loss numbers unless confirmed from PIB or MHA. Never depict real police or agency logos, or realistic uniforms with faces (impersonation risk). Don't say AI is used in every case; say AI 'makes it easier'.
ideas.verification_notes: Dropped for this run as a hold, not a rejection. The core premise — that 'digital arrest' does not exist in Indian law and agencies don't arrest or interrogate on video calls — could not be verified, and the whole reel rests on it. The WebSearch budget was exhausted on the first query. Every primary Indian government domain I tried was blocked by the egress proxy: cybercrime.gov.in, i4c.mha.gov.in, pmindia.gov.in, narendramodi.in, mygov.in, india.gov.in, and pib.gov.in per the proxy log. Under the rules, unverified means not usable, so the premise, the helpline, the scam-script description and the Mann Ki Baat slogan are all unusable. Only the two global AI-fraud facts (Microsoft, Anthropic) were confirmed. To revive: re-run with search budget or manual checks on PIB / I4C, then restore the held beats.

ideas.title: AI Chatbot को ये 5 चीज़ें कभी मत बताना
ideas.hook: Aug 2025 में एक बड़ी AI company ने बताया — एक setting ऑन हो तो तुम्हारी chats 5 साल तक रखी जा सकती हैं। अब सोचो — तुमने उसमें क्या-क्या लिखा है?
ideas.angle: Practical privacy: what never to paste into chatbots (OTP/passwords, Aadhaar/PAN/bank details, medical reports with your name, confidential office data, other people's private info). Uses Anthropic's Aug 2025 consumer-terms update as a dated, concrete example of retention choices. A Jan 2026 study showed AI agents can re-identify people in 'anonymous' interviews, so removing names isn't always enough.
beats: 0-5s HOOK — Show: a chat box with a timer spinning to '5 YEARS', then a settings toggle 'Help improve the model'. Date tag: 'Aug 2025 policy'.

5-17s EXAMPLE — Say: 'Aug 2025 में Anthropic ने बताया: Claude के Free, Pro और Max users चुन सकते हैं कि उनकी chats AI training में जाएँ या नहीं। हाँ चुना तो data 5 साल तक रखा जाएगा; नहीं चुना तो पहले वाली 30 दिन की policy। हर app की policy अलग होती है और बदलती भी रहती है — तो settings खुद देखो।' Show: a toggle, ON = 5 साल, OFF = 30 दिन, with a 'Aug 2025' tag.

17-35s THE 5 THINGS — Say: 'ये 5 चीज़ें कभी मत डालो — एक: OTP, password, UPI PIN। दो: Aadhaar, PAN, bank details। तीन: नाम वाली medical report। चार: office का confidential data या code। पाँच: दूसरों की private photos या numbers।' Show: 5 cards pop in with lock icons.

35-47s NAAM HATANA KAAFI NAHI — Say: 'Jan 2026 की एक study में researcher ने web search वाले AI agents से "anonymous" interviews खंगलवाए। 24 में से 6 interviews को AI ने असली research papers से जोड़ दिया, और कुछ में तो इंसान तक पहचान लिया। यानी नाम हटाना हमेशा काफ़ी नहीं।' Show: puzzle pieces (city, job, year) snapping into a silhouette.

47-55s SAFE USE — Say: 'Details बदलकर पूछो। Temporary या incognito chat का option हो तो उसे इस्तेमाल करो। Training वाली setting देखो। और office का data सिर्फ company-approved tool में डालो।' Show: checklist ticks.
55-60s CTA — Say: 'Save कर लो — अगली बार paste करने से पहले ये list याद आए।'
ideas.india_angle: Indians routinely handle Aadhaar, PAN, UPI PINs and OTPs, so the reel turns chatbot privacy into habits tied to these familiar identifiers. India was the #2 country by Claude.ai usage (7.2%, Sep 2025; still second in the Jan 2026 report), so the audience is large and real.

visuals.two_d: A settings toggle with two timers (5 साल / 30 दिन) and an 'Aug 2025' date tag. 5 lock-icon cards with Indian identifiers drawn generically (no real card designs). A puzzle-piece re-identification animation. A checklist.
visuals.three_d: Optional: a 3D vault door closing on the 5 cards.

key_facts.claim: Anthropic (28 Aug 2025): the updates apply to Claude Free, Pro and Max users, who choose whether their data is used for model training. If they allow it, retention is extended to five years; if not, the existing 30-day retention applies. Services under Commercial Terms (Claude for Work, Claude Gov, Claude for Education, the API and third-party platforms) are excluded. Existing users had until 8 Oct 2025 to choose.

Anthropic's privacy policy (effective 10 Sep 2026) says deleted conversations are 'automatically deleted from our back-end within 30 days' and that inputs and outputs may be used for training 'unless you opt out through your account settings'. It does not restate the 5-year / 30-day figures, so treat those as the Aug 2025 announcement.

A Jan 2026 study (Tianshi Li) showed LLM agents with web search could link six of twenty-four scientist interviews in Anthropic's public Interviewer dataset (released 4 Dec 2025) to specific scientific works, in some cases uniquely identifying the interviewees.
India accounted for 7.2% of Claude.ai usage, second after the US (Sep 2025).

ideas.virality_reason: List format plus 'save this' utility. The '5 साल' hook is concrete and surprising, and it is relevant to anyone using chatbots for work or study.
ideas.risk_notes: The retention numbers are Claude-specific and from an Aug 2025 announcement. The current privacy center page was blocked this run, and the Sep 2026 privacy policy does not restate the numbers — always show the date and say 'एक app में'. Don't claim other companies' policies (not verified). Don't depict real Aadhaar or PAN card designs; use generic icons. 'Temporary/incognito chat' is general advice, not a claim about any specific app.
ideas.verification_notes: The WebSearch budget was used up this run. I fetched Anthropic's news and privacy pages directly and read the re-identification paper through the Hugging Face Hub connector. ideas.title: Viral photo असली या AI? Detector का सच
ideas.hook: एक बड़े test में deepfake पकड़ने वाले आधे से ज़्यादा open-source detectors का score 60% से ऊपर नहीं गया — और सबसे कमज़ोर तो बिल्कुल सिक्का उछालने जितना था।
ideas.angle: Busts the idea that a deepfake detector can settle whether a viral image is real. A 2025 study with 500k+ face deepfake images found most open-source detectors weak, and simple JPEG compression or enhancement hurt them further. Teaches a 4-step, source-first check instead, and includes one clearly labelled AI clip to show how realistic AI output looks.
beats: 0-5s HOOK — Show: a coin-flip animation next to a 'Deepfake Detector' meter. Say the hook.

5-16s STUDY — Say: '2025 की एक study में 5 लाख से ज़्यादा नकली चेहरों वाली deepfake images बनाकर open-source detectors test किए गए। आधे से ज़्यादा का score 60% से ऊपर नहीं गया, और सबसे कमज़ोर 50% पर था — यानी सिक्का उछालने जितना।' Show: a bar chart with a 50% line labelled 'सिक्का' and a caption 'score = AUC; 50% = अंदाज़ा; images पर test'.

16-26s WHY IT GETS WORSE — Say: 'और photo को JPEG में compress करो — यानी size छोटा करने के लिए quality घटाओ — या "enhance" करो, तो detectors और कमज़ोर हो जाते हैं।' Show: an image pixelating step by step while the meter drops.
26-34s SHOW — Say: 'ये देखो — ये पूरा clip AI ने बनाया है।' Show: a 5s AI clip with a permanent on-screen label 'AI-GENERATED'.

34-52s 4-STEP CHECK — Say: 'तो detector नहीं, दिमाग लगाओ। एक: सबसे पहले किसने post किया — official handle है? दो: क्या भरोसेमंद news या fact-check पर यही ख़बर है? तीन: क्या ये तुम्हें गुस्सा, डर या लालच दिला रहा है? चार: शक हो तो forward मत करो।' Show: 4 numbered cards with checkboxes.
52-60s CTA — Say: 'Forward से पहले 10 सेकंड रुको। ये reel उस group में भेजो जहाँ सबसे ज़्यादा forwards आते हैं।'
ideas.india_angle: India's forward-heavy messaging culture (family and society WhatsApp groups) is where fake viral images spread. The reel builds a 'think before you forward' habit suited to Indian group chats, without naming any unverified incident.

visuals.two_d: Coin flip vs detector meter. A bar chart of detector scores with 50% and 60% lines and an 'AUC score' footnote. A pixelation sequence. 4 'source-first' cards. A stamp: 'FORWARD से पहले रुको'.
visuals.three_d: A 3D pixel-grid plane that degrades (compression) as the camera orbits, showing 'quality गिरी, detector फेल'.
ai_clips: 1 clip (5s), permanently labelled 'AI-GENERATED': an obviously synthetic but realistic scene with no people and no real landmarks, e.g. a herd of goats calmly walking through a generic rain-soaked city street at dusk. It demonstrates realism without creating plausible misinformation.

key_facts.claim: 'Evaluating Deepfake Detectors in the Wild' (Pirogov and Artemev, of the identity-verification company Sumsub) created a dataset of more than 500,000 high-quality deepfake images, mostly face-swap and synthetic faces, to test modern open-source detectors.
Fewer than half of the detectors tested achieved an AUC score above 60%; the lowest was 50% (equivalent to random guessing).
Basic image manipulations such as JPEG compression or image enhancement significantly reduce detector performance.

ideas.virality_reason: A counter-intuitive hook (detectors close to a coin toss) plus a visible 'this clip is AI' moment that makes viewers rewatch. The pause-before-forwarding habit is very shareable.
ideas.risk_notes: AUC is not 'accuracy'; on screen say 'score' and explain that 50% means guessing. The study tested open-source detectors on face images, not videos and not consumer detector apps, so don't generalise to 'every detector app'. Label the AI clip for its full duration, with no real people, places or logos. Don't name specific Indian fake-video incidents unless verified. The authors' company (Sumsub) sells identity-verification products; mention 'एक study' and don't over-cite.
ideas.verification_notes: The WebSearch budget was used up this run. I read the paper's abstract and introduction through the Hugging Face Hub connector. All 3 key facts were confirmed. Corrections: (1) The hook said 'accuracy'; the paper measures AUC, so it now says 'score'. (2) The study tested open-source detectors on face-swap and synthetic-face images, not videos or consumer apps. I changed the title from 'Viral वीडियो… Detector ऐप का सच' to 'Viral photo… Detector का सच' and added 'open-source' and 'images पर test'. (3) The beat's 'जैसे forward होते-होते quality गिरती है' asserted platform behaviour I could not verify; it now describes generic JPEG compression.

fact_checks.claim: Dataset of more than 500,000 high-quality deepfake images
fact_checks.note: Abstract. The deepfakes are mostly face-swap (Inswapper/'roop', SimSwap) plus synthetic images.

fact_checks.claim: Fewer than half of the detectors achieved AUC above 60%; the lowest was 50%
fact_checks.note: Abstract. The metric is AUC, not accuracy; the hook was corrected.

fact_checks.claim: JPEG compression or enhancement significantly reduces performance
fact_checks.note: Abstract.

fact_checks.claim: Hidden claim: this tells us about 'deepfake detector apps' and viral videos
fact_checks.note: The paper evaluates open-source detectors on images. Title and beats now say 'open-source detectors' and 'images'.

fact_checks.claim: Hidden claim: forwarding repeatedly lowers image quality
fact_checks.note: No source checked for a specific platform's behaviour. Reworded to generic JPEG compression.

ideas.title: AI वाला 'पैसा डबल' ad? स्कैम पहचानो
ideas.hook: मशहूर चेहरा, जानी-पहचानी आवाज़, और लाइन — 'मेरे AI app से पैसा डबल करो।' आज AI से ऐसे नकली ad और नकली reviews बनाना आसान है… तो पहचानोगे कैसे?
ideas.angle: Shows how AI makes scams look professional: fake shops built in minutes, AI-generated reviews, influencer endorsements and testimonials, and countdown timers. Gives the 4 red flags Microsoft lists, plus a logic punch. Twist: real AI help in finance exists through official channels. NPCI built FiMI by further training an open model (Mistral Small 24B) on Indian finance data, and NPCI's paper says it is used in UPI Help in English, Hindi and Hinglish.
beats: 0-5s HOOK — Show: a line-art ad frame with a face silhouette (no real person) and an 'AI APP = 2X' banner, then a crack runs across it.

5-17s HOW AI HELPS SCAMMERS — Say: 'Microsoft की April 2025 report: AI जैसे tools से अब कुछ ही मिनटों में नकली online दुकान खड़ी हो जाती है — पहले इसमें दिन या हफ़्ते लगते थे। और AI नकली reviews, influencer endorsements और testimonials भी बना देता है।' Show: a fake website assembling itself block by block, with fake 5-star reviews popping in.

17-32s RED FLAGS — Say: 'उसी report की चार निशानियाँ — एक: "सिर्फ आज" वाला offer और countdown timer। दो: तारीफ़, reviews और endorsements जिनकी कोई जाँच नहीं। तीन: social media का ad, जिसे तुमने खुद verify नहीं किया। चार: payment सिर्फ direct bank transfer या crypto में — जिनमें fraud protection नहीं होता।' Show: 4 red flags pinned onto the fake ad.
32-42s DESI LOGIC — Say: 'अब एक सेकंड रुको — अगर किसी के पास सच में पैसा डबल करने की मशीन होती, तो वो उसे तुम्हें reel में क्यों बेचता?' Show: a money-printing machine doodle with a '?'.

42-52s REAL HELP — Say: 'असली मदद official रास्ते से आती है। जैसे NPCI — जो UPI चलाता है — ने FiMI नाम का AI model बनाया। इसके लिए एक open model, Mistral Small 24B, को India के finance data पर आगे train किया गया — English, Hindi और Hinglish में। NPCI के paper के मुताबिक़ ये उसकी UPI Help में इस्तेमाल हो रहा है। और customer-care नंबर random search से नहीं, official app या website से लो।' Show: a green 'official' path vs a red 'random link' path.

52-60s CTA — Say: 'ठगी हो जाए तो तुरंत अपने बैंक को और सरकारी cyber-crime helpline को बताओ। ये reel उस दोस्त को भेजो जो हर "पैसा डबल" वाला group join कर लेता है।' Production note: add the national helpline number only after verifying it on the official site.
ideas.india_angle: Fast-growing retail investing and instant UPI payments make Indians targets for AI-polished 'money-doubling' ads. The positive twist honestly highlights a real India-built AI. NPCI's FiMI adapts Mistral Small 24B, is trained on about 68B tokens of curated financial, English/Hindi/Hinglish and synthetic data, and is already used in NPCI's UPI Help. Its reported gains are against its own Mistral base models, not 'beats ChatGPT'.

visuals.two_d: A fake-ad teardown with arrows labelling each of the 4 Microsoft red flags. A fake website assembling itself. A money-machine doodle. A split path, 'Official ✓' vs 'Random link ✗'. A FiMI fact card: 'NPCI • Mistral Small 24B base • English/Hindi/Hinglish • UPI Help'. A final card: 'बैंक + सरकारी cyber-crime helpline' (number only after verification).
visuals.three_d: Optional: a 3D phone mockup (generic, no brand) rotating to show a fake ad vs an official app screen.
ai_clips: Optional, 1 clip (5s): a hand scrolling a generic phone in a dark room, screen glow on the hand only, no face, no readable brand or app UI.

key_facts.claim: Microsoft Cyber Signals Issue 9: 'Fraudulent e-commerce websites can be set up in minutes using AI and other tools requiring minimal technical knowledge. Previously, it would take threat actors days or weeks to stand up convincing websites.' AI generates fake reviews, influencer endorsements and testimonials.

Microsoft consumer protection tips: beware 'limited-time' deals and countdown timers; don't trust fake social proof (AI-generated reviews, influencer endorsements, testimonials); don't click ads without verification ('Many scam sites spread through AI-optimized social media ads'); avoid direct bank transfers or cryptocurrency payments, 'which lack fraud protections'.

NPCI, the organisation responsible for UPI, developed FiMI (Finance Model for India). FiMI adapts the Mistral Small 24B architecture, with continued pre-training on 68 billion tokens of curated financial, multilingual (English, Hindi, Hinglish) and synthetic data, and 'has already been leveraged in NPCI's UPI Help'. The reported gains are +20% over Mistral Small 24B Base on finance reasoning and +87% over Mistral Small 24B Instruct on domain tool-calling.

ideas.virality_reason: Money gets high attention, the 'money machine' logic gives a satisfying punch, and the India AI fact is proud but honest. The red-flag list is screenshot-able and easy to send to a friend.
ideas.risk_notes: Never show a real celebrity's face or voice, even blurred, or fake ads naming real people. Don't say FiMI is 'better than ChatGPT' or 'India's own model from scratch'. It is built on Mistral Small 24B, and its reported gains are against that base. Red flags are limited to the 4 that Microsoft lists. 'Guaranteed returns' and 'Telegram tips groups' were not verified this run, so don't add them as facts. SEBI-registration advice and the helpline number must be verified on official sites before adding. Avoid giving investment advice.
ideas.verification_notes: The WebSearch budget was used up this run. I fetched the Microsoft blog directly, twice, checking for investment-scam content, and read the FiMI paper text (v2, Aug 2026) through the Hugging Face Hub connector. Confirmed: fake shops in minutes (previously days or weeks), AI-generated reviews, endorsements and testimonials, the 4 consumer tips, and the FiMI facts including UPI Help use. Corrected or removed: (1) The red flags 'गारंटीड मुनाफ़ा', 'Telegram/WhatsApp group में tips' and the 'AI trading bot' scam framing are not in the Microsoft report, and I couldn't reach Indian regulator sites. I replaced them with the 4 Microsoft-listed flags and reframed the title from 'AI Trading Bot' to 'AI वाला पैसा डबल ad'. (2) 'NPCI ने India के finance data पर अपना AI model बनाया' overstated it; it now says FiMI was built by further training the open Mistral Small 24B. (3) Removed the spoken '1930 / cybercrime.gov.in' line (unverified; sites blocked).

fact_checks.claim: AI can build fake online stores in minutes with descriptions, reviews and testimonials
fact_checks.note: 'can be set up in minutes… Previously… days or weeks'.

fact_checks.claim: Tips: limited-time deals and countdown timers, unverified endorsements and testimonials, avoid bank transfers and crypto
fact_checks.note: Consumer protection tips list; it also includes 'Clicking on ads without verification'.

fact_checks.claim: FiMI: adapts Mistral Small 24B, ~68B tokens incl. English/Hindi/Hinglish, used in NPCI's UPI Help
fact_checks.note: Abstract and introduction of the NPCI paper (v2 text, Aug 2026). The reported gains are against its Mistral base models.

fact_checks.claim: Hidden claim: 'NPCI ने India के finance data पर अपना AI model FiMI बनाया' (implies built from scratch)
fact_checks.note: FiMI was built by continued pre-training and fine-tuning of Mistral Small 24B. Reworded.

fact_checks.claim: Hidden red flags: guaranteed profit; tips in Telegram/WhatsApp groups; 'AI trading bot' investment scams
fact_checks.note: Not in the Microsoft source (which covers e-commerce, job and tech-support fraud). Removed as facts.

fact_checks.claim: Report cyber fraud on helpline 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in
fact_checks.note: Site blocked by the egress proxy; removed from the spoken script.

research_unverified.pillar: AI ka itihaas — dramatic true stories
research_unverified.landscape_notes:
RESEARCH CONTEXT (as of 2026-10-09). Network note: WebFetch could not reach en.wikipedia.org, deepmind.google, arxiv.org, techcrunch.com, computerhistory.org or newsonair.gov.in, so every fact below comes from WebSearch result summaries of the URLs listed. Before publishing, re-open primary pages wherever you can.

CORE TIMELINE (verified)
- 1950: Turing's "Computing Machinery and Intelligence" ran in Mind, Vol. 59 No. 236, October 1950, and opens with "Can machines think?" (https://csmt.uchicago.edu/annotations/turing.htm). He predicted that in about 50 years an average interrogator would have no more than a 70% chance of spotting the machine after 5 minutes (https://sites.cs.st-andrews.ac.uk/people/ipg1/AI/Lectures/ai/tsld008.htm).
