India link: his father was in the Indian Civil Service at Chatrapur (Madras Presidency, now Odisha). Biographer Andrew Hodges says Alan was conceived in British India, "most likely" at Chatrapur. Turing was born in London on 23 June 1912 (https://turingfilm.com/short-biography-by-andrew-hodges). Never say he was born in India.
- 2025 Turing-test study by Jones & Bergen (UC San Diego, arXiv 2503.23674, March 2025): with a humanlike persona prompt, GPT-4.5 was judged human 73% of the time and LLaMa-3.1-405B 56%. ELIZA and GPT-4o were baselines (https://arxiv.org/html/2503.23674v1). Without the persona it scored about 36% (https://decrypt.co/314780/openais-gpt-4-5-passes-turing-test?amp=1). Peer-review status is unclear.
- 1955/56 Dartmouth: the proposal is dated 31 Aug 1955 and signed by McCarthy, Minsky, Rochester and Shannon. It asked for a "2 month, 10 man study" in summer 1956 (https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/aimagazine/article/view/1904). The workshop ran 18 June–17 Aug 1956 (https://spectrum.ieee.org/dartmouth-ai-workshop). Some sources give the date as 2 Sep 1955.
- Raj Reddy: born 13 June 1937 in Katur, Chittoor district, Andhra Pradesh (https://www.britannica.com/biography/Raj-Reddy). He did his PhD under McCarthy, finished in 1966, and his thesis was the first PhD from Stanford's new CS department (https://amturing.acm.org/award_recipient/reddy_9634208). CHM says he shared that "first" with Bill McKeeman on the same day (https://computerhistory.org/blog/meet-2021-chm-fellow-honoree-raj-reddy/). He shared the 1994 Turing Award with Feigenbaum "for pioneering the design and construction of large scale AI systems" (https://awards.acm.org/award_winners/reddy_9634208) and was the first person of Asian origin to win it (https://heidelberg-laureate-forum.org/laureate/raj-reddy). Hearsay-I was demonstrated in June 1972 (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19930075166). DARPA set a 1,000-word goal in 1971; Harpy, built in his group in 1976, handled 1,011 words (https://soniox.com/wiki/history-of-speech-recognition). He helped set up RGUKT for rural youth (https://computerhistory.org/profile/raj-reddy/).
- 1966 ELIZA (Weizenbaum, MIT, CACM Jan 1966; https://elmcip.net/node/1538). The secretary anecdote comes from Weizenbaum's own account (https://www.mentalfloss.com/posts/eliza-chatbot-history). His 1976 warning about "powerful delusional thinking" is quoted at https://www.aol.com/articles/1960s-chatbot-precursor-ai-maker-153315777.html. Printouts of the code turned up at MIT in 2021, and it was run again on an emulated IBM 7094/CTSS (arXiv 2501.06707, Jan 2025; https://the-decoder.com/eliza-the-worlds-first-chatbot-is-back-online-after-six-decades-thanks-to-ai-historians/).
- Hype and winters: on 8 July 1958 the NYT reported the Navy's Perceptron claims (walk, talk, see, write, reproduce itself, be conscious). The real demo on an IBM 704 learned left versus right card marks after 50 trials (https://news.cornell.edu/node/313946). In 1970 Minsky told Life "in from three to eight years" (https://quoteinvestigator.com/2017/06/21/robot-pet/). The 1973 Lighthill report led to UK cuts (https://datacamp.com/blog/ai-winter). The Lisp-machine market collapsed in 1987, starting the second winter (https://www.holloway.com/g/making-things-think/sections/the-second-ai-winter-19871993). India's KBCS project in the late 1980s had UNDP help of about US$5.25M; the date in the 1988 Lok Sabha record is from garbled OCR, so hedge it (https://eparlib.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/2566444/1/08_X_02-03-1988_p74_p74_u1411.pdf).
- Deep Blue: it won game 1 on 10 Feb 1996, but Kasparov took that match 4–2 (https://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/february-10/kasparov-loses-chess-game-to-computer). On 11 May 1997, game 6 of the rematch, Kasparov resigned after 19 moves; the machine won 3.5–2.5 and searched about 200M positions a second (https://history.com/this-day-in-history/kasparov-defeats-chess-playing-computer). India links: chaturanga dates to the Gupta era, around the 6th century (https://www.chess.com/blog/OfficialShort/the-precursor-to-chess). Gukesh became the youngest world champion at 18 on 12 Dec 2024, beating Kasparov's record of 22 (https://www.thenewsminute.com/news/indias-18-year-old-gukesh-is-youngest-world-chess-champion).
- AlphaGo: the match ran 9–15 March 2016 in Seoul and ended 4–1 (https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/tech-science/20160315/alphago-wins-final-game-after-neck-and-neck-race). DeepMind's page gives: Move 37 was a 1-in-10,000 chance (a model estimate), Lee's Move 78 was also 1 in 10,000, more than 200M people watched, and Go has 10^170 possible configurations (https://deepmind.google/research/alphago/). Lee retired in Nov 2019 and spoke of "an entity that cannot be defeated" (https://edition.cnn.com/2019/11/27/tech/go-master-google-intl-hnk-scli/index.html). AlphaZero (Dec 2017) beat Stockfish 8 with 28 wins, 72 draws and 0 losses after about 4 hours of self-play (https://www.sciencealert.com/it-took-4-hours-google-s-ai-world-s-best-chess-player-deepmind-alphazero). Critics questioned the time controls (https://www.chess.com/news/view/updated-alphazero-crushes-stockfish-in-new-1-000-game-match).
- ImageNet and AlexNet (2012): top-5 error was 15.3% against 26.2% for the runner-up. It trained for 5–6 days on two GTX 580 3GB cards (https://courses.cs.duke.edu/fall16/compsci527/papers/Krizhevsky%20et%20al%20DNN%20ImageNet%202012.pdf). CHM says the training ran in Krizhevsky's bedroom at his parents' house; the code was released in March 2025 (https://computerhistory.org/blog/chm-releases-alexnet-source-code/, https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-alexnet-github-ai/). Fei-Fei Li says almost 50,000 workers from 167 countries did the labelling (https://unthinking.photography/imgexhaust/we-knew-we-needed-to-collect-a-data-set-that-has-far-more-images-than-we-have-ever-had-before-perhaps-thousands-of-times-more). India: Jitendra Malik (IIT Kanpur B.Tech 1980, UC Berkeley; https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~malik/malik-bio.html) co-authored R-CNN (CVPR 2014, more than 30% relative gain, 53.3% mAP; https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_cvpr_2014/papers/Girshick_Rich_Feature_Hierarchies_2014_CVPR_paper.pdf).
- Transformer: posted to arXiv on 12 June 2017 with 8 authors (https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762) and presented at NIPS 2017 (https://research.google/pubs/attention-is-all-you-need/). It scored 28.4 BLEU on English-German and trained in 3.5 days on 8 P100s (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762). The paper says author order is random and contributions were equal. India: Ashish Vaswani (B.Tech BIT Mesra) and Niki Parmar (B.E. PICT Pune) both studied in India (https://officechai.com/stories/the-indian-researchers-whose-work-led-to-the-creation-of-chatgpt). Say "studied in India". Do not call either the "lead author" or claim "Indians made ChatGPT".
- GPT-3: arXiv 28 May 2020, 175B parameters, 31 authors (https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165v2). Pune-born Prafulla Dhariwal is a co-author; he later led GPT-4o, and Altman credited him in May 2024 (https://yourstory.com/2024/05/prafulla-dhariwal-indian-creator-chatgpt-4o).
- ChatGPT: launched 30 Nov 2022 as a free research preview (https://www.nationalworld.com/recommended/technology/chatgpt-what-is-it-how-it-works-4001398). It passed 1M users in 5 days, per Altman (https://gizmodo.com/chatgpt-apps-ai-microsoft-google-1850065429). UBS estimated about 100M monthly users in Jan 2023; this is an estimate (https://tech.yahoo.com/apps/articles/chatgpt-may-fastest-growing-consumer-114524444.html). It reached 800M weekly on 6 Oct 2025 (https://tech.eu/2025/10/07/chatgpt-has-more-than-800m-weekly-active-users-says-altman/) and 900M weekly with 50M paying in Feb 2026 (https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/27/chatgpt-reaches-900m-weekly-active-users). India passed 100M weekly in Feb 2026 and is the #2 market with the most student users (https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-india-100-million-weekly-chatgpt-users/). On about 31 July 2026 OpenAI said its products have more than 1B "active users" (https://news.bloomberglaw.com/artificial-intelligence/openai-has-more-than-1-billion-users-2-million-businesses). Whether that is weekly, and whether it is ChatGPT only, is unconfirmed, so avoid stating "1B weekly".
- AlphaFold and the Nobels: AlphaFold2 was announced at CASP14 on 30 Nov 2020. Indian-born Nobel laureate Venki Ramakrishnan called it "a stunning advance on the protein-folding problem, a 50-year-old grand challenge" (https://deepmind.google/blog/alphafold-a-solution-to-a-50-year-old-grand-challenge-in-biology/). The Physics Nobel on 8 Oct 2024 went to Hopfield and Hinton (https://indiaai.gov.in/article/nobel-prize-in-physics-2024-awarded-to-ai-scientists). The Chemistry Nobel on 9 Oct 2024 went half to Baker and half to Hassabis and Jumper (https://alphagalileo.org/en-gb/Item-Display/ItemId/250899). The AlphaFold DB has more than 3M users in over 190 countries (https://deepmind.google/blog/alphafold-five-years-of-impact/, 25 Nov 2025). Hinton left Google on 1 May 2023 to speak about risks (https://www.cnbc.com/2023/05/01/godfather-of-ai-leaves-google-after-a-decade-to-warn-of-dangers.html).

MOST IMPORTANT 2025–2026 DEVELOPMENTS (verified)
- 27 Jan 2025: DeepSeek-R1 panic. Nvidia lost about $589B in a day, a record (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-01-27/asml-sinks-as-china-ai-startup-triggers-panic-in-tech-stocks). On 30 Jan 2025 India announced it would build its own foundation models on 18,693 GPUs (https://www.dtnext.in/news/national/global-ai-race-india-to-build-own-foundational-models-18693-gpus-to-power-compute-facility-821161). Sarvam was picked under the IndiaAI Mission in April 2025.
- 19–21 Jul 2025, IMO 2025: Gemini Deep Think scored 35/42, gold-level and IMO-certified (https://www.maginative.com/article/gemini-with-deep-think-achieves-gold-at-international-math-olympiad/). OpenAI's 35 was not officially entered. India won 3 gold, 2 silver and 1 bronze, came 7th, and set a record 193/252. Kanav Talwar scored 37 (https://www.imo-official.org/results/team/year/2025/country/IND/).
- 7 Aug 2025: GPT-5 released (https://abc7news.com/post/gpt-5-openai-releases-latest-model-fueling-chatgpt/17463301/).
- 16–20/21 Feb 2026: India AI Impact Summit at Bharat Mandapam, the first summit in this series hosted in the Global South (https://stratnewsglobal.com/india/india-preps-for-first-global-south-ai-summit/). Sarvam-30B and Sarvam-105B launched (benchmarks self-reported; Apache 2.0; https://www.drishtiias.com/daily-updates/daily-news-analysis/sarvam-30b-and-sarvam-105b/print_manually), along with BharatGen Param2 (17B MoE) and Gnani's model (https://www.freepressjournal.in/amp/tech/ai-summit-2026-meet-the-3-sovereign-ai-llm-models-that-were-unveiled-in-delhi-to-rival-global-tech-giants). The IndiaAI Mission has a ₹10,372 crore outlay, approved March 2024 (https://inc42.com/buzz/centre-to-set-up-600-data-labs-deploy-38k-gpus-indiaai-mission-ceo/), and more than 38,000 GPUs (https://negd.gov.in/press_release/indiaai-mission-expands-ai-ecosystem-with-affordable-compute-and-startup-support/).
- 19 Jun 2026: John Jumper left DeepMind for Anthropic. In July 2026 the FT reported that DeepMind had broken up the dedicated AlphaFold team. The database and server stay up (https://scientificamerican.com/article/why-google-deepmind-broke-up-the-alphafold-team, https://the-decoder.com/deepmind-dismantles-its-alphafold-team-as-key-authors-leave-for-anthropic/). Headlines saying "Google shuts down AlphaFold" are wrong.
- July 2026, IMO Shanghai: Huawei and Xiaohongshu said their AI models scored 42/42. These are company claims, and the models solved the problems after the human contest (https://standardmedia.co.ke/business/sci-tech/article/2001553533/ai-catches-up-with-humans-to-score-100pc-at-top-maths-contest). India won 2 gold and 4 silver (https://www.freepressjournal.in/education/international-mathematics-olympiad-2026-india-wins-2-gold-4-silver-medals).
- The 2026 Physics Nobel (Halzen, IceCube) and Chemistry Nobel (Kagan and Soai, announced 6–7 Oct 2026) are not AI-related (https://www.ynetnews.com/health_science/article/bk2wuc7smx). Do not say AI won a Nobel again in 2026.

DO NOT USE (unverified or false)
"GPT-6 released March 2026", "Hassabis stepped down" (single source), "Turing was born in India", "Indians built ChatGPT", "Raj Reddy invented Siri/Alexa", "AlexNet trained in a garage", "Dartmouth got $7,500" (unverified), and "1B weekly ChatGPT users" (unconfirmed).

AI-CLIP BUDGET FOR THIS PILLAR
9 clips at 7.5 credits = 67.5 credits. Every clip is human-free or hands-only, and none shows real people's faces. Real people (Turing, Reddy, Kasparov, Gukesh, Lee Sedol, the IMO students) appear only as line-art silhouettes or name cards, never as generated likenesses.

ideas.title: 1950 का AI exam — जो 75 साल बाद AI ने दिया
ideas.hook: 1950 में एक आदमी ने मशीनों के लिए एक exam बनाया… और 75 साल बाद AI उसमें इंसानों से आगे निकल गया — पर एक शर्त पर।
ideas.angle: Simple explanation of Turing's imitation game (Turing test) and his prediction. The 2025 UCSD study is the payoff: GPT-4.5 was judged human 73% of the time, but only with a persona prompt. The twist is that fooling people in chat is not the same as thinking.
beats: (0–3s) Hook line. SHOW: a typewriter page slides onto the cream background with 'Mind, October 1950 — Can machines think?'; an orange underline draws itself.

Turing ने कहा — 'सोचना' define करना मुश्किल है, तो एक खेल खेलो: imitation game, यानी नकल का खेल। Judge सिर्फ़ chat करके बताए — पर्दे के पीछे इंसान कौन, मशीन कौन। SHOW: 3 line-art boxes (Judge / Human / Machine), connector lines and chat bubbles pop in.
मज़ेदार बात — उस वक्त Turing के पिता Indian Civil Service में आज के ओडिशा के छत्रपुर में तैनात थे। SHOW: 3D globe, London ↔ Chatrapur arc, label '1912'.

उनकी भविष्यवाणी: करीब 50 साल में, 5 मिनट की बातचीत के बाद judge के सही पहचानने का chance 70% से ज़्यादा नहीं रहेगा। 2000 आया — ऐसा हुआ नहीं। SHOW: 5:00 countdown clock, meter capped at 70%, calendar flips 1950→2000 and gets an orange cross.

2025, UC San Diego की study: GPT-4.5 को 73% बार इंसान समझा गया — असली इंसान से भी ज़्यादा बार। 1966 वाला ELIZA भी तुलना के लिए test में था। SHOW: bar chart animates GPT-4.5 73%, LLaMa-3.1 56%, ELIZA and GPT-4o tagged 'baseline'.
लेकिन ध्यान से सुनो — शर्त थी: AI को पहले बोला गया 'इंसान जैसा persona बनाओ'। बिना उसके करीब 36%। SHOW: 'persona prompt ✓' checkbox unticks and the bar drops to ~36%.

सही: chat में AI इंसान जैसा लग सकता है। गलत: इसका मतलब ये नहीं कि वो इंसान जैसा सोचता या महसूस करता है। तुम judge होते तो AI को कैसे पकड़ते? Comment करो। SHOW: Sahi / Galat cards with tick and cross, then CTA card.
ideas.india_angle: Turing's father served in the Indian Civil Service at Chatrapur (Madras Presidency, now Odisha). Biographer Andrew Hodges says Alan was conceived in British India, 'most likely' at Chatrapur. Turing was born in London. This is presented as a light, true trivia hook.

visuals.two_d: Cream background with orange accent. Typewriter title card for Mind 1950. Three-box imitation-game diagram with drawn connector lines and chat bubbles. 5-minute clock and 70% meter. Calendar flip to 2000 with a cross. Bar chart of the 2025 study results. Persona-prompt checkbox that toggles. Sahi/Galat tick-and-cross cards. Phrase captions throughout.
visuals.three_d: Globe scene: camera starts on London (1912 label), draws a dotted arc to Chatrapur in Odisha, and gently zooms on a pin labelled 'छत्रपुर, ओडिशा'.
ai_clips: (1 clip, 5s) A 1950s British study desk lit by morning window light: a typewriter with a half-typed page, a fountain pen and a cup of tea. Slow dolly-in. No people and no faces.

key_facts.claim: Turing's 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence' was published in Mind, Vol. 59, No. 236, October 1950, and opens with the question 'Can machines think?'
Turing predicted that in about fifty years an average interrogator would have no more than a 70% chance of identifying the machine after five minutes of questioning (around the year 2000).
Turing was born 23 June 1912 in London. His father Julius Mathison Turing was in the Indian Civil Service at Chatrapur. Hodges writes he was conceived in British India, most likely at Chatrapur.
In Jones & Bergen's 2025 three-party, 5-minute Turing test, GPT-4.5 with a humanlike persona prompt was judged human 73% of the time, LLaMa-3.1-405B 56%. ELIZA and GPT-4o were baselines.
Without the persona prompt, GPT-4.5's rate dropped to about 36%.

ideas.virality_reason: It combines a 'test made in 1950, passed in 2025' payoff, a surprising number (73% beats real humans), a myth-bust twist (the persona condition) and an Odisha trivia hook. It also invites comments ('how would you catch the AI?').
ideas.risk_notes: Do not say Turing was born in India; say 'biographer के मुताबिक शायद'. Always state the persona condition and that the 2025 study's peer-review status is unclear. Do not claim AI 'thinks' or 'is conscious'. No generated face of Turing; use a silhouette or name card if needed.

ideas.title: 'Artificial Intelligence' — ये नाम आया कहाँ से?
ideas.hook: 'Artificial Intelligence' — ये नाम किसी lab में नहीं, पैसों की एक अर्ज़ी में पैदा हुआ था।
ideas.angle: The Dartmouth proposal of August 1955 named the field and promised big progress in 'one summer' of 1956. Seventy years later the checklist is still being worked on, which shows over-optimism is normal in AI. It ends on a cliffhanger leading into the Raj Reddy reel.
beats: (0–3s) Hook line. SHOW: a typed proposal sheet dated 'August 31, 1955' slides in and the phrase 'artificial intelligence' glows orange.

चार लोग — John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Nathaniel Rochester, Claude Shannon — ने लिखा: '2 महीने, 10 लोग' की study, 1956 की गर्मियों में, Dartmouth College में। SHOW: 4 name cards pop in (initials only, no faces); calendar 'Summer 1956'.
उनका दावा: सीखने का हर पहलू इतना साफ़-साफ़ describe किया जा सकता है कि मशीन उसकी नकल कर ले। SHOW: quote card animates in typewriter style.
लक्ष्य: मशीन भाषा बोले-समझे, concepts बनाए, इंसानों वाले problems सुलझाए, और खुद को improve करे — और सोचा, एक गर्मी में बड़ा advance हो जाएगा। SHOW: 4 empty checkboxes appear one by one.

जैसे हम सोचते हैं छुट्टियों में पूरा syllabus खत्म कर देंगे… Workshop 18 जून से 17 अगस्त 1956 तक चली — और ये checklist 70 साल बाद भी पूरी नहीं हुई, हालाँकि हर box में तेज़ progress है। SHOW: year ticker 1956→2026; checkboxes partly fill with orange bars labelled 'सांकेतिक'.

और McCarthy का एक छात्र — 1966 में Stanford Computer Science की पहली PhD में से एक, आंध्र प्रदेश के एक गाँव से — आगे चलकर computer science का सबसे बड़ा सम्मान लाया। कौन? अगली reel में। SHOW: 3D globe arc from Hanover, New Hampshire to Andhra Pradesh; a silhouette with '?'.
Follow करो ताकि Part 2 miss ना हो। SHOW: CTA card 'Part 2: कटूर गाँव से Turing Award'.
ideas.india_angle: McCarthy, who led the Dartmouth proposal, supervised Raj Reddy of Katur, Andhra Pradesh. Reddy completed his PhD in 1966, among the first PhDs of Stanford's new CS department. That sets up the next reel (series hook).

visuals.two_d: Typewritten proposal page with lines highlighting one by one. Four initials-only name cards. 'Summer 1956' calendar. Quote card. Four goal checkboxes with progress bars marked 'सांकेतिक' (illustrative). Year ticker. Silhouette with question mark.
visuals.three_d: Globe arc from Hanover, New Hampshire (USA) to Chittoor district, Andhra Pradesh, ending on a pulsing pin.

key_facts.claim: The Dartmouth proposal is dated 31 August 1955 and authored by McCarthy, Minsky, Rochester and Shannon. It proposed 'a 2 month, 10 man study of artificial intelligence' in summer 1956 at Dartmouth College.

The proposal's conjecture: every aspect of learning or any other feature of intelligence can in principle be so precisely described that a machine can be made to simulate it. It also says a significant advance can be made if a selected group works on it together for a summer.
The workshop ran from 18 June to 17 August 1956.
Raj Reddy completed his PhD in 1966 under John McCarthy. It was the first PhD granted by Stanford's newly formed CS department.
CHM notes Reddy shared the 'first Stanford CS PhD' distinction with Bill McKeeman, who defended the same day.

ideas.virality_reason: It answers a common question ('AI नाम किसने रखा?'), uses a relatable desi analogy (the vacation-syllabus plan) and ends on a cliffhanger that drives follows for Part 2.
ideas.risk_notes: The proposal date varies (31 Aug versus 2 Sep 1955), so say 'अगस्त 1955 के proposal में'. Do not state funding amounts, which could not be verified. Label the progress bars as illustrative. Use no photos or generated faces of the four authors; initials only.

ideas.title: कटूर गाँव से Turing Award तक: राज रेड्डी
ideas.hook: Computer science का सबसे बड़ा सम्मान जीतने वाले पहले एशियाई मूल के इंसान — आंध्र प्रदेश के एक छोटे से गाँव से थे।
ideas.angle: Raj Reddy's journey: he grew up in a village, studied under McCarthy, worked on getting machines to understand continuous speech (Hearsay, Harpy), won the 1994 Turing Award, then came back to build education for rural Indian youth. The reel teaches what speech recognition is.
beats: (0–3s) Hook line. SHOW: 3D globe zooms into Chittoor district, AP; pin 'कटूर, 1937'.

1960s में Stanford में John McCarthy के छात्र बने, और 1966 में वहाँ के नए Computer Science department की पहली PhD में से एक पाई — topic: speech recognition, यानी मशीन को इंसान की आवाज़ समझाना। SHOW: timeline line-art; a sound wave morphs into letters.
1972: Carnegie Mellon में उनका Hearsay-I — लगातार बोले गए वाक्य समझने वाले शुरुआती systems में से एक। SHOW: waveform segments matched to words with drawn connector lines.
1971 में DARPA ने लक्ष्य दिया: करीब 1,000 शब्द। 1976 में उनके group का Harpy — 1,011 शब्द। SHOW: counter 0→1,011 with a goal line at 1,000 and a tick.
1994: Turing Award — Edward Feigenbaum के साथ — 'large scale AI systems' के लिए। Turing Award पाने वाले पहले एशियाई मूल के इंसान। SHOW: award card pops in with the citation phrase.
फिर भारत लौटकर नींव रखी: RGUKT जैसी university बनाने में मदद — गाँव के होनहार, कम आय वाले बच्चों के लिए। SHOW: India map pins for Hyderabad/AP; graduation-cap icons multiply.
आज जब तुम phone से बोलकर search करते हो — उस सफ़र की नींव में ऐसे pioneers हैं। ये reel उस दोस्त को भेजो जो सोचता है गाँव से बड़ा नहीं बन सकते। SHOW: phone mic icon pulses; CTA.
ideas.india_angle: This is a fully Indian story. Reddy was born in Katur, Chittoor district, AP, was the first person of Asian origin to win the Turing Award, and later helped found education institutions for rural youth in India. The tone is pride without overclaiming (he did not 'invent Siri/Alexa').

visuals.two_d: Line-art journey map Katur → Stanford → Pittsburgh (CMU). Sound-wave-to-text morph. 0→1,011 word counter against a goal line. Award card with an orange ribbon. Graduation caps on an India map. Reddy shown only as a line-art name card (no realistic face).
visuals.three_d: Globe sequence: zoom into Andhra Pradesh, then arcs to California and Pennsylvania, then back to Hyderabad with a glowing return arc.
ai_clips: (1 clip, 5s) A 1970s university computer lab: reel-to-reel tape drives spinning, a vintage microphone on a desk, a green-phosphor terminal showing waveform lines. Warm tungsten light, no people and no faces.

key_facts.claim: Raj Reddy was born 13 June 1937 in Katur, a village in Chittoor district of present-day Andhra Pradesh.
He shared the 1994 ACM A.M. Turing Award with Edward Feigenbaum 'for pioneering the design and construction of large scale artificial intelligence systems'.
Reddy was the first person of Asian origin to receive the Turing Award.
PhD 1966 under John McCarthy, the first PhD of Stanford's newly formed CS department. ACM notes ideas from his group underlie much of modern commercial speech recognition.
Hearsay-I, the first speech understanding system at CMU, was demonstrated in June 1972.
key_facts.source_date: NASA NTRS record of Reddy retrospective

key_facts.claim: DARPA's Speech Understanding Research program began in 1971 with a ~1,000-word goal. Harpy (Lowerre, in Reddy's group) met it in 1976 with 1,011 words.
Reddy helped establish Rajiv Gandhi University of Knowledge Technologies to serve low-income, gifted, rural youth.

ideas.virality_reason: A village-to-global-top story is highly shareable in India. Pride without exaggeration, plus a 'send to a friend' CTA that suits WhatsApp sharing.
ideas.risk_notes: Say 'एशियाई मूल के पहले' (first of Asian origin), not 'first Asian-born'. Do not claim he invented modern voice assistants; say 'नींव में योगदान'. The Stanford 'first PhD' was shared with McKeeman, so use 'पहली PhD में से एक'. No generated likeness of Reddy.

ideas.title: 1966 का chatbot जिससे लोग दिल की बात करने लगे
ideas.hook: 1966 का एक chatbot — जो बस तुम्हारी ही बात घुमाकर लौटा देता था — फिर भी लोग उससे दिल की बातें करने लगे।
ideas.angle: The reel shows how ELIZA's simple pattern-matching trick works and explains the 'ELIZA effect': people read real understanding and feelings into machine words. The twist is that the original code was revived in 2025 and used in a modern Turing test. The responsible takeaway: caring-sounding text is not real feeling, and real help is available.
beats: (0–3s) Hook line. SHOW: line-art terminal types 'मैं उदास हूँ' → 'तुम उदास क्यों हो?'
1966, MIT: Joseph Weizenbaum का ELIZA। उसका DOCTOR script एक therapist की नकल करता था। SHOW: 'Communications of the ACM, Jan 1966' card.
Trick सिंपल: pattern matching, यानी keyword पकड़ो और तुम्हारा ही वाक्य सवाल बनाकर लौटा दो। ना समझ, ना memory। SHOW: keyword highlighted in orange; arrows swap words into a template.
फिर भी — Weizenbaum ने खुद लिखा — उनकी secretary ने थोड़ी देर बात करके कहा: 'आप ज़रा कमरे से बाहर जाइए।' SHOW: door icon swings shut; caption 'ELIZA effect'.

ELIZA effect यानी मशीन के शब्दों में इंसानी समझ और भावनाएँ देख लेना। Weizenbaum इतने परेशान हुए कि 1976 में चेतावनी भरी किताब लिखी। SHOW: quote card 'powerful delusional thinking in quite normal people'.

2021 में इसका original code MIT के archive में printouts में मिला, 2025 में फिर से चलाया गया — और 2025 के Turing test experiment में भी ELIZA शामिल था। SHOW: a box of papers opens and turns into an emulator screen.

सीख: आज के chatbots ELIZA से कहीं ज़्यादा capable हैं, पर हमदर्दी वाले शब्द = असली feelings नहीं। मन भारी हो तो किसी इंसान से बात करो — Tele-MANAS 14416, free, 24×7, अपनी भाषा में। ये reel किसी ऐसे को भेजो जिसे ज़रूरत हो। SHOW: helpline card, then CTA.
ideas.india_angle: For Indian viewers who use chatbots for emotional conversations, the reel points to India's government Tele-MANAS helpline (14416), which is free, runs 24/7 and works in the caller's chosen language. It is a responsible, genuine local resource, not a forced link.

visuals.two_d: Terminal-style chat in cream/orange line art. Keyword-highlight and template-swap animation. Door icon. 'ELIZA effect' definition card. Quote card. A box of printouts turning into an emulator window. Tele-MANAS helpline card with a phone icon.
visuals.three_d: Optional: a simple code-rendered 3D teletype terminal model rotating slowly while the text prints (no data scene needed).
ai_clips: (1 clip, 5s) A 1960s university computer room: a teletype terminal printing lines of text on continuous paper, a large mainframe cabinet with blinking lights behind it. Soft fluorescent light, no people and no faces.

key_facts.claim: Weizenbaum's ELIZA paper appeared in Communications of the ACM, Volume 9, Issue 1, January 1966.
ELIZA's DOCTOR script parodied a Rogerian psychotherapist. Weizenbaum's secretary reportedly asked him to leave the room so she could talk with it privately.
In Computer Power and Human Reason (1976) Weizenbaum wrote that 'extremely short exposures to a relatively simple computer program could induce powerful delusional thinking in quite normal people.'
Printouts of the original ELIZA code were found in Weizenbaum's MIT archives in 2021 and run again on a restored CTSS on an emulated IBM 7094 (arXiv paper Jan 2025).
ELIZA was included as a baseline in the 2025 Jones & Bergen Turing test study.
Tele-MANAS national tele-mental-health helpline: 14416 (or 1-800-89-14416), toll-free, 24/7, caller's language of choice. Launched 10 Oct 2022.

ideas.virality_reason: The secretary anecdote is surprising and human. It ties straight to how people use ChatGPT today, and the helpline adds save-and-share value.
ideas.risk_notes: Mental-health sensitivity: do not shame people who use AI for support or say AI is 'dangerous'. Just separate words from feelings and give the helpline respectfully. Attribute the secretary story to Weizenbaum's own account. Check the helpline number right before publishing. No visual distress imagery.

ideas.title: 1958 में भी कहा था 'AI सब कर लेगा' — फिर आई सर्दी
ideas.hook: 1958 में अख़बार ने छापा: ये मशीन चलेगी, बोलेगी, देखेगी, लिखेगी… और खुद को महसूस भी करेगी। 68 साल हो गए।
ideas.angle: AI hype cycles: the 1958 Perceptron headlines, Minsky's 1970 '3–8 years' prediction, the 1973 Lighthill report and the first AI winter, and the 1987 Lisp-machine collapse and second winter. The reel gives a sahi/galat/normal framework for judging today's AI claims, and notes that India had an AI project in the 1980s too.
beats: (0–3s) Hook line. SHOW: generic old-newspaper-style line-art card (no real masthead) with verbs popping in: चलेगी, बोलेगी, देखेगी, लिखेगी…

असल demo: Navy का Perceptron, IBM 704 computer पर — 50 बार की कोशिश के बाद बस ये पहचानना सीखा कि card पर निशान बाएँ है या दाएँ। SHOW: two cards with left/right marks; checkbox ticks after the counter reaches 50.
1970: Marvin Minsky ने Life magazine से कहा — 3 से 8 साल में औसत इंसान जितनी general intelligence वाली मशीन। SHOW: countdown 1970→1978, then an orange cross.
वादे पूरे नहीं हुए → 1973 में UK की Lighthill report → AI funding कटा → पहली 'AI winter', यानी पैसा और भरोसा दोनों ठंडे। SHOW: an 'AI मौसम' thermometer drops; snowflakes fall.
1980s में expert systems का boom, फिर 1987 में महंगी Lisp machines का बाज़ार ढहा — दूसरी सर्दी। SHOW: the thermometer rises and then dips again.

भारत भी इस कहानी में था — 1980s में KBCS यानी Knowledge Based Computer Systems project, UNDP की मदद से। और आज IndiaAI Mission: ₹10,372 करोड़, 38,000 से ज़्यादा GPUs। SHOW: India map card, then 3D GPU bars rise.

सही: आज का AI सच में काम कर रहा है। गलत: 'अगले साल सब बदल जाएगा' वाले हर दावे पर आँख मूँदकर भरोसा। Normal: hype और सर्दी का cycle पहले भी आया है। अगला AI दावा सुनो तो पूछो — demo है या सिर्फ़ दावा? SHOW: Sahi/Galat/Normal cards, then CTA 'Follow for सच्चा AI'.
ideas.india_angle: India ran its own UNDP-assisted Knowledge Based Computer Systems (KBCS) project in the late 1980s, with nodal centres and KBCS conferences such as KBCS '89 in Bombay. Today the IndiaAI Mission has a ₹10,372 crore outlay and more than 38,000 GPUs. This places India inside the history, not outside it.

visuals.two_d: Generic vintage newspaper card (no NYT logo or layout). Left/right card-recognition demo with a trial counter. Countdown to 1978 with a cross. An 'AI मौसम' thermometer line chart across 1958–2026, explicitly labelled 'सांकेतिक' (illustrative), with snowflakes in the winters. India map card for KBCS. Sahi/Galat/Normal triad.
visuals.three_d: 3D data scene: a bar for the IndiaAI Mission's 38,000+ GPUs rising beside a ₹10,372 crore label (real numbers only).
ai_clips: (1 clip, 5s) An abandoned 1980s computer lab: dust-covered beige workstations and a big cabinet computer, snow falling outside a large window, cold blue light. No people and no faces.

key_facts.claim: On 8 July 1958 the New York Times reported the Navy's Perceptron, which it was expected would walk, talk, see, write, reproduce itself and be conscious of its existence. In the demo on an IBM 704, it learned to tell left-marked from right-marked cards after 50 trials.
In a 1970 LIFE magazine article Minsky said: 'In from three to eight years we will have a machine with the general intelligence of an average human being.'
The 1973 Lighthill report criticised AI's failure to meet its 'grandiose objectives', leading to UK funding cuts (first AI winter).
Around 1987 the specialised Lisp-machine market collapsed as cheaper workstations caught up, part of the second AI winter (c. 1987–1993).
India's KBCS project was a five-year project with Rs 8 crore budget and UNDP assistance of US$5.25 million (1988 Lok Sabha record; start date in OCR unclear, late 1980s).
The IndiaAI Mission was approved in March 2024 with an outlay of ₹10,372 crore over five years.
More than 38,000 GPUs have been onboarded on the IndiaAI compute portal.

ideas.virality_reason: Contrarian and useful: a vintage hype quote set against today's hype, plus a reusable 'demo या दावा?' rule that viewers can apply to any AI news. The India-in-the-1980s fact surprises people.
ideas.risk_notes: Do not reproduce the NYT masthead. Label the hype thermometer as illustrative, not data. Hedge the KBCS dates ('1980s में'). Do not predict a coming 'AI winter'. Re-check the GPU count before posting, since it grows over time.

ideas.title: Deep Blue ने Kasparov को हराया — फिर आया गुकेश
ideas.hook: 1997 में एक मशीन ने दुनिया के chess champion को हरा दिया… और 2024 में उसी champion का एक record एक 18 साल के भारतीय ने तोड़ दिया।
ideas.angle: Deep Blue against Kasparov (1996 and 1997), explained honestly: Deep Blue calculated about 200 million positions a second by brute-force search rather than 'thinking'. The India loop: chess comes from India's chaturanga, and Gukesh broke Kasparov's youngest-champion record.
beats: (0–3s) Hook line. SHOW: line-art chessboard; the black king topples with an orange flash.
10 फरवरी 1996: IBM के Deep Blue ने Kasparov को एक game में हराया — पर match Kasparov जीते, 4–2। SHOW: scoreboard card '1996: Kasparov 4 – 2'.
1997 rematch, New York — 11 मई, game 6: Kasparov ने सिर्फ़ 19 चालों में हार मान ली। Final: 3.5–2.5, मशीन जीती। SHOW: '1997' scoreboard; move counter stops at 19.

पर क्या Deep Blue 'सोचता' था? नहीं — ये हर सेकंड करीब 20 करोड़ positions calculate करता था। यानी brute force — जैसे exam में हर option try करके देखना। SHOW: 3D search tree explodes outward; counter '200,000,000 / sec'.
और ये खेल आया कहाँ से? भारत के चतुरंग से — गुप्त काल, करीब छठी सदी। चार अंग: पैदल, घोड़े, हाथी, रथ। SHOW: 4 army icons pop in over an India map.

Twist: Kasparov 1985 में 22 साल की उम्र में world champion बने — सबसे कम उम्र का record। 12 दिसंबर 2024 को 18 साल के गुकेश ने ये record तोड़ा — Anand के बाद दूसरे भारतीय world champion। SHOW: age bars 22 vs 18; trophy card.
मशीन ने champion को हराया, पर चतुरंग की धरती ने champion बनाना नहीं छोड़ा। अपने chess वाले दोस्त को tag करो। SHOW: CTA card.
ideas.india_angle: Chess descends from India's chaturanga (Gupta era, around the 6th century CE). In December 2024, D. Gukesh of Chennai became the youngest world champion at 18, breaking the age record Kasparov set in 1985, and became the second Indian world champion after Viswanathan Anand.

visuals.two_d: Chessboard line art. Scoreboard cards for 1996 and 1997. A 19-move counter. A spinning '200,000,000/sec' counter. Four chaturanga army icons (infantry, cavalry, elephant, chariot) on an India outline. Age bar comparison 22 vs 18. People shown only as name cards.
visuals.three_d: Code-rendered 3D move-search tree branching from a chess position (an illustration of brute-force search), then a slow orbit around 3D chess pieces.
ai_clips: (1 clip, 5s) A dramatic 1990s event hall: a chessboard on a table under a single spotlight, a tall black server cabinet with blinking lights behind it. No people and no faces.

key_facts.claim: On 10 February 1996 in Philadelphia, Deep Blue won game 1, the first game a computer won against a reigning world champion under tournament conditions.
Kasparov won the 1996 match 4–2.
On 11 May 1997 Kasparov resigned game 6 after 19 moves. Deep Blue won the rematch 3½–2½. The upgraded Deep Blue could examine 200 million positions per second.
The earliest clear reference to chaturanga is from north India in the Gupta Empire, around the 6th century AD. Chaturanga means 'four limbs' (infantry, cavalry, elephants, chariots).
On 12 December 2024 in Singapore, 18-year-old Gukesh beat Ding Liren to become the youngest world champion, second Indian after Anand.
Gukesh broke Kasparov's record; Kasparov was 22 when he won the title in 1985.

ideas.virality_reason: Man against machine, plus Indian chess pride (Gukesh is a recent national hero), plus a satisfying 'record broken' loop. The tag-a-friend CTA reaches chess communities.
ideas.risk_notes: Say 'youngest undisputed world champion' if challenged. Do not repeat Kasparov's cheating allegation as fact (IBM denied it). Say 'करीब 20 करोड़'. No generated faces of Kasparov, Gukesh or Anand; name cards only. Gukesh's Chennai origin is fine to state.

ideas.title: Move 37: वो चाल जो 10,000 में 1 इंसान चलता
ideas.hook: 2016 में एक AI ने ऐसी चाल चली कि commentators को लगा — गलती हो गई। फिर वही चाल game जिता गई।
ideas.angle: AlphaGo against Lee Sedol. It explains why Go is hard (10^170 positions) and what reinforcement learning means, using the move DeepMind estimated a human would play 1 time in 10,000. The twist is that the human answered with his own '1 in 10,000' Move 78. The coda is AlphaZero learning chess from the rules alone.
beats: (0–3s) Hook line. SHOW: 19×19 line-art grid; a stone drops at an odd spot; a big orange '37'.

Go — एक पुराना board game। इसकी संभावित positions करीब 10^170 — यानी 1 के बाद 170 ज़ीरो — ब्रह्मांड के atoms (करीब 10^80) से कहीं ज़्यादा। SHOW: 3D zoom-out from the board into a galaxy; log-scale bars 10^80 vs 10^170.
मार्च 2016, Seoul: DeepMind का AlphaGo vs Lee Sedol। Game 2, move 37 — DeepMind के अंदाज़े से कोई इंसान ऐसी चाल 10,000 में 1 बार चलता। SHOW: a 10,000-dot grid with one orange dot.

Commentators हैरान — गलती या जादू? वही चाल game जिता गई। AlphaGo ने इंसानी games से सीखा, फिर खुद से बार-बार खेलकर — इसे reinforcement learning कहते हैं, यानी इनाम-सज़ा से सीखना। SHOW: self-play loop arrows; +1/-1 reward tokens.
पर इंसान ने भी जवाब दिया: Game 4 में Lee का move 78 — वो भी 10,000 में 1 वाली चाल — और Lee जीते। Final 4–1। SHOW: scoreboard 4–1 with Game 4 highlighted.

2017 में AlphaZero ने सिर्फ़ rules से, खुद से खेलकर chess सीखा — वही chess जिसकी जड़ भारत का चतुरंग है — और Stockfish के खिलाफ 100 games में एक भी नहीं हारा। 2019 में Lee ने retire होते वक्त कहा: 'एक entity है जिसे हराया नहीं जा सकता।' SHOW: chessboard card 28W–72D–0L; quote card.
तुम्हें क्या लगता है — Move 37 creativity थी या सिर्फ़ calculation? Comment करो। SHOW: poll-style two-option card.
ideas.india_angle: AlphaGo's successor AlphaZero learned chess, a descendant of India's chaturanga, purely by self-play from the rules. This is a modest, true link. The reel also uses a desi analogy: a gully-cricket shot that no coaching book teaches but that wins the match.

visuals.two_d: 19×19 grid with stones popping in. A big '37'. A 10,000-dot probability grid. Self-play loop diagram with reward tokens. Scoreboard 4–1. AlphaZero 28/72/0 card. Quote card. People shown only as name cards.
visuals.three_d: Data scene: camera pulls back from a 3D Go board into a starfield, with log-scale bars comparing ~10^80 atoms against 10^170 Go positions.
ai_clips: (1 clip, 5s) Extreme close-up of a hand (no face, no identifiable person) placing a white stone on a wooden Go board. Cinematic shallow depth of field, soft side light, the stone clicks into place.

key_facts.claim: AlphaGo vs Lee Sedol was played in Seoul, 9–15 March 2016, and AlphaGo won 4–1.
DeepMind says Move 37 in game 2 had a 1 in 10,000 chance of being played (model-based estimate). Lee's Move 78 in game 4 also had about a 1 in 10,000 chance.
Go has about 10^170 possible board configurations, more than the number of atoms in the known universe. DeepMind says the match was watched by over 200 million people.
Lee Sedol retired in November 2019, saying 'Even if I become the number one, there is an entity that cannot be defeated.'
In Dec 2017, AlphaZero, given only chess rules, trained by self-play for about 4 hours and beat Stockfish 8 in 100 games: 28 wins, 72 draws, 0 losses.
Critics noted the 2017 time control (1 minute per move) disadvantaged Stockfish. A later 1,000-game match still favoured AlphaZero.

ideas.virality_reason: A mystery move, a jaw-dropping number (10^170), a human comeback (Move 78) and a debate CTA ('creativity या calculation?') that drives comments.
ideas.risk_notes: Frame 1-in-10,000 as DeepMind's estimate. Lee's retirement had other reasons too (a dispute with the Korea Baduk Association), so say 'मुख्य वजह AI बताई'. Present AI 'creativity' as a debate, not a fact. Give the 200M viewers as DeepMind's figure. Only hands, no faces.

ideas.title: 2 gaming GPU, 1 bedroom — और AI बदल गया
ideas.hook: आज वाले AI की नींव का एक बड़ा पल किसी बड़े lab में नहीं — एक लड़के के bedroom में, दो gaming graphics cards पर आया था।
ideas.angle: What ImageNet, deep learning and GPUs are, told through AlexNet in 2012: a 15.3% error rate against 26.2%, trained on two GTX 580s in Krizhevsky's bedroom. India angle: Jitendra Malik's R-CNN used the same kind of network to find where objects are in a photo.
beats: (0–3s) Hook line. SHOW: line-art bedroom at night, a PC with two graphics cards glowing orange.
पहला ingredient: ImageNet — लाखों labelled photos। Label किए करीब 50,000 लोगों ने, 167 देशों से, internet पर। SHOW: thumbnail grid (cat, dog, mushroom icons) getting tick-labels; world dots light up.
2012 का ImageNet competition: Toronto के Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever और Geoffrey Hinton का AlexNet — top-5 error 15.3%, दूसरे नंबर की team 26.2%। SHOW: bar race, 26.2 shrinking to 15.3 in orange.

Trick: deep neural network — यानी rules हम नहीं लिखते, model photos देखकर खुद features सीखता है। और GPU यानी हज़ारों छोटे हिसाब एक साथ — जैसे एक student की जगह पूरी class एक-एक sum साथ में solve करे। SHOW: 3D CNN layer blocks; classroom analogy icons.
Training: 5–6 दिन, दो NVIDIA GTX 580 पर — Computer History Museum के मुताबिक Alex के parents के घर वाले bedroom में। SHOW: calendar ticks 5–6 days; back to the bedroom scene.

India connection: IIT Kanpur से पढ़े Berkeley professor जितेंद्र मलिक की टीम ने इसी तरह के network से R-CNN बनाया — photo में चीज़ें कहाँ हैं, ये ढूँढना — पिछले best से 30% से ज़्यादा बेहतर। SHOW: a street photo where boxes draw themselves around objects.
बड़ी खोजें हमेशा बड़े labs से नहीं आतीं। Save करो — और बताओ, तुम्हारे laptop में कौन सा GPU है? SHOW: CTA.
ideas.india_angle: Jitendra Malik (born in Mathura, B.Tech IIT Kanpur 1980, now at UC Berkeley) co-authored R-CNN. That paper took ImageNet-pretrained CNNs (AlexNet-style) and applied them to object detection, the 'where is it in the photo' problem behind many camera and vision applications.

visuals.two_d: Bedroom line art with glowing GPUs. Image-label grid with ticks. Error-rate bar race. Classroom-parallelism analogy. 5–6 day calendar. A photo with bounding boxes drawing on. Phrase captions: 'deep learning', 'GPU', 'ImageNet'.
visuals.three_d: Code-rendered 3D stack of convolutional layers (blocks shrinking and deepening) with data flowing through, then a globe whose dots pulse to represent the 167 countries of labellers (labelled 'सांकेतिक', since per-country data is not shown).
ai_clips: (1 clip, 5s) A 2012-era teenager's bedroom at night: a PC tower with its side panel open, two graphics cards with spinning fans and an orange glow, a CRT-style monitor showing a falling training-loss curve. No people and no faces.

key_facts.claim: AlexNet (Krizhevsky, Sutskever, Hinton) achieved 15.3% top-5 error in ILSVRC-2012, versus 26.2% for the second-best entry. It took 5–6 days to train on two GTX 580 3GB GPUs.
The Computer History Museum says AlexNet was trained on a computer with two NVIDIA cards in Krizhevsky's bedroom at his parents' house. CHM released the source code with Google in March 2025.
Coverage of the CHM code release dated 27 March 2025.
Fei-Fei Li: almost 50,000 workers from 167 countries helped clean, sort and label ImageNet's candidate images.
Jitendra Malik: B.Tech IIT Kanpur 1980, PhD Stanford 1985, at UC Berkeley since 1986. His group's work includes R-CNN.
R-CNN (Girshick, Donahue, Darrell, Malik; CVPR 2014) improved mAP by more than 30% relative to the previous best on PASCAL VOC 2012, achieving 53.3%.

ideas.virality_reason: The underdog 'bedroom to revolution' story connects with gamers and students. The GPU question in the CTA invites comments, and the IIT Kanpur connection gives Indian pride.
ideas.risk_notes: Attribute the bedroom detail to CHM and do not say 'garage'. Do not say AlexNet 'invented' deep learning; say 'turning point'. Avoid NVIDIA logos (show generic cards). Say ImageNet has 'लाखों/करोड़ों' images unless a ~14M figure is confirmed from a non-wiki source. No faces of the researchers.

ideas.title: ChatGPT का 'T' — 8 लेखक, 2 ने भारत में पढ़ाई की
ideas.hook: ChatGPT में जो 'T' है ना — वो 2017 के एक research paper से आया… और उसके 8 लेखकों में से 2 ने engineering भारत में की थी।
ideas.angle: The reel explains 'attention' and the Transformer in plain words, and why it trains fast in parallel. It busts the overclaim 'भारतीयों ने ChatGPT बनाया' while stating the true India link: Vaswani (BIT Mesra) and Parmar (PICT Pune) are among the eight equal co-authors.
beats: (0–3s) Hook line. SHOW: big 'GPT' letters; the 'T' zooms forward.
GPT यानी Generative Pre-trained Transformer। Transformer आया 12 जून 2017 के paper 'Attention Is All You Need' से — Google के 8 researchers। SHOW: paper title card; 8 name cards shuffle.

Attention समझो: 'राहुल ने रोहन को बैट दिया क्योंकि उसका match था।' 'उसका' किसका? Model हर शब्द को बाकी सब शब्दों से जोड़कर देखता है — यही attention। SHOW: connector lines from 'उसका' to 'राहुल' and 'रोहन' with different thickness.

पुराने models एक-एक शब्द क्रम से पढ़ते थे; Transformer पूरा वाक्य एक साथ — इसलिए GPUs पर तेज़। Paper का बड़ा model 8 GPUs पर 3.5 दिन में train हुआ। SHOW: sequential vs parallel animation; '8 GPU × 3.5 दिन' card.
India connection: 8 में से 2 — आशीष वासवानी (BIT Mesra, रांची) और निकी परमार (PICT, पुणे) — ने engineering भारत में की। SHOW: India map pins Ranchi and Pune with arcs to California.

Myth-buster: 'भारतीयों ने ChatGPT बनाया' — गलत, overclaim। ChatGPT OpenAI ने बनाया। सही: उसकी नींव वाले paper के 8 बराबर co-authors में 2 भारत में पढ़े। Paper में लिखा है — author order random है। SHOW: Sahi/Galat cards; the name cards shuffle again to show the random order.
Title भी मज़ेदार — Beatles के गाने 'All You Need Is Love' का reference। ये reel engineering वाले दोस्त को भेजो। SHOW: music-note doodle, then CTA.
ideas.india_angle: Two of the eight equal co-authors of the 2017 Transformer paper did their engineering degrees in India: Ashish Vaswani (B.Tech, BIT Mesra, Ranchi) and Niki Parmar (B.E., PICT, Pune). The reel deliberately corrects the common overclaim that 'Indians made ChatGPT'.

visuals.two_d: GPT letters with the T zooming. Paper title card. Eight shuffling name cards (text only). An attention diagram with weighted connector lines over a Hindi sentence. Sequential-vs-parallel reading animation. Sahi/Galat cards. India map with Ranchi and Pune pins.
visuals.three_d: Globe arc from Ranchi and Pune to California; optionally a 3D 'attention web' of word tokens connected by glowing lines.

key_facts.claim: 'Attention Is All You Need' was submitted to arXiv on 12 June 2017 by eight authors: Vaswani, Shazeer, Parmar, Uszkoreit, Jones, Gomez, Kaiser, Polosukhin.
The paper was published at NIPS 2017.
The big Transformer reached 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-German. Training took 3.5 days on 8 P100 GPUs. The author footnote states equal contribution and random listing order.
Ashish Vaswani completed engineering in Computer Science at BIT Mesra, then a Master's and PhD at USC.
Niki Parmar earned a B.E. in Information Technology from Pune Institute of Computer Technology and a master's from USC.
OpenAI's 2018 paper 'Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training' introduced the generative pre-training + fine-tuning approach behind GPT.
The paper's title references the Beatles song 'All You Need Is Love'.

ideas.virality_reason: Everyone uses 'GPT' without knowing what the T means. The honest India link, together with a myth-bust of a viral WhatsApp-style claim, builds trust and gets shares among engineering students.
ideas.risk_notes: Say 'भारत में पढ़े' rather than 'Indian-origin', and never 'lead author' (the order is random). Do not say they built ChatGPT. The Beatles fact rests on secondary sources, so drop it if no better source is found. Do not mention reported 2026 job moves (the NVIDIA acquihire is unconfirmed). Name cards only, no faces.

ideas.title: 5 दिन में 10 लाख users: ChatGPT की असली कहानी
ideas.hook: 30 नवंबर 2022 — एक 'free research preview' लॉन्च हुआ। 5 दिन में 10 लाख लोग। और आज भारत उसका दूसरा सबसे बड़ा देश है।
ideas.angle: The prequel is GPT-3 (2020, 175B parameters, used mostly by developers). Then ChatGPT put that kind of model in a simple chat box. The growth numbers are presented carefully, separating estimates from official figures and monthly from weekly users. India is now the #2 market with the most student users.
beats: (0–3s) Hook line. SHOW: date card '30 Nov 2022'; a counter starts ticking.

Prequel: मई 2020 — GPT-3, 175 billion parameters, यानी model के अंदर करीब 17,500 करोड़ 'knobs' जो training में सेट होते हैं। ताकतवर था, पर ज़्यादातर developers के लिए। SHOW: a grid of tiny knobs zooming out to a huge field.
ChatGPT ने इसे एक simple chat box बना दिया — free research preview। 5 दिन में 10 लाख users — Sam Altman ने खुद बताया। SHOW: generic chat UI (no logo); counter hits 1,000,000.
UBS के अनुमान से जनवरी 2023 तक करीब 10 करोड़ monthly users — TikTok को 9 महीने लगे थे, Instagram को ढाई साल। SHOW: bar race with an 'अनुमान' tag on the ChatGPT bar.
अक्टूबर 2025: OpenAI के मुताबिक हर हफ्ते 80 करोड़ लोग। SHOW: 3D globe dots brighten worldwide.

और India? फरवरी 2026 में Altman ने बताया — भारत में हर हफ्ते 10 करोड़ से ज़्यादा users, US के बाद दूसरा सबसे बड़ा देश, और students सबसे ज़्यादा यहीं से। GPT-3 paper के 31 लेखकों में पुणे में जन्मे प्रफुल्ल धारीवाल भी थे, जिन्होंने बाद में GPT-4o lead किया। SHOW: India lights up orange on the globe with '100M+ weekly'; name card.
तुम ChatGPT सबसे ज़्यादा किस काम में use करते हो — पढ़ाई, coding या कुछ और? Comment करो। SHOW: 3-option poll card.
ideas.india_angle: India passed 100 million weekly ChatGPT users and is its second-largest market after the US, with the largest number of student users (Altman, February 2026). Pune-born Prafulla Dhariwal is one of the 31 GPT-3 co-authors and later led GPT-4o.

visuals.two_d: Date card. Knob-grid metaphor for parameters. Generic chat box (no brand logos). Counters for 1M and 100M (with an 'अनुमान' tag). App-growth bar race. Name card for Dhariwal (no photo). Poll CTA.
visuals.three_d: Globe data scene: dots for users brighten; the US and India get highlighted rings, with India labelled '100M+ weekly (Feb 2026)'. An optional rising-line chart of official weekly figures: 100M (2023) → 500M (Mar 2025) → 800M (Oct 2025) → 900M (Feb 2026).
ai_clips: (1 clip, 5s) A night-time Indian hostel room: a student's hands (no face) typing on a laptop, the screen glowing with a generic chat interface, chai cup and notebooks on the desk, warm desk-lamp light.

key_facts.claim: GPT-3 paper 'Language Models are Few-Shot Learners' was posted 28 May 2020. 175 billion parameters, 31 authors led by Tom B. Brown, including Prafulla Dhariwal.
ChatGPT launched on 30 November 2022 as a free research preview (GPT-3.5).
ChatGPT crossed one million users five days after launch, per Sam Altman's post.
UBS (using Similarweb data) estimated ChatGPT reached ~100 million monthly active users by end-January 2023. TikTok took 9 months and Instagram 2.5 years to reach the same.
At DevDay on 6 Oct 2025 Altman said more than 800 million people use ChatGPT every week.
India has 100 million weekly ChatGPT users, its second-largest market after the US, with the largest number of student users (Altman, Feb 2026).
Pune-born Prafulla Dhariwal led OpenAI's Omni team behind GPT-4o. Altman credited his vision in May 2024.

ideas.virality_reason: Huge, relatable numbers, plus the national-pride stat that India is #2, plus a comment-bait poll. Students see themselves in the story.
ideas.risk_notes: Clearly separate monthly from weekly users, and estimates from official figures. Do not say '1 billion weekly' (unconfirmed; OpenAI's July 2026 '>1B active users' covers all products). Avoid ChatGPT and OpenAI logos; use a generic UI. The 'fastest-growing app' title was later challenged (Threads), so say 'उस वक्त'. Re-check user numbers on publish day.

ideas.title: 50 साल की पहेली, AI ने सुलझाई — फिर मिला Nobel
ideas.hook: एक protein का आकार पता करने में कभी सालों लग जाते थे। फिर एक AI आया — और 2024 में उसके बनाने वालों को Nobel मिला।
ideas.angle: Protein folding explained with a lock-and-key analogy. AlphaFold2 at CASP14 in 2020 drew praise from Indian-born Nobel laureate Venki Ramakrishnan. The free database is now used by 3M+ researchers, including Indian labs. October 2024 brought two Nobel prizes in two days with AI behind both.
beats: (0–3s) Hook line. SHOW: a bead-chain line drawing folds itself into a 3D-ish shape.

Protein = amino acids की माला जो मुड़कर एक 3D shape बनाती है। Shape ही तय करता है काम — जैसे चाबी का आकार तय करता है कौन सा ताला खुलेगा। SHOW: lock-and-key animation; the wrong shape fails, the right shape clicks.

ये shape बताना biology की 50 साल पुरानी पहेली थी। 30 नवंबर 2020: DeepMind के AlphaFold2 ने CASP14 competition में कई proteins का shape lab experiments जितनी accuracy के करीब बता दिया। SHOW: accuracy meter jumps; '50 साल' badge.

भारत में जन्मे Nobel laureate वेंकी रामकृष्णन — तब UK की Royal Society के president — ने इसे 'stunning advance' कहा, 50 साल पुरानी grand challenge पर। SHOW: quote card with an India pin at Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu.

फिर करीब 20 करोड़ predicted structures का free database — 190 से ज़्यादा देशों के 30 लाख से ज़्यादा researchers ने use किया। भारत में BITS के scientists ने soybean breeding research में भी। SHOW: 3D rotating protein ribbon; globe dots; India dot highlighted.

8 अक्टूबर 2024: Physics Nobel — Hopfield और Hinton, neural networks के लिए। 9 अक्टूबर 2024: Chemistry Nobel — David Baker, और AlphaFold के लिए Demis Hassabis व John Jumper। दो दिन, दो Nobel — दोनों के पीछे AI। SHOW: two generic medal cards with dates.
अगली बार कोई कहे 'AI बस chatbot है' — ये reel भेज देना। SHOW: CTA.
ideas.india_angle: Venki Ramakrishnan was born in Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu, won the 2009 Chemistry Nobel for ribosome structure, and as Royal Society president publicly hailed AlphaFold. DeepMind's Asia-Pacific report lists Indian researchers (BITS) using AlphaFold for soybean breeding work.

visuals.two_d: Bead-chain folding animation. Lock-and-key analogy. Accuracy meter. Quote card. Two generic Nobel-style medal cards (not official imagery) dated 8 Oct and 9 Oct 2024. Phrase captions: 'protein folding', 'structure = function'.
visuals.three_d: Code-rendered rotating 3D protein ribbon (from public PDB/AlphaFold DB coordinates in three.js), then a globe with dots for 190+ countries and India highlighted.
ai_clips: (1 clip, 5s) A cinematic microscopic fly-through inside a cell: a glowing chain of beads twists and folds into a compact 3D protein shape, soft bioluminescent colours. No humans.

key_facts.claim: AlphaFold's CASP14 result was announced 30 Nov 2020. Venki Ramakrishnan called it 'a stunning advance on the protein-folding problem, a 50-year-old grand challenge in biology', decades earlier than many expected.
AlphaFold determined the shape of around two-thirds of CASP14 proteins with accuracy comparable to laboratory experiments.
Venki Ramakrishnan was born in Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu, shared the 2009 Chemistry Nobel for ribosome work, and served as Royal Society president (2015–2020).
The 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry: half to David Baker (computational protein design), half jointly to Demis Hassabis and John Jumper (protein structure prediction).
On 8 Oct 2024 the Physics Nobel went to John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton 'for foundational discoveries and inventions that enable machine learning with artificial neural networks'.
The AlphaFold Protein Database has been used by more than 3 million researchers in over 190 countries.
Indian researchers at BITS used AlphaFold in soybean breeding work (DeepMind Asia-Pacific report).
The AlphaFold database houses more than 200 million predicted structures and remains available after DeepMind's 2026 team reorganisation.

ideas.virality_reason: 'AI won a Nobel' surprises people who think AI is only chatbots. The Indian-born Nobel laureate's endorsement and the lock-and-key analogy make it easy to explain to parents and teachers.
ideas.risk_notes: Do not claim AlphaFold 'solved biology'. Some proteins and complexes remain hard. If you add the July 2026 news (team reassigned, Jumper to Anthropic), say 'team reorganise हुई, database चालू है'; never 'AlphaFold बंद'. Do not say AI won a 2026 Nobel (it did not). Use generic medal art, not official Nobel imagery. No faces of the laureates.

ideas.title: Math Olympiad: AI को gold, पर भारत के कनव के 37 नंबर
ideas.hook: 2025 में AI ने दुनिया का सबसे कठिन school math exam दिया और gold वाले नंबर लाया — 35 में 42… नहीं, 42 में 35। उसी साल दिल्ली के एक लड़के ने 37 लाए।
ideas.angle: An AI milestone in 2025–26: AI reached gold-level at the International Math Olympiad (35/42, officially graded for Gemini Deep Think), and in 2026 companies claimed perfect scores. It sits alongside India's record 2025 team, whose top scorer beat the AI's mark. The lesson is that AI is a practice partner, not a reason to stop learning.
beats: (0–3s) Hook line (the deliberate self-correction '35 में 42… नहीं, 42 में 35' acts as a pattern-interrupt). SHOW: exam card 'IMO 2025'; '35/42' stamps in with a gold line.
IMO यानी International Mathematical Olympiad — school students का सबसे कठिन math competition। 6 सवाल, 42 नंबर; 2025 में gold की cutoff — 35। SHOW: 6 boxes × 7 points; the cutoff line at 35.

Google DeepMind का advanced Gemini Deep Think — 35/42, IMO के graders ने officially check किया: gold-level। OpenAI ने भी 35 का दावा किया, पर वो officially entered नहीं था। SHOW: abstract AI icon with an 'IMO certified ✓' badge vs a 'self-reported' tag.

और भारत? 3 gold, 2 silver, 1 bronze — 7th rank — अब तक का सबसे ज़्यादा team score: 252 में 193। सबसे ऊपर दिल्ली के कनव तलवार — 37 नंबर। SHOW: bars AI 35 vs Kanav 37, Aarav 35, Adhitya 35; medal icons.
पर रफ़्तार देखो: 2026 के Shanghai IMO के बाद दो Chinese कंपनियों ने दावा किया कि उनके AI ने 42/42 लाए — एक साल में 35 से 42। SHOW: 3D arc Australia → Shanghai; '42/42 (कंपनी का दावा)' card.
तो क्या math पढ़ना बेकार? बिल्कुल नहीं — 2026 में भी भारत ने 2 gold, 4 silver जीते। सही: AI को practice partner बनाओ। गलत: सोचने का काम पूरा AI को सौंप देना। SHOW: Sahi/Galat cards.
ये reel उस दोस्त को भेजो जो olympiad या JEE की तैयारी कर रहा है। SHOW: CTA.
ideas.india_angle: India's IMO 2025 team won 3 gold, 2 silver and 1 bronze, ranked 7th and set its highest-ever score of 193/252. Kanav Talwar (Delhi) scored 37, above the 35 the AI systems achieved. India also won 2 gold and 4 silver at IMO 2026.

visuals.two_d: Exam-paper card. 6×7 point grid with a gold cutoff line. AI badge 'certified' vs 'self-reported'. Score bar comparison. Medal-tally icons. Sahi/Galat cards. Students appear only as text name cards (no faces).
visuals.three_d: Globe arc from Sunshine Coast, Australia (2025) to Shanghai (2026), with 3D score columns rising at each pin: 35 (AI 2025), 37 (Kanav), 42 (company-claimed AI 2026).

key_facts.claim: At IMO 2025, an advanced Gemini Deep Think solved 5 of 6 problems for 35/42, the gold cutoff. IMO coordinators graded and confirmed it. Google announced on 21 July 2025.
OpenAI announced a 35/42 result on 19 July 2025, but its model was not officially entered, so the score is not IMO-certified.
Official IMO 2025 India results: Kanav Talwar 37 (gold, rank 9), Aarav Gupta 35 (gold), Adhitya Mangudy Venkata Ganesh 35 (gold). Team total 193/252.
India ranked 7th at IMO 2025 with 3 gold, 2 silver, 1 bronze and its highest-ever score of 193.
After IMO 2026 in Shanghai, Huawei and Xiaohongshu said their AI models scored 100% (42/42). In 2025 AI models had reached gold level but not matched the five perfect-scoring humans.
At IMO 2026, India won 2 gold and 4 silver medals.

ideas.virality_reason: A 'kid vs AI' comparison with a real Indian name and a true number (37 > 35), plus fast-moving 2026 news (42/42) and exam-season relevance (JEE/olympiad aspirants).
ideas.risk_notes: These are minors, so use only their officially published names and scores, generate no faces and add no personal details. Do not frame it as a head-to-head match (the AI attempted the problems separately); say 'नंबरों में'. Mark the 2026 AI 42/42 results as company claims. If the self-correcting hook feels confusing in testing, use the plain version: 'AI ने 42 में से 35 लाए — दिल्ली के कनव ने 37।'

research_unverified.pillar: AI का ABC: GenAI के शब्द आसान भाषा में (AI ka ABC, GenAI terms explained simply)
research_unverified.landscape_notes:
STATE OF THE FIELD AS OF 2026-10-09, as it matters for an Indian "AI ka ABC" reel series.
(Research method: WebFetch was blocked by the proxy for openai.com, arxiv.org, sarvam.ai, pib.gov.in, huggingface.co and artificialanalysis.ai. I read arXiv papers in full text through the Hugging Face Papers mirror (huggingface.co/papers/<id>) and read model cards through the Hugging Face hub. Facts from openai.com, sarvam.ai and pib.gov.in come from search-result summaries of those exact pages and are marked as such below.)

1) TOKENS AND THE "HINDI TAX" (strongest evergreen India hook in this pillar)
- Petrov et al., Oxford, NeurIPS 2023 (https://huggingface.co/papers/2305.15425; also https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/hash/74bb24dca8334adce292883b4b651eda-Abstract.html). They ran the same 2,000 FLORES-200 sentences through each tokenizer. With cl100k_base, the ChatGPT/GPT-4 tokenizer, the ratio to English is: Hindi 4.79x, Marathi 5.07x, Bengali 5.84x, Assamese 6.20x, Gujarati 7.69x, Kannada 8.90x, Malayalam 9.00x, Odia 12.48x. These figures are from the appendix table, which I read myself. The paper says this gap means higher cost, slower responses (latency), and less text fitting in the context window. Even MuRIL, a tokenizer built for Indian languages, still treats English most efficiently.
- Newer tokenizers have narrowed the gap but not closed it. OpenAI's GPT-4o launch post (13 May 2024, https://openai.com/index/hello-gpt-4o/, seen via search summary) gives these sample counts: Hindi 90 to 31 tokens (2.9x fewer), Gujarati 145 to 33 (4.4x), Telugu 159 to 45 (3.5x). Each of those is one sample sentence, not a corpus average.
- Sarvam-1 blog (https://sarvam.ai/blogs/sarvam-1, Oct 2024, seen via search summary): many multilingual models need 4 to 8 tokens per word in Indian languages, against about 1.4 for English. Sarvam says its own tokenizer needs 1.4 to 2.1. These are vendor claims.
- Production tip: show live counts on screen using OpenAI's tokenizer tool when recording, rather than quoting a current ratio from memory.

2) INDIAN MODELS (2025-26)
- Sarvam-105B model card (https://huggingface.co/sarvamai/sarvam-105b, released March 2026): mixture-of-experts (MoE) design with 10.3B active parameters per token, top-8 routing over 128 experts, 128K context, Apache license, state-of-the-art across 22 Indian languages "for its size" (Sarvam's own claim).
- TechCrunch, 18 Feb 2026 (https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/18/indian-ai-lab-sarvams-new-models-are-a-major-bet-on-the-viability-of-open-source-ai/): Sarvam's 30B and 105B models were unveiled at the India AI Impact Summit. They were trained from scratch, not fine-tuned, on IndiaAI Mission compute, with Yotta providing infrastructure and Nvidia technical support.
- Sarvam later became a unicorn after a $234M round led by HCLTech (https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/15/sarvam-becomes-indias-newest-ai-unicorn-with-234-million-funding-round-led-by-hcltech/).
- Sarvam-M (https://huggingface.co/sarvamai/sarvam-m, May 2025) is a fine-tune of Mistral-Small-3.1-24B. Post-training used SFT plus RL with verifiable rewards. Sarvam reports +20% on Indian-language benchmarks. Its docs (https://docs.sarvam.ai/api-reference-docs/getting-started/models/sarvam-m) describe a Wikipedia lookup feature. A "5% to 72% SimpleQA" figure circulates online, but I could not find it in a primary source, so do not use it.
- BharatGen Param2 is a 17B MoE model covering 22 languages, launched at the Feb 2026 summit (https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/bharatgen-to-launch-17-billion-parameter-multilingual-ai-model-at-india-ai-impact-summit-515923-2026-02-12). Param-1 2.9B paper: https://huggingface.co/papers/2507.13390.
- Framing rule: present these as real milestones, not as "India's ChatGPT beat everyone". Sarvam-105B scores only modestly on independent indices such as Artificial Analysis.

3) COMPUTE AND GPUs
- PIB release "12 Companies Developing Foundation Models Using 38,000 GPUs at ₹65/Hour" (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2177598, Oct 2025, seen via search summary).
- MeitY statement, 25 Mar 2026: more than 38,000 GPUs onboarded (https://telecomtalk.info/?p=1005751). In Feb 2026 the government said another 20,000 GPUs would be added "in coming weeks". I found no confirmation that this happened.
- Nvidia became the first company worth $5 trillion on 29 Oct 2025 (https://www.forbes.com.au/news/investing/nvidia-becomes-first-company-worth-5-trillion/).
- AlexNet (2012) won ImageNet with a 15.3% top-5 error against 26.2% for the runner-up. It was trained on two GTX 580 gaming GPUs (paper: https://cvml.ista.ac.at/courses/DLWT_W17/material/AlexNet.pdf).
- DeepSeek-V3 technical report (https://huggingface.co/papers/2412.19437): 671B total parameters, 37B active; 14.8T training tokens; 2.788M H800 GPU-hours on 2,048 H800s. The headline $5.576M assumes a $2/hour rental price and, in the report's own words, excludes "prior research and ablation experiments".

4) HALLUCINATION
- OpenAI paper "Why Language Models Hallucinate" (4 Sep 2025, https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.04664). Its argument is that models are graded like exams where guessing beats saying "I don't know". The paper names Indian JEE, NEET and GATE as exams that penalise wrong answers, and proposes the same kind of penalty for AI benchmarks.
- OpenAI's companion blog (https://openai.com/index/why-language-models-hallucinate/, seen via summary) gives SimpleQA results: gpt-5-thinking-mini abstained 52%, was accurate 22% and wrong 26%; o4-mini abstained 1%, was accurate 24% and wrong 75%.
- India case: on 27 Feb 2026 the Supreme Court took suo motu notice of an Andhra Pradesh trial-court order that relied on four non-existent AI-generated judgments, and called such reliance misconduct (https://www.business-standard.com/india-news/sc-flags-serious-concern-over-trial-court-citing-ai-generated-cases-126030201055_1.html; https://www.scconline.com/blog/post/2026/03/11/sc-raises-concern-use-ai-generated-fake-precedents/). On 5 May 2026 it asked the Bar Council of India to form an expert panel (https://www.livelaw.in/top-stories/use-of-ai-generated-fake-judgments-supreme-court-urges-bci-to-form-expert-panel-to-examine-issue-533023).

5) AGENTS AND MCP
- Agentic payments pilot announced 9 Oct 2025 by NPCI, Razorpay and OpenAI, with UPI inside ChatGPT. Users pre-authorise an agent within spending limits. Banks: Axis and Airtel Payments Bank; BigBasket was an early merchant (https://www.onmanorama.com/news/business/2025/10/09/npci-razorpay-openai-chatgpt-payments.html).
- Reuters reported on 1 Sep 2026 that NPCI would unveil a "Unified Agent Protocol" at Global Fintech Fest 2026. I found no confirmation that it was launched, so treat it as unconfirmed.
- MCP: Anthropic introduced it on 25 Nov 2024 and donated it to the Linux Foundation's new Agentic AI Foundation on 9 Dec 2025, co-founded with OpenAI and Block. Anthropic reports more than 10,000 active public MCP servers, and adoption by ChatGPT, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Cursor and VS Code (https://www.anthropic.com/news/donating-the-model-context-protocol-and-establishing-of-the-agentic-ai-foundation).
- Indian MCP example: Zerodha's Kite MCP launched 20 May 2025 (https://nithinkamath.substack.com/p/connect-your-zerodha-account-to-ai; https://tradingqna.com/t/introducing-kite-mcp-connect-your-kite-account-to-ai-assistants/181830). In beta, order placement was not available.
- Hype check from Gartner (June 2025): more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be scrapped by 2027. On "agent washing", Gartner says only about 130 of thousands of "agentic" vendors are genuine (https://www.outlookbusiness.com/artificial-intelligence/over-40-of-agentic-ai-projects-will-be-scrapped-by-2027-says-gartner).

6) USAGE IN INDIA
- Sam Altman said on 15 Feb 2026 that India has 100M weekly ChatGPT users, the second-largest market, and the largest student user base (https://www.techcrunch.com/2026/02/15/india-has-100m-weekly-active-chatgpt-users-sam-altman-says/).
- ChatGPT Go was made free for a year in India (https://storyboard18.com/digital/india-now-has-100-million-weekly-chatgpt-users-says-sam-altman-89705.htm).
- Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image): a Google DeepMind lead said India was the No. 1 country by usage during the Sept 2025 retro-saree trend (https://techcrunch.com/2025/09/17/india-leads-the-way-on-googles-nano-banana-with-a-local-creative-twist). Outputs carry the SynthID watermark. Google has not disclosed whether it is a diffusion model, so do not say it is.

7) EVERGREEN ANCHORS
- AI term: Dartmouth proposal dated 31 Aug 1955, for the 1956 workshop (https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/aimagazine/article/view/1904).
- "Machine learning" term: Arthur Samuel, 1959. His checkers program learned to beat its own author (https://people.csail.mit.edu/brooks/idocs/Samuel.pdf).
- Transformer paper, 12 Jun 2017, 8 authors listed in random order (https://huggingface.co/papers/1706.03762). Base model trained in 12 hours on 8 P100 GPUs; the "big" model has 213M parameters.
- Co-authors with an Indian education: Ashish Vaswani (BIT Mesra) and Niki Parmar (Pune Institute of Computer Technology). These are secondary sources: https://officechai.com/stories/the-indian-researchers-whose-work-led-to-the-creation-of-chatgpt and https://www.analyticsinsight.net/people/indians-leading-ai-revolution-niki-parmar-co-founder-essential-ai-adept-ai-labs-technical-staff-anthropic.
- GPT-3: 175B parameters (https://huggingface.co/papers/2005.14165).
- InstructGPT/RLHF: a 1.3B model was preferred over 175B GPT-3 despite having 100x fewer parameters (https://huggingface.co/papers/2203.02155).
- RAG: Lewis et al. 2020, Facebook AI Research, UCL and NYU (https://huggingface.co/papers/2005.11401).
- Lost in the Middle (https://huggingface.co/papers/2307.03172): models use information best when it sits at the start or end of a long context.
- Gemini 1.5 (15 Feb 2024): 1M tokens, roughly 1 hour of video, 11 hours of audio, 30k lines of code, or more than 700k words (https://blog.google/technology/ai/google-gemini-next-generation-model-february-2024/).
- Diffusion: DDPM 2020 (https://huggingface.co/papers/2006.11239); latent diffusion / Stable Diffusion family 2022 (https://huggingface.co/papers/2112.10752). OpenAI calls Sora "a diffusion model", specifically a diffusion transformer working on spacetime patches (https://openai.com/index/video-generation-models-as-world-simulators/).
- Open-weight vs open source: gpt-oss-120b, 5 Aug 2025, Apache 2.0, about 117B total / 5.1B active parameters; weights released, training data not (https://docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/reference/openai-gpt-oss-120b). OSI's Open Source AI Definition 1.0 (Oct 2024) requires training-data information plus full code; Llama does not qualify (https://the-decoder.com/open-source-initiative-releases-first-formal-definition-of-open-source-ai/).
- AGI definitions: OpenAI charter, "highly autonomous systems that outperform humans at most economically valuable work" (https://openai.com/charter/). DeepMind's "Levels of AGI" (Nov 2023) put ChatGPT, Bard and Llama 2 at Level 1 "Emerging AGI", and said "Competent AGI" had not yet been achieved (https://huggingface.co/papers/2311.02462; https://the-decoder.com/chatgpt-is-an-emerging-agi-according-to-google-deepmind/). Under the Microsoft-OpenAI deal of Oct 2025, any OpenAI declaration of AGI must be verified by an independent expert panel (https://openai.com/index/next-chapter-of-microsoft-openai-partnership/).
- UPI fraud detection as an everyday ML example: NPCI gives banks AI/ML risk-scoring models, per a Lok Sabha reply of 15 Dec 2025 (https://eparlib.sansad.in/bitstream/123456789/3018042/1/AU2481_5bIzKk.pdf).

BACKUP IDEA, NOT IN THE 12: a standalone GPU/TPU reel, "Nvidia दुनिया की सबसे महंगी कंपनी कैसे बनी?" It would use the AlexNet gaming-GPU story, the CPU-professor vs GPU-classroom analogy, Nvidia's $5T milestone (29 Oct 2025), and IndiaAI's 38k GPUs at ₹65/hr plus 1,050 Google Trillium TPUs in its third tender. The TPU figure is secondary (https://inc42.com/buzz/indiaai-to-add-over-3800-gpus-via-third-tender-report).

AI-CLIP BUDGET FOR THIS PILLAR: about 6 Kling clips (about 45 credits) across 12 reels, none showing real people's faces.

ideas.title: AI, ML, Deep Learning, GenAI — असली फर्क
ideas.hook: ChatGPT AI है... लेकिन हर AI, ChatGPT नहीं होता।
ideas.angle: चार शब्द जो सब एक जैसे बोलते हैं, असल में एक के अंदर एक रखे टिफिन के डिब्बे हैं: AI ⊃ ML ⊃ Deep Learning ⊃ GenAI. Twist यह है कि तुम्हारा UPI fraud alert भी ML है, पर वो GenAI नहीं है। आखिर में 'AGI' का डिब्बा dotted line में दिखता है, जिसे अभी तक कोई भर नहीं पाया।
beats: HOOK (0-3s). Say: 'ChatGPT AI है... लेकिन हर AI, ChatGPT नहीं होता। ये 4 डिब्बे समझ लो।' Show: 4 nested टिफिन डिब्बे pop-in होते हैं, orange outline में।

AI, सबसे बड़ा डिब्बा (3-13s). Say: 'AI यानी मशीन से समझदारी वाला काम करवाना। ये शब्द 1955 के एक proposal में आया, और 1956 में Dartmouth में इस पर पहली बड़ी बैठक हुई।' Show: डिब्बे पर '1956' का stamp, rule-book वाला robot icon।

ML, दूसरा डिब्बा (13-25s). Say: 'Machine Learning यानी rules रटाने की जगह examples से सीखना। 1959 में Arthur Samuel का checkers program अपने ही बनाने वाले को हराना सीख गया। और याद रखना, तुम्हारे UPI में fraud पकड़ने वाले risk score भी NPCI के AI/ML models से आते हैं।' Show: checkers board, फिर UPI-style generic phone screen पर 'risk score' meter।

DEEP LEARNING (25-37s). Say: 'Deep Learning यानी ML जो कई परतों वाले neural network से सीखता है। 2012 में AlexNet ने photo पहचानने में गलती 26% से घटाकर करीब 15% कर दी, और वो भी दो gaming GPUs पर train होकर।' Show: layered network की परतें drawn lines से जुड़ती हैं, साथ में error bar 26.2 → 15.3।

GENAI (37-48s). Say: 'GenAI यानी Deep Learning जो कुछ नया बनाता है: text, photo, आवाज़। 30 नवंबर 2022 को ChatGPT आया, और आज भारत में हर हफ्ते करीब 10 करोड़ लोग इसे इस्तेमाल करते हैं।' Show: सबसे छोटा डिब्बा glow करता है, फिर India counter '100M weekly' दिखता है।

PAYOFF + CTA (48-58s). Say: 'तो हर GenAI, AI है... पर हर AI, GenAI नहीं। और AGI? उस डिब्बे का साइज़ अभी कोई तय नहीं कर पाया। अगली reel में। Save कर लो, और अगली बार कोई "AI" बोले तो पूछना: कौन सा डिब्बा?' Show: dotted 'AGI?' डिब्बा wobble करता है, checkbox 'Saved' tick होता है।
ideas.india_angle: रोज़ का ML उदाहरण UPI fraud detection है: सरकार ने लोकसभा में बताया कि NPCI बैंकों को AI/ML-based risk scoring देता है। साथ में भारत का GenAI scale दिखाओ: करीब 10 करोड़ weekly ChatGPT users, और Altman के मुताबिक भारत दूसरा सबसे बड़ा market है।

visuals.two_d: Cream background पर orange line-art में टिफिन के 4 डिब्बे, जो एक के अंदर एक खुलते हैं। हर डिब्बे पर साल का stamp: 1956, 1959, 2012, 2022। नीचे एक timeline ribbon चलता है। ML वाले हिस्से में checkers board पर एक-एक चाल drawn होती है। DL वाले हिस्से में 3-4 परतों का network line-draw होता है और 26.2 → 15.3 वाला bar animate होता है। GenAI पर एक chat bubble pop होता है। आखिर में dotted 'AGI?' डिब्बा। Captions phrase-by-phrase आते हैं।
visuals.three_d: Opening में 4 translucent nested cubes (matryoshka जैसे) धीरे-धीरे घूमते हैं और camera सबसे अंदर वाले cube तक जाता है (three.js → ffmpeg)। Optional: AlexNet error drop का 3D bar।

key_facts.claim: 'Artificial intelligence' शब्द 31 Aug 1955 के Dartmouth proposal (McCarthy, Minsky, Rochester, Shannon) से आया, जो 1956 के summer workshop के लिए था
Arthur Samuel ने 1959 के IBM paper में 'machine learning' शब्द इस्तेमाल किया; उनका checkers program अपने programmer से बेहतर खेलना सीख गया
AlexNet (2012): ImageNet top-5 error 15.3% (runner-up 26.2%), दो NVIDIA GTX 580 GPUs पर 5-6 दिन train हुआ
NPCI सभी बैंकों को AI/ML-based fraud monitoring देता है, जो alerts generate करता है और संदिग्ध transactions decline करता है
ChatGPT 30 Nov 2022 को launch हुआ
भारत में करीब 10 करोड़ (100M) weekly ChatGPT users; भारत OpenAI का दूसरा सबसे बड़ा market (Sam Altman)

ideas.virality_reason: हर कोई ये चारों शब्द मिलाकर बोलता है, इसलिए एक ही reel में confusion साफ हो जाता है और लोग इसे save करते हैं। टिफिन वाली analogy याद रहती है, और UPI वाला twist हर Indian user को अपनी बात लगता है।
ideas.risk_notes: 'McCarthy ने 1956 में शब्द बनाया' मत बोलो; proposal 1955 का है। Samuel के नाम से घूमने वाली 'learn without being explicitly programmed' quote मत डालो, वो 1959 के paper में नहीं है। Face Unlock जैसे किसी app को किसी डिब्बे में बिना source मत डालो। 100M users OpenAI का self-reported आंकड़ा है, इसलिए 'Altman के मुताबिक' बोलो।

ideas.title: ChatGPT कैसे बना? 'अगला शब्द' + इंसानी ट्यूशन
ideas.hook: ChatGPT की पढ़ाई एक बच्चों वाले खेल से शुरू हुई: 'अगला शब्द बताओ'।
ideas.angle: LLM यानी Large Language Model, जो पहले बहुत सारा text पढ़कर अगला शब्द (token) guess करना सीखता है। Twist: सिर्फ बड़ा होने से कोई model अच्छा assistant नहीं बनता। इंसानों की feedback से tuning (RLHF) होने के बाद 1.3B वाला model 175B वाले GPT-3 से ज़्यादा पसंद किया गया।
beats: HOOK (0-3s). Say: 'ChatGPT की पढ़ाई एक बच्चों वाले खेल से शुरू हुई: अगला शब्द बताओ।' Show: 'मेरा भारत ___' card और उसके नीचे 3 options के bars (on-screen label: 'उदाहरण')।

LLM क्या है (3-15s). Say: 'LLM यानी Large Language Model। GPT का पूरा नाम है Generative Pre-trained Transformer। 2018 के पहले GPT को सिखाया गया कि text में अगला शब्द क्या आएगा। समझो phone के keyboard वाला autocomplete, बस steroids पर।' Show: phone keyboard की suggestion bar फूलकर 'LLM' बन जाती है।

LARGE यानी parameters (15-25s). Say: 'Large यानी अरबों parameters, यानी अंदर के knobs जो पढ़ाई के दौरान सेट होते हैं। 2020 के GPT-3 में 175 अरब थे।' Show: knobs की grid zoom-out होकर galaxy जैसी बन जाती है, counter '175,000,000,000' पर रुकता है।

TWIST (25-35s). Say: 'लेकिन ध्यान से सुनो। OpenAI के अपने paper की पहली line है: model को बड़ा करने से वो तुम्हारी बात मानने में अपने-आप बेहतर नहीं होता। सिर्फ अगला शब्द guess करने वाला model झूठ भी बोल सकता है, बदतमीज़ी भी कर सकता है, बेकार जवाब भी दे सकता है।' Show: robot के ऊपर 3 red cross वाले checkboxes।

RLHF यानी इंसानी ट्यूशन (35-47s). Say: 'इसका इलाज है RLHF, यानी इंसानी feedback से सीखना। पहले लोग अच्छे जवाब लिखकर दिखाते हैं, फिर model के कई जवाबों को best से worst तक rank करते हैं। जैसे ट्यूशन वाली टीचर की red pen।' Show: A/B/C answer cards, ranking arrows, और ✔ tick।

PROOF + INDIA (47-58s). Say: 'नतीजा? 1.3 अरब वाला InstructGPT लोगों को 175 अरब वाले GPT-3 से ज़्यादा पसंद आया, जबकि उसके parameters 100 गुना कम थे। भारत का Sarvam-M भी इसी तरह post-training से तैयार हुआ: Mistral Small पर fine-tuning और reinforcement learning।' Show: छोटा orange ball और बड़ा grey sphere, छोटे ball पर '👍 जीता' का label।
