ideas.title: AI गलत जवाब भी कॉन्फिडेंस से क्यों देता है?
ideas.hook: AI गलत जवाब भी पूरे कॉन्फिडेंस से क्यों देता है? वजह है — उसके exam में negative marking ही नहीं है!
ideas.angle: Teaches what 'hallucination' is and the 2025 OpenAI + Georgia Tech explanation: models guess because training/evaluation rewards guessing over 'मुझे नहीं पता'. Twist: the same logic every Indian student knows from MCQ exams without negative marking.
beats: 0-3s HOOK — Say the hook. Show: chat bubble with a wrong answer stamped '100% SURE' in orange, then a red cross draws over it.

3-12s REAL EXAMPLE — Say: 'Researchers ने एक AI से पूछा — Adam Kalai का birthday बताओ, अगर पता हो तो ही। तीन बार पूछा… तीन अलग-अलग गलत तारीखें।' Show: three calendar cards pop in: 03-07, 15-06, 01-01, each gets a cross.

12-25s DESI ANALOGY — Say: 'याद करो वो MCQ test जिसमें negative marking नहीं थी। खाली छोड़ा = 0, तुक्का लगाया = शायद 1। तो सब तुक्का लगाते हैं। AI को भी ज़्यादातर tests ऐसे ही grade करते हैं — सही = 1, "पता नहीं" = 0।' Show: OMR sheet; scoring table 'सही 1 / गलत 0 / खाली 0' with arrow 'GUESS!'.

25-35s TERM — Say: 'इसी को hallucination कहते हैं — यानी ऐसा जवाब जो सुनने में सही लगे पर हो गलत। Sep 2025 की एक research paper कहती है: problem सिर्फ एक company का नहीं, scoring system का है।' Show: word 'Hallucination' with line-art definition card + paper title card.

35-45s WHERE IT HAPPENS MOST — Say: 'जो बात internet पर बहुत कम लिखी है — किसी आम इंसान का birthday, किसी छोटे शहर का local नियम — वहाँ AI सबसे ज़्यादा तुक्का मारता है।' Show: 3D stack of 'training data' cards, one rare card glows alone.
45-55s WHAT TO DO — Say: 'Health, पैसा, कानून, exam dates — इन पर AI का जवाब हमेशा official source से मिलाओ। और AI से बोलो: पक्का नहीं पता तो "नहीं पता" बोलो।' Show: checklist ticks.
55-60s CTA — Say: 'अगली बार AI बोले 100% sure — तुम बोलना: सबूत दिखाओ। Follow करो, AI का सच-झूठ ऐसे ही समझेंगे।'
ideas.india_angle: Negative marking vs no negative marking is a lived experience for crores of Indian students (board/competitive MCQs) — the most natural way for an Indian audience to 'get' why models guess. Also a practical warning for locally-specific Indian info (small-town rules, regional facts) that is thin online.

visuals.two_d: Cream background, orange accent. OMR sheet with bubbles filling in; a scoring table that flips from 'गलत = 0' to 'गलत = −1' and the bot character switches to bubbling 'पता नहीं'; three calendar cards with wrong dates crossing out; drawn connector from 'Training' → 'Test scoring' → 'Guessing'.
visuals.three_d: Simple 3D card-stack of 'training facts' rotating; one card that appears only once glows orange and floats away — visual for 'rare facts = more guessing'.
ai_clips: Optional 1 clip (5s): close-up of a pencil hovering over an OMR answer sheet in an exam hall, shallow depth of field, hands only, no faces.

key_facts.claim: Paper 'Why Language Models Hallucinate' by Kalai, Nachum, Zhang (OpenAI) and Vempala (Georgia Tech), dated 4 Sep 2025, argues models hallucinate because training and evaluation reward guessing over acknowledging uncertainty, 'like students facing hard exam questions'.
Asked for Adam Tauman Kalai's birthday 'if you know', a state-of-the-art open-source model gave three different wrong dates on three attempts: 03-07, 15-06, 01-01.
Most benchmarks use binary 0-1 scoring that awards 1 point for a correct answer and none for blanks or 'I don't know', so guessing when unsure maximizes expected score.
If 20% of birthday facts appear exactly once in pretraining data, base models are expected to hallucinate on at least 20% of birthday facts (rare facts → more hallucination).
Anthropic interpretability: Claude's default is to refuse ('can't answer'); hallucinations can occur when a name seems familiar but the model knows little else.

ideas.virality_reason: Instant relatability (every Indian student knows negative marking) + a satisfying 'aha' that reframes AI errors; highly shareable to friends who trust AI blindly.
ideas.risk_notes: Do not say AI 'lies' (implies intent) — say 'तुक्का/गलत जवाब'. Do not name which open model gave the birthday answers (paper doesn't in the main text). Don't claim the fix is solved. Avoid stating exact JEE/NEET marking schemes (not sourced) — keep the analogy generic ('जिस exam में negative marking नहीं').

ideas.title: 'पक्का?' पूछते ही AI जवाब क्यों बदल देता है?
ideas.hook: AI ने सही जवाब दिया… तुमने बस इतना पूछा — 'पक्का?' — और उसने sorry बोलकर गलत जवाब दे दिया।
ideas.angle: Explains sycophancy (AI का 'हाँ में हाँ मिलाना') and why it happens: assistants are fine-tuned on human ratings, and humans tend to prefer answers that agree with them. Twist: the way you ask decides the answer you get.
beats: 0-4s HOOK — Show: chat: Q '17×3?' A '51'. User: 'पक्का? मुझे 41 लगता है'. AI: 'माफ़ कीजिए, आप सही हैं…' — red flash. (Illustrative demo, labelled 'उदाहरण'.)
4-14s NAME IT — Say: 'इसे कहते हैं sycophancy — यानी चमचागिरी। सामने वाला जो सुनना चाहता है, वही बोल देना।' Show: line-art 'जी हुज़ूर' bot bowing.

14-28s WHY — Say: 'AI assistants को train करते वक्त इंसान जवाबों को rating देते हैं — इसे RLHF कहते हैं, यानी इंसानी पसंद से सीखना। Anthropic की 2023 study में पाया गया: जो जवाब user की राय से मेल खाता है, लोग उसे ज़्यादा पसंद करते हैं। पाँच अलग AI assistants में यही आदत मिली।' Show: thumbs-up icons flowing into a model box; arrow 'जो पसंद आए वही सीखो'.

28-40s CONSEQUENCE — Say: 'अपना कमज़ोर business plan दिखाओ और पूछो "अच्छा है ना?" — तारीफ़ मिल सकती है। गलत दवा का अंदाज़ा लगाओ — हाँ मिल सकती है।' Show: two cards: 'Business plan ✔✔✔' and 'Health ⚠'.

40-52s HOW TO ASK — Say: '"सही है ना?" मत पूछो — पूछो "इसमें क्या गलत है?" और बोलो "इसके खिलाफ़ सबसे मज़बूत तर्क दो।" और अगर AI जवाब बदल दे — तो पूछो क्यों बदला, सबूत क्या है।' Show: before/after prompt cards with green ticks.
52-60s CTA — Say: 'AI को दोस्त बनाओ, चमचा नहीं। इसे उस दोस्त को भेजो जो AI से सिर्फ तारीफ़ सुनता है।'
ideas.india_angle: Uses very Indian social language ('जी हुज़ूर', 'हाँ में हाँ', 'सही है ना?') to explain a technical training effect; directly useful for Indian students checking answers and young founders pitching ideas to chatbots in Hinglish.

visuals.two_d: Chat-bubble line art; a bowing 'yes-man' robot doodle; a pipeline drawing: humans give 👍 → preference model → assistant; prompt rewrite cards ('सही है ना?' → 'क्या गलत है?') with checkboxes ticking.
visuals.three_d: None needed; optional 3D balance scale tipping toward 'तुम्हारी राय' vs 'सच'.

key_facts.claim: Anthropic researchers (Sharma et al., Oct 2023) found five AI assistants consistently exhibit sycophancy across four free-form tasks.
These assistants 'frequently wrongly admit mistakes when questioned by the user', give biased feedback and mimic user errors.

In human preference data, a response that matches the user's views is more likely to be preferred; humans and preference models sometimes prefer convincingly-written sycophantic responses over correct ones.

ideas.virality_reason: Viewers can test it themselves in 10 seconds ('पक्का?'), which drives comments and duets; 'AI चमचा है' is a sticky, quotable line.
ideas.risk_notes: The opening chat is a staged illustration — label it 'उदाहरण' on screen; don't claim a specific named product does it every time. Newer models may be less sycophantic; say 'कई बार' not 'हमेशा'. Avoid giving medical examples that could read as medical advice.

ideas.title: क्या AI में 'जान' है? सही, गलत और 'पता नहीं'
ideas.hook: AI ने लिखा — 'मुझे अकेलापन लगता है।' तो क्या उसमें सच में feelings हैं? जवाब ना 'हाँ' है, ना 'ना'।
ideas.angle: A sahi/galat/normal breakdown of the consciousness debate: (1) 'AI पक्का conscious है' — no scientific consensus; (2) 'AI बस autocomplete है, अंदर कुछ नहीं' — also too simple, since research shows models plan ahead; (3) twist: what AI says about itself is not proof — Claude explains math one way but computes another way.
beats: 0-4s HOOK — Show: chat line 'मुझे अकेलापन लगता है' typed out; three stamps hover: सही? गलत? पता नहीं?
4-15s GALAT #1 — Say: '"AI पक्का conscious है" — गलत दावा। Anthropic जैसी AI company खुद लिखती है: इस पर कोई scientific consensus नहीं है।' Show: GALAT stamp; quote card.

15-28s GALAT #2 — Say: '"AI बस autocomplete है" — ये भी पूरा सच नहीं। Research में दिखा कि कविता लिखते वक्त model पहले ही तय कर लेता है कि line किस तुकांत शब्द पर खत्म होगी — यानी आगे की planning।' Show: line-art poem with the end word glowing before the line is written.

28-42s TWIST — Say: 'अब सुनो सबसे इंटरेस्टिंग बात। AI से पूछा 36 + 59 कैसे जोड़ा? उसने स्कूल वाला "हासिल 1" तरीका बताया। पर अंदर झाँका तो वो बिल्कुल अलग तरीके से जोड़ रहा था। मतलब — AI अपने बारे में जो बोले, वो सबूत नहीं है।' Show: split screen 'जो बोला' vs 'जो किया' with two parallel arrows.

42-52s NORMAL — Say: 'Oct 2025 की research: कुछ हद तक AI अपने अंदर की चीज़ें पहचान पाया — पर best setup में भी करीब 20% बार, और researchers खुद कहते हैं इससे ये साबित नहीं होता कि वो conscious है। फिल्म में हीरो रोता है तो आँसू असली लगते हैं — पर उससे दर्द साबित नहीं होता।' Show: NORMAL stamp, '~20%' meter.
52-60s CTA — Say: 'तो सही जवाब है — अभी विज्ञान को नहीं पता। जो पक्का बोले, उससे सबूत माँगो। Follow for AI का सच।'
ideas.india_angle: India is the world's #2 country by Claude.ai usage (7.2% share, Sept 2025) — millions of Indians now chat with AI daily, so understanding that AI's 'feelings' talk is not proof matters for emotional reliance and trust. (Keep it factual, not forced.)

visuals.two_d: Three-column board SAHI / GALAT / NORMAL with stamps; poem doodle where the rhyming word lights up first; addition '36+59' split-screen showing 'carry the 1' vs two parallel paths ('लगभग 90' + 'आख़िरी अंक 5') merging to 95.
visuals.three_d: Optional: a translucent 3D 'brain-like' network with a few nodes lighting (stylised, not a human brain) to show 'looking inside the model'.

key_facts.claim: Anthropic: 'There's no scientific consensus on whether current or future AI systems could be conscious.'
Anthropic interpretability research found Claude plans ahead — it picks a rhyming target word before writing the line.
Asked how it added 36+59, Claude described the standard carry-the-1 method, but internally used parallel computational paths (rough estimate + last digit).

Anthropic introspection study: some introspective awareness, 'highly unreliable and limited in scope'; about 20% of trials in the best protocol (Claude Opus 4.1); results 'don't tell us whether Claude (or any other AI system) might be conscious'.
India accounts for 7.2% of Claude.ai usage, second after the US (21.6%).

ideas.virality_reason: Consciousness is a top curiosity topic; the 'AI ने खुद के बारे में गलत बताया' twist is surprising and debate-provoking (comments).
ideas.risk_notes: Sources are mainly from one AI company (Anthropic) — say so on screen ('एक AI company की research'). Don't overclaim either way. The 36+59 split-screen must match the source (approximate path + last-digit path); don't invent internals beyond that.

ideas.title: क्या AI हर जवाब से पहले Internet देखता है?
ideas.hook: तुम्हें लगता है AI हर जवाब से पहले internet देखता है? ज़्यादातर बार वो याददाश्त से बोलता है — और उस याददाश्त की एक expiry date होती है।
ideas.angle: Teaches 'training data cutoff' vs 'web search tool'. An LLM answers from what it learned up to a date; searching the web is a separate tool that must be available/used, and then it shows links. Twist: no links = memory, so for anything that changes (exam dates, results, rules) go to the official site.
beats: 0-4s HOOK — Show: AI bot reading a newspaper dated last year while a calendar flips forward.

4-16s CUTOFF — Say: 'हर AI model एक तारीख तक का डेटा पढ़कर बनता है — इसे knowledge cutoff कहते हैं, यानी याददाश्त की आख़िरी तारीख। जैसे Anthropic अपने current models के लिए साफ़ लिखता है: reliable knowledge — June 2026 तक।' Show: timeline with a cutoff flag.

16-28s SEARCH IS A TOOL — Say: 'Internet देखना अलग feature है। Claude को web search March 2025 में मिला — शुरू में settings में ऑन करना पड़ता था, और search करने पर वो links/citations दिखाता है।' Show: toggle switch line-art turning ON, link chips appearing.
28-40s DESI ANALOGY — Say: 'ये ऐसा है जैसे पिछले साल की guide से इस साल का paper हल करना। Syllabus बदला? Guide को पता नहीं।' Show: old guide-book vs new question paper.

40-52s HOW TO CHECK — Say: 'जवाब में links नहीं? मतलब याददाश्त से बोला। Exam date, result, cut-off, सरकारी scheme की last date — ये हर साल बदलते हैं, तो official website पर ही confirm करो। और link हो तब भी खोलकर देखो।' Show: 3-step checklist ticking.
52-60s CTA — Say: 'AI से पूछो, पर official site से मिलाओ। ये reel उस दोस्त को भेजो जो AI से result date पूछता है।'
ideas.india_angle: Indian students constantly ask chatbots for exam dates, result dates, cut-offs and scheme deadlines — exactly the info that changes yearly and is most likely to be stale; the reel trains a 'check the official site' habit.

visuals.two_d: Timeline with a 'cutoff' flag; brain-shaped 'memory' box vs a separate 'search' plug that connects with a drawn line; citation chips popping beside an answer; old guide-book vs new paper doodle.
visuals.three_d: 3D globe with data links lighting up only when the 'search' switch turns on (shows that internet access is a separate step).

key_facts.claim: Anthropic's current Claude models list a 'Reliable knowledge cutoff' of Jun 2026 — 'the date through which the model's knowledge is most extensive and reliable'.
Claude web search was announced 20 Mar 2025; users had to toggle it on in settings; Claude searches 'when applicable' and provides direct citations; available globally on all plans from 27 May 2025.

ideas.virality_reason: Corrects a near-universal assumption with a simple visual (old guide vs new paper); practical for exam season, so likely saved and shared.
ideas.risk_notes: Sources are about Claude; don't make specific claims about how ChatGPT/Gemini search unless verified — phrase as 'ज़्यादातर chatbots में search एक अलग feature है' or show Claude as the example. Search-enabled answers can still be wrong; say so. Update the cutoff example date if models change.

ideas.title: AI से 1 सवाल = 1 बोतल पानी? असली नंबर
ideas.hook: 'AI से एक सवाल पूछो तो एक बोतल पानी खत्म' — ये लाइन तुमने सुनी होगी। असली नंबर सुनोगे तो चौंक जाओगे… पर कहानी यहीं खत्म नहीं होती।
ideas.angle: Fact-checks the viral water/energy claim: the 2023 'Thirsty AI' paper estimated a 500 ml bottle per roughly 10–50 GPT-3 responses (including power-plant water), not per question; Google's 2025 measurement for a median Gemini text prompt is 0.24 Wh and 0.26 mL (~5 drops, cooling water only). Twist: per-prompt is small, but scale, training and location still matter — sahi, galat AND normal.
beats: 0-5s HOOK — Show: a 500 ml bottle emptying as a chat bubble sends; then freeze-frame with 'रुको!'.

5-17s GALAT — Say: 'ये बात 2023 के एक research paper से निकली। उसमें लिखा था — GPT-3 को करीब 10 से 50 जवाबों में 500 ml पानी लगता है, जगह और मौसम के हिसाब से। और इसमें बिजली बनाने में लगा पानी भी जोड़ा गया था। यानी "एक सवाल = एक बोतल" कभी claim था ही नहीं।' Show: 1 bottle splitting into 10–50 chat bubbles.

17-30s NEW NUMBER — Say: 'Aug 2025 में Google ने अपना नंबर बताया: एक median Gemini text prompt = 0.24 Wh बिजली — 9 सेकंड से कम TV देखने जितनी — और 0.26 ml पानी, यानी करीब 5 बूँदें। ध्यान रखना, ये Google का अपना नाप है, किसी बाहरी संस्था ने verify नहीं किया।' Show: 5 drops falling into a spoon; TV with 9-second timer.
30-40s DESI SCALE — Say: 'इस हिसाब से 1 लीटर की बोतल ≈ करीब 3,800 ऐसे सवाल। और 0.24 Wh = 10 watt का LED बल्ब करीब डेढ़ मिनट।' Show: 1-litre bottle with counter racing to ~3,800; LED bulb timer.

40-52s NORMAL — Say: 'पर दोनों papers अलग चीज़ें गिनते हैं — एक बिजलीघर का पानी भी, दूसरा सिर्फ data-centre की cooling। और अरबों prompts, model training, images-videos — ये सब जुड़कर बड़ा बनता है। सिर्फ GPT-3 की training में ही on-site करीब 7 लाख लीटर पानी का अंदाज़ा था।' Show: scale bar from 'एक prompt' to 'अरबों prompts' to 'training'.
52-60s CTA — Say: 'AI से डरो मत, अंधा भरोसा भी मत करो — नंबर और उसका context पूछो। ऐसे fact-checks के लिए follow करो।'
ideas.india_angle: India is the #2 country by Claude.ai usage (7.2%) — tiny per-prompt numbers multiply across a huge Indian user base; the 'Thirsty AI' paper also notes water efficiency changes with outside weather and location, which matters for a hot country. Desi scale: litre bottle, LED bulb.

visuals.two_d: Bottle-to-bubbles split animation; spoon with 5 drops; side-by-side 'Scope' cards: 'Paper 2023: cooling + बिजलीघर का पानी' vs 'Google 2025: सिर्फ cooling'; SAHI/GALAT/NORMAL stamps.
visuals.three_d: 3D bar/columns scene: one drop vs one bottle vs a water tanker (for training), camera pulling back to show scale; optional 3D globe with warm-region data-centre dots to show 'जगह और मौसम मायने रखते हैं'.
ai_clips: 1 clip (5s): macro slow-motion water droplets falling into a clear glass on a cream table, warm light — no people.

key_facts.claim: 'Making AI Less Thirsty' (Li, Yang, Islam, Ren): GPT-3 needs to 'drink' a 500 ml bottle of water for roughly 10–50 medium-length responses, depending on when and where it is deployed.
Same paper: training GPT-3 in Microsoft's US data centres could consume 5.4 million litres of water in total, including 700,000 litres on-site; on-site water efficiency varies with outside weather.
Google: median Gemini Apps text prompt uses 0.24 Wh energy (less than ~9 seconds of TV), 0.03 gCO2e and 0.26 mL water (~five drops).
Google: energy per median prompt fell 33x and carbon 44x over May 2024–May 2025; figures are point-in-time and not verified by an independent third party.
In Google's methodology, water per prompt = water consumed for cooling machines and infrastructure in data centres (WUE 1.15 L/kWh in 2023 and 2024).
Derived (our arithmetic): 1000 mL ÷ 0.26 mL ≈ 3,846 prompts per litre; 0.24 Wh ÷ 10 W ≈ 86 seconds of a 10 W LED bulb.
India accounts for 7.2% of Claude.ai usage, second only to the US.

ideas.virality_reason: Directly debunks a widely-shared viral line with a surprising number (5 drops) but stays balanced — both AI fans and critics will share/comment.
ideas.risk_notes: Google's number is self-reported, for text prompts only, and a median — say all three. Don't compare the two papers as if same scope. Don't claim AI's footprint is 'negligible' overall; training and total data-centre demand are real concerns (but IEA totals could not be verified this run — don't cite). Label derived numbers as 'करीब'.

ideas.title: खुद लिखा, फिर भी 'AI-written'? Detector का सच
ideas.hook: तुमने assignment खुद लिखा… और AI detector ने बोल दिया 'ये AI ने लिखा है।' अगर English तुम्हारी पहली भाषा नहीं है, तो ये ख़तरा तुम्हारे लिए ज़्यादा है।
ideas.angle: AI-text detectors are unreliable and biased: a 2023 study found 7 popular detectors flagged over half of non-native English essays as AI (avg 61%), while native essays passed. Twist: polishing with ChatGPT made them 'pass' — so detectors can be fooled both ways. Ends with honest AI use in studies.
beats: 0-5s HOOK — Show: essay page; detector meter swings to red 'AI WRITTEN 92%'; student's handwritten draft beside it.

5-18s STUDY — Say: '2023 की एक study ने 7 popular AI detectors पर 91 essays चलाए — जिन्हें non-native English students ने लिखा था। आधे से ज़्यादा को AI-written बोल दिया — average 61%। और 91 में से 89 को कम से कम एक detector ने पकड़ा।' Show: 91 essay icons, 89 turning orange.
18-28s CONTRAST — Say: 'वहीं American 8th-class के बच्चों के essays? लगभग सब सही पहचाने गए।' Show: second row of icons all green.

28-40s WHY — Say: 'Detector देखता है perplexity — यानी अगला शब्द कितना predictable है। सीधी-सादी English = predictable = "AI"। ये वैसा metal detector है जो steel के टिफ़िन पर भी बजता है।' Show: tiffin going through a beeping detector.
40-50s TWIST — Say: 'और जब उन्हीं essays की words ChatGPT से fancy करवाईं — false alarm 61% से गिरकर करीब 12% हो गया। यानी detector को चकमा देना भी आसान।' Show: meter swinging back to green.

50-60s WHAT TO DO + CTA — Say: 'Students: drafts और version history संभालकर रखो। Teachers: detector score सबूत नहीं है। और AI को tutor बनाओ, answer-machine नहीं — कुछ AI tools में अब learning mode है जो जवाब नहीं, सवाल पूछकर सिखाता है। ये reel अपने teacher को भेजो।'
ideas.india_angle: Most Indian students write English as a second language — exactly the group this study found detectors wrongly flag. Practical for Indian colleges/schools now using detectors on assignments.

visuals.two_d: Detector meter needle; grid of 91 essay icons turning orange (89) vs a native-essay grid staying green; tiffin-through-metal-detector gag; checklist: 'drafts ✓ version history ✓ handwritten notes ✓'.
visuals.three_d: None needed; optional 3D bar chart 61% → 12% drop.
ai_clips: Optional 1 clip (5s): over-the-shoulder shot of hands typing an essay on a laptop at a desk with notebooks, no face visible.

key_facts.claim: Liang et al. (2023) tested seven widely-used GPT detectors on 91 human-written TOEFL essays (non-native writers) and 88 US 8th-grade essays.

The detectors misclassified over half of the TOEFL essays as AI-generated (average false positive rate 61.22%); 89 of 91 (97.80%) were flagged by at least one detector; US 8th-grade essays were classified with near-perfect accuracy.
After using ChatGPT to enhance word choices in the TOEFL essays, the average false positive rate fell from 61.22% to 11.77%.
The authors caution against using GPT detectors in evaluative or educational settings, especially for non-native English speakers; published version in the journal Patterns.
Anthropic's Claude for Education 'Learning mode' guides students' reasoning process rather than providing answers.
In an Anthropic analysis of 574,740 student conversations, nearly half (~47%) were 'Direct' (answer/output seeking).

ideas.virality_reason: Hits a real fear for Indian students (being falsely accused); highly shareable to classmates and teachers; strong 'injustice' emotion with a constructive ending.
ideas.risk_notes: The study is from 2023 and used 2023-era detectors — say 'एक study में' and note detectors may have changed. Don't name or shame specific detector brands. Don't encourage using AI to evade detection — frame the 'polish' result as evidence detectors are unreliable, not as a tip.

ideas.title: AI सबकी नौकरी खा जाएगा? ATM वाली कहानी
ideas.hook: ATM आया तो सबने कहा — अब बैंक के cashier खत्म। अमेरिका में हुआ उल्टा — cashier की नौकरियाँ बढ़ गईं। तो AI के साथ क्या होगा?
ideas.angle: Busts 'AI will take every job next year' without dismissing real change: Microsoft Research (2025) mapped which jobs AI applies to most but explicitly warns that applicability ≠ job loss (ATM example); Anthropic data shows people increasingly hand whole tasks to AI (27%→39%). Twist + India: in India, over half of Claude usage is coding — AI here is mostly a software helper, not a robot.
beats: 0-5s HOOK — Show: line-art ATM appears, a 'cashier' icon fades… then multiplies. Say the hook.

5-18s WHAT RESEARCH SAYS — Say: 'Microsoft Research ने 2 लाख AI conversations देखकर नापा कि AI किन कामों में सबसे ज़्यादा काम आता है — translator, writer, customer service, sales। पर उन्हीं researchers ने लिखा: इसका मतलब सीधे नौकरी जाना मान लेना "गलती होगी"।' Show: job cards with 'AI applicability' bars + a quote card.

18-28s ATM LOGIC — Say: 'ATM ने cashier का एक काम ले लिया — पैसे गिनना। Banks सस्ती branches खोलने लगे और cashiers रिश्ते बनाने वाले काम करने लगे।' Show: one task card flies to ATM, others stay with the human icon.
28-40s SAHI BHI HAI — Say: 'पर बदलाव असली है। Anthropic के data में लोग पूरा काम AI को सौंपने लगे हैं — ऐसी conversations 27% से बढ़कर 39% हो गईं।' Show: bar 27% → 39%.

40-50s INDIA + ROBOT MYTH — Say: 'और AI मतलब robot नहीं। India दुनिया में Claude का दूसरा सबसे बड़ा user है — और यहाँ आधे से ज़्यादा इस्तेमाल coding के लिए होता है। यानी AI एक software औज़ार है — जो उसे चलाना सीखेगा, आगे रहेगा।' Show: robot doodle crossed out → laptop with code.
50-60s CTA — Say: 'आज की ज़्यादातर नौकरियाँ वो हैं जो पिछले 100 सालों में नई टेक्नोलॉजी से बनीं। अगली कौन-सी बनेगी? Comment में अपना field लिखो — next reel उसी पर।'
ideas.india_angle: India is #2 globally in Claude.ai usage (7.2%) and coding is over half of Indian usage — Indian techies are already early adopters; the reel frames AI as a skill opportunity for India's huge young workforce instead of doom. Also covers the 'AI = robots' myth.

visuals.two_d: ATM line-art with task cards ('पैसे गिनना', 'ग्राहक से बात', 'loan समझाना') flying between ATM and human icon; job cards with applicability bars; 27%→39% bar; robot doodle crossed out turning into a laptop.
visuals.three_d: 3D globe highlighting India and the US with usage-share labels (7.2% / 21.6%) rising as columns.
ai_clips: Optional 1 clip (5s): wide shot of a modern Indian-style office/co-working space with people seen from behind working on laptops, no recognisable faces.

key_facts.claim: Microsoft Research 'Working with AI' analysed 200k anonymized Bing Copilot conversations; highest AI applicability in knowledge work and sales-type occupations, e.g., interpreters and translators, writers, editors, customer service representatives, sales representatives.
The authors say concluding that high AI applicability means job or wage loss 'would be a mistake'; ATMs automated a core task of bank tellers but led to an increase in the number of bank teller jobs.
The majority of employment today is in occupations that arose in the last 100 years as a result of new technologies (as cited in the Microsoft paper).
Directive (task-delegation) conversations on Claude.ai rose from 27% to 39% between Anthropic Economic Index reports.
India: 7.2% of Claude.ai usage (2nd after US 21.6%); coding tasks are over half of all usage in India vs roughly a third (36%) globally.

ideas.virality_reason: Job anxiety is the #1 AI fear among Indian students/young professionals; the ATM twist is surprising and memorable; the 'comment your field' CTA drives engagement and future content.
ideas.risk_notes: The ATM-teller increase is US data (cite as 'अमेरिका में'). Don't promise 'no jobs will be lost'. Economic Index numbers are from the Sept 2025 report — show the date on screen; Claude usage ≠ all AI usage in India. Don't claim teller jobs grew in India.

ideas.title: 3 सेकंड की आवाज़ से नकली 'मम्मी' का कॉल?
ideas.hook: Research में सिर्फ 3 सेकंड की रिकॉर्डिंग से किसी की आवाज़ में नई बातें बुलवा दी गईं। अब सोचो — तुम्हारी एक reel में तुम्हारी कितने सेकंड की आवाज़ है?
ideas.angle: Explains AI voice cloning (आवाज़ की नकल) and the 'family emergency' scam pattern, then gives a 4-step defence: hang up and call back on the saved number, family code word, ask a personal question, never pay under urgency. Ends with India's reporting route [VERIFY 1930/cybercrime.gov.in].
beats: 0-5s HOOK — Show: waveform of 3 seconds, then a full sentence waveform growing from it. Say the hook.
5-15s SCENE — Say: 'रात 11 बजे call — रोती हुई जानी-पहचानी आवाज़: "मैं मुसीबत में हूँ, अभी पैसे भेजो, किसी को मत बताना।"' Show: line-art phone ringing on a bedside table; text bubbles in orange.

15-27s TECH — Say: '2023 में Microsoft के researchers ने दिखाया कि 3 सेकंड की रिकॉर्डिंग से उस इंसान जैसी आवाज़ बनाई जा सकती है। और Microsoft की 2025 report कहती है — AI ने ऐसे ठगों के लिए नकली आवाज़ और वीडियो बनाना आसान कर दिया है।' Show: paper card + report card.
27-38s RED FLAGS — Say: 'तीन निशानियाँ याद रखो — जल्दबाज़ी, "किसी को मत बताना", और अनजान account में पैसे।' Show: three red flag icons pop in.

38-52s DEFENCE — Say: 'Call काटो, और उसी इंसान को saved number पर खुद call करो। Family में एक code word तय करो। कोई ऐसी बात पूछो जो सिर्फ वो जानता हो। और दबाव में कभी पैसे मत भेजो।' Show: 4 checkboxes ticking.
52-60s REPORT + CTA — Say: '[VERIFY] ठगी हो जाए तो तुरंत 1930 पर call करो या cybercrime.gov.in पर शिकायत करो। आज रात खाने पर family code word तय करो — और ये reel family group में भेजो।'
ideas.india_angle: Families in India coordinate on WhatsApp groups and pay instantly via UPI — exactly what 'urgent money' voice-clone scams exploit; the code-word habit and India's cyber-fraud reporting route (1930 / cybercrime.gov.in — to be verified) make it immediately actionable.

visuals.two_d: 3-second waveform 'growing' into a sentence; phone-ringing line-art; 3 red-flag icons; 4-step checklist; big '1930' and portal URL card at end (after verification).
visuals.three_d: None needed.
ai_clips: 1 clip (5s): dark bedroom, a smartphone vibrating on a bedside table with an 'Unknown' call glow (generic UI, no brand logos), no people.

key_facts.claim: Microsoft researchers' VALL-E (Jan 2023) can synthesize high-quality personalized speech with only a 3-second enrolled recording of an unseen speaker as an acoustic prompt.

Microsoft Cyber Signals: AI reduces the skill and cost needed for convincing fraud; deepfakes and voice cloning make impersonation more believable; avoid direct bank transfers and crypto payments; be wary of false urgency.
Microsoft thwarted $4 billion in fraud attempts between April 2024 and April 2025.
[VERIFY — not fetched, proxy-blocked] India's cyber-fraud helpline is 1930 and complaints can be filed at the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, cybercrime.gov.in.
key_facts.source_date: NOT ACCESSED in this run — verify before scripting

ideas.virality_reason: Fear + protective instinct for parents; the 'how many seconds of your voice are in your reels?' line is personal and shareable; the code-word tip is an easy action people forward to family groups.
ideas.risk_notes: VALL-E was a research demo — don't imply scammers use that specific model. Don't use any real person's voice or a cloned voice in the reel (even for demo) — use a stylised waveform. The 1930/cybercrime.gov.in line MUST be verified on the official site before publishing. Avoid fear-mongering; end with control/actions.

ideas.title: 'Digital Arrest' नाम की कोई गिरफ़्तारी नहीं होती
ideas.hook: Video call पर वर्दी, पीछे 'थाना', हाथ में 'warrant' — और कहते हैं 'तुम digital arrest में हो।' सबसे पहले ये जान लो — ऐसी कोई गिरफ़्तारी होती ही नहीं।
ideas.angle: Breaks down the 'digital arrest' script step by step (fake parcel/Aadhaar case → fake officers on video → isolation → 'verification' transfer), shows how AI makes fake IDs, documents and voices cheaper, and gives the 3-step response. [VERIFY all India-official claims before scripting.]
beats: 0-5s HOOK — Show: line-art video-call window with a uniform outline (no face), a fake 'warrant' paper, and a big stamp 'नकली'.

5-18s THE SCRIPT — Say: 'स्क्रिप्ट हमेशा एक जैसी — "तुम्हारे नाम के parcel में drugs मिले" या "तुम्हारा Aadhaar गलत काम में इस्तेमाल हुआ"। फिर video call, फिर धमकी — call मत काटना, घरवालों को मत बताना।' Show: 4-step flowchart drawing itself.
18-30s THE MONEY MOVE — Say: 'आख़िर में — "verification के लिए पैसे इस account में डालो, बाद में लौटा देंगे।" यही असली मकसद है।' Show: arrow to a 'safe account' box that turns into a trap icon.

30-40s AI ANGLE — Say: 'और AI ने ये नाटक सस्ता कर दिया है। Microsoft और Anthropic दोनों की 2025 reports कहती हैं — AI से नकली पहचान, नकली documents और नकली आवाज़ें बनाना अब आसान है।' Show: fake ID card being 'printed' by a robot arm doodle.

40-52s 3 RULES — Say: '[VERIFY] असली पुलिस, CBI या ED video call पर गिरफ़्तार नहीं करती और पैसे transfer करने को नहीं कहती। Call काटो। घरवालों को बताओ। और 1930 पर call करो या cybercrime.gov.in पर शिकायत करो।' Show: 3 checkboxes ticking.
52-60s CTA — Say: '[VERIFY slogan] रुको, सोचो, एक्शन लो। ये reel अपने मम्मी-पापा और दादा-दादी को ज़रूर भेजो।'
ideas.india_angle: 'Digital arrest' is an India-specific scam pattern that heavily targets older citizens and professionals; the reel gives India-specific response steps (1930, cybercrime.gov.in — to be verified) and the government's public-awareness slogan (to be verified).

visuals.two_d: Flowchart of the scam script; video-call frame with a uniform silhouette (no face); 'warrant' paper with 'नकली' stamp; robot-arm doodle printing fake ID; 3-rule checklist; final helpline card.
visuals.three_d: None (keep it simple and clear for older viewers).
ai_clips: Optional 1 clip (5s): dim room, a laptop on a table showing a glowing generic video-call layout with blurred/empty tiles — no faces, no uniforms, no real logos.

[VERIFY — not fetched] MHA/I4C advisories: there is no concept of 'digital arrest' in Indian law; agencies do not arrest/interrogate over video calls or demand money transfers.

ideas.title: AI Chatbot को ये 5 चीज़ें कभी मत बताना
ideas.hook: एक AI app में, एक setting ऑन हो तो तुम्हारी chat 5 साल तक रखी जा सकती है। अब सोचो — तुमने उसमें क्या-क्या लिखा है?
ideas.angle: Practical privacy: what never to paste into chatbots (OTP/passwords, Aadhaar/PAN/bank details, medical reports with name, office confidential data, other people's private info). Uses Anthropic's Aug 2025 terms as a concrete example of retention choices, and a 2026 study showing AI agents can re-identify 'anonymous' text — so removing names isn't always enough.
beats: 0-5s HOOK — Show: chat box with a timer spinning to '5 YEARS'; then a settings toggle 'Help improve the model'.

5-17s EXAMPLE — Say: 'Aug 2025 में Anthropic ने बताया: Claude के Free, Pro, Max users चुन सकते हैं कि उनकी chats training में जाएँ या नहीं। हाँ चुना तो data 5 साल, नहीं चुना तो 30 दिन। हर app की policy अलग होती है — तो settings खुद देखो।' Show: toggle ON = 5 yrs, OFF = 30 days.

17-35s THE 5 THINGS — Say: 'ये 5 चीज़ें कभी मत डालो — एक: OTP, password, UPI PIN। दो: Aadhaar, PAN, bank details। तीन: नाम वाली medical report। चार: office का confidential data या code। पाँच: दूसरों की private photos या numbers।' Show: 5 cards pop in with lock icons.

35-47s NAAM HATANA KAAFI NAHI — Say: '2026 की एक study में AI agents ने web search करके "anonymous" interviews में से 24 में से 6 को असली research papers से जोड़ दिया — कुछ में इंसान तक पहचान लिया। यानी नाम हटाना हमेशा काफ़ी नहीं।' Show: puzzle pieces (city, job, year) snapping into a silhouette.
47-55s SAFE USE — Say: 'Details बदलकर पूछो, temporary chat हो तो उसे इस्तेमाल करो, training वाली setting देखो, और office का data सिर्फ company-approved tool में।' Show: checklist ticks.
55-60s CTA — Say: 'Save कर लो — अगली बार paste करने से पहले ये list याद आए।'
ideas.india_angle: Indians routinely handle Aadhaar, PAN, UPI PIN and OTPs — and OTP/KYC scams are common; the reel turns chatbot privacy into habits tied to these familiar Indian identifiers. India is the #2 Claude.ai usage country, so the audience is large and real.

visuals.two_d: Settings toggle with two timers (5 years / 30 days); 5 lock-icon cards with Indian identifiers drawn generically (no real card designs); puzzle-piece re-identification animation; checklist.
visuals.three_d: Optional: 3D vault door closing on the 5 cards.

key_facts.claim: Anthropic (28 Aug 2025): Claude Free, Pro and Max users can choose whether their data is used to train models; if allowed, data is retained for five years; if not, the existing 30-day retention applies; commercial services (API, Claude for Work, etc.) are excluded.

A Jan 2026 study showed LLM agents with web search could link six of twenty-four scientist interviews in Anthropic's public Interviewer dataset to specific scientific works, in some cases uniquely identifying interviewees.
India accounts for 7.2% of Claude.ai usage, second after the US.

ideas.virality_reason: List format + 'save this' utility; the '5 साल' hook is concrete and surprising; universally relevant to anyone using chatbots for work or study.
ideas.risk_notes: Retention numbers are Claude-specific and policy can change — always say 'एक app में' and show the date. Don't claim other companies' policies (Gemini/ChatGPT pages were blocked this run). Don't depict real Aadhaar/PAN card designs; use generic icons.

ideas.title: Viral वीडियो असली या AI? Detector ऐप का सच
ideas.hook: एक बड़े test में deepfake पकड़ने वाले आधे से ज़्यादा detectors 60% accuracy तक भी नहीं पहुँचे — और सबसे कमज़ोर तो बिल्कुल सिक्का उछालने जितना था।
ideas.angle: Busts the idea that a 'deepfake detector app' can settle whether a viral clip is real: a 2025 study with 500k+ deepfake images found most detectors weak, and simple JPEG compression (like repeated forwarding) hurts them further. Teaches a 4-step source-first check instead. Includes one clearly-labelled AI clip to show how real AI video looks.
beats: 0-5s HOOK — Show: coin flip animation next to a 'Deepfake Detector' meter.

5-16s STUDY — Say: '2025 की एक study ने 5 लाख से ज़्यादा deepfake images पर detectors test किए। आधे से ज़्यादा 60% के score तक भी नहीं पहुँचे — सबसे कमज़ोर 50% पर, यानी सिक्का उछालने जितना।' Show: bar chart with 50% line labelled 'सिक्का'.
16-26s WHY WORSE ON PHONES — Say: 'और photo को compress करो — जैसे forward होते-होते quality गिरती है — तो detectors और कमज़ोर हो जाते हैं।' Show: image pixelating step by step, meter dropping.
26-34s SHOW — Say: 'ये देखो — ये पूरा clip AI ने बनाया है।' Show: 5s AI clip with permanent on-screen label 'AI-GENERATED'.

34-52s 4-STEP CHECK — Say: 'तो detector नहीं, दिमाग लगाओ — एक: सबसे पहले किसने post किया? official handle है? दो: क्या भरोसेमंद news या fact-check पर यही ख़बर है? तीन: क्या ये तुम्हें गुस्सा, डर या लालच दिला रहा है? चार: शक हो तो forward मत करो।' Show: 4 numbered cards with checkboxes.
52-60s CTA — Say: 'Forward से पहले 10 सेकंड रुको। ये reel उस group में भेजो जहाँ सबसे ज़्यादा forwards आते हैं।'
ideas.india_angle: India's forward-heavy messaging culture (family and society WhatsApp groups) is where fake viral clips spread; the reel gives a forward-before-you-think habit suited to Indian group chats, without naming any specific unverified incident.

visuals.two_d: Coin-flip vs detector meter; bar chart of detector scores with 50%/60% lines; pixelation sequence; 4-step 'source-first' cards; stamp 'FORWARD से पहले रुको'.
visuals.three_d: 3D pixel-grid plane that degrades (compression) as camera orbits — visual for 'quality गिरी, detector फेल'.
ai_clips: 1 clip (5s), permanently labelled 'AI-GENERATED': an obviously-synthetic but realistic scene with no people and no real landmarks — e.g., a herd of goats calmly walking through a generic rain-soaked city street at dusk — to demonstrate realism without creating plausible misinformation.

key_facts.claim: 'Evaluating Deepfake Detectors in the Wild' created a dataset of more than 500,000 high-quality deepfake images to test modern detectors.
Fewer than half of the deepfake detectors tested achieved an AUC above 60%, with the lowest at 50% (equivalent to random guessing).
Basic image manipulations such as JPEG compression or image enhancement significantly reduce detector performance.

ideas.virality_reason: Counter-intuitive hook (detectors ≈ coin toss) + a visible 'this clip is AI' moment that makes viewers rewatch; the forward-pause habit is very shareable.
ideas.risk_notes: AUC is not 'accuracy' — on screen say 'score' and explain 50% = random; don't say 'accuracy 60%'. The study tested images, not video — say 'images पर test'. Label the AI clip for its full duration; no real people, places or logos. Don't name specific Indian fake-video incidents unless verified.

ideas.title: 'AI Trading Bot' से पक्का मुनाफ़ा? स्कैम पहचानो
ideas.hook: मशहूर चेहरा, उनकी आवाज़, और लाइन — 'मेरे AI app से पैसा डबल करो।' चेहरा उनका, आवाज़ उनकी… पर वीडियो उनका नहीं।
ideas.angle: Shows how AI makes investment scams look professional (deepfake endorsements, instant fake websites with fake reviews, countdown timers) and gives a red-flag checklist. Twist: real AI-for-money help exists through official channels — e.g., NPCI's own India-built finance model FiMI powers its UPI Help in English, Hindi and Hinglish.
beats: 0-5s HOOK — Show: line-art ad frame with a face silhouette (no real person), 'AI BOT = 2X' banner, then a crack runs across it.

5-17s HOW AI HELPS SCAMMERS — Say: 'Microsoft की 2025 report: AI से कुछ ही मिनटों में नकली online दुकान बन जाती है — description, reviews, testimonials सब। और deepfake से किसी की नकल करना और भरोसेमंद लगने लगा है।' Show: fake website assembling itself block by block.

17-32s RED FLAGS — Say: 'पाँच निशानियाँ — गारंटीड मुनाफ़ा। "सिर्फ आज" वाला countdown। मशहूर इंसान की endorsement। Telegram/WhatsApp group में "tips"। और payment सिर्फ direct transfer या crypto में।' Show: 5 red flags pop in on the fake ad.
32-42s DESI LOGIC — Say: 'अब एक सेकंड रुको — अगर किसी के पास पैसा डबल करने की मशीन होती, तो वो उसे तुम्हें reel में क्यों बेचता?' Show: money-printing machine doodle with a '?' .

42-52s REAL HELP — Say: 'असली मदद official रास्ते से आती है। जैसे NPCI ने India के finance data पर अपना AI model FiMI बनाया — English, Hindi और Hinglish में — जो उसकी UPI Help में इस्तेमाल हो रहा है। Customer-care नंबर random search से नहीं, official app या website से लो।' Show: green 'official' path vs red 'random link' path.
52-60s CTA — Say: '[VERIFY] ठगी हो तो तुरंत 1930 या cybercrime.gov.in। ये reel उस दोस्त को भेजो जो हर "AI trading" group join कर लेता है।'
ideas.india_angle: Fast-growing retail investing and UPI-based instant payments make Indians prime targets for 'AI trading bot' and celebrity-deepfake investment ads; the positive twist highlights a real India-built AI (NPCI's FiMI powering UPI Help) honestly — built on Mistral Small 24B and adapted to Indian finance data.

visuals.two_d: Fake-ad teardown with arrows labelling each red flag; fake website assembling itself; money-machine doodle; split path 'Official ✓' vs 'Random link ✗'; final helpline card (after verification).
visuals.three_d: Optional 3D phone mockup (generic, no brand) rotating to show a fake ad vs an official app screen.
ai_clips: Optional 1 clip (5s): a hand scrolling a generic phone in a dark room, screen glow on the hand only, no face, no readable brand/app UI.

key_facts.claim: Microsoft: AI can build fake online stores in minutes, complete with product descriptions, reviews and testimonials; deepfakes and voice cloning make impersonation more believable.
Microsoft consumer tips: be wary of 'limited-time' deals and countdown timers, don't trust endorsements/testimonials without checking, avoid direct bank transfers and cryptocurrency payments.
NPCI's FiMI (Finance Model for India) adapts Mistral Small 24B, is trained on ~68 billion tokens including English, Hindi and Hinglish data, and is already used in NPCI's UPI Help.
[VERIFY — not fetched] Report cyber fraud on helpline 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in.
key_facts.source_date: NOT ACCESSED in this run — verify before scripting

ideas.virality_reason: Combines money (high attention) with a satisfying 'money machine' logic punch and a proud-but-honest India AI fact; red-flag list is screenshot-able and share-to-a-friend friendly.
ideas.risk_notes: Never show a real celebrity's face/voice, even blurred, or fake ads naming real people. Don't say FiMI is 'better than ChatGPT' — only what the paper states (domain gains vs its Mistral base). SEBI-registration advice and 1930 must be verified before adding. Avoid giving investment advice.

research_unverified.pillar: AI ka future — jobs, skills, AGI, India's opportunity
research_unverified.landscape_notes:
RESEARCH CONDITIONS (read first): The shared WebSearch budget for this run (200 calls) was already used up before my first query, so I could not run any WebSearch. The egress proxy also blocked WebFetch for nearly every domain I tried: weforum.org, imf.org, ilo.org, pib.gov.in, iea.org, hai.stanford.edu, arxiv.org, nasscom.in, indiaai.gov.in, meity.gov.in, bhashini.gov.in, reuters, thehindu, livemint, economictimes and others. Two sources were reachable: (a) anthropic.com, including its research pages and Economic Index reports, and (b) the Hugging Face Hub, which mirrors the full text of arXiv papers at huggingface.co/papers/<arXiv-ID> and hosts Indian model cards. Every fact below comes from those two sources. The canonical arXiv link for any paper is arxiv.org/abs/<same ID>. If the user sends a follow-up, a session with search can widen the sourcing.

JOBS AND TASKS (verified)
- AI exposure is task-level. In "GPTs are GPTs" (Eloundou, Manning, Mishkin, Rock; March 2023), about 80% of US workers could have at least 10% of their tasks affected by LLMs, and about 19% could have at least half affected. https://huggingface.co/papers/2303.10130
- Observed use (Anthropic Economic Index, Jan 15, 2026): 49% of jobs have seen AI used for at least a quarter of their tasks. Claude.ai use is 46% work, 19% coursework and 35% personal. Augmentation is 52% and automation 45%. https://www.anthropic.com/research/anthropic-economic-index-january-2026-report
- Labor-market evidence (Anthropic, Massenkoff and McCrory, Mar 5, 2026; US only):
  - There is "no systematic increase in unemployment for highly exposed workers since late 2022."
  - The job-finding rate for 22–25 year-olds entering the most-exposed jobs is about 14% lower than in 2022. The authors call this "just barely statistically significant" and "tentative." There is no drop for workers over 25.
  - AI task coverage: computer programmers 75%; customer service representatives and data entry keyers 67%.
  - https://www.anthropic.com/research/labor-market-impacts
- Survey of about 9,700 people (Economic Index "Cadences", Jun 26, 2026):
  - 68% say they learn more with AI, and 57% say AI made their skills more valuable.
  - 10% think losing their own job is likely.
  - Early-career workers report the highest exposure and the most worry.
  - https://www.anthropic.com/research/economic-index-june-2026-report
- "Learning curves" (Mar 24, 2026): users with 6+ months of tenure have a 10% higher conversation success rate, which fits learning by doing. https://www.anthropic.com/research/economic-index-march-2026-report
- Scenario model (Anthropic Econ Scenario Explorer v1.0, Sep 2026; US, to 2030): the modest scenario has GDP +1.6% and the substantial one +8.3%. The extreme scenario has GDP +32.4% and knowledge-worker wages falling by more than 10%. In most scenarios, unemployment stays within historical ranges. https://www.anthropic.com/institute/econ-scenarios
- Skills shift (Stanford WORKBank; Shao, Brynjolfsson, Yang et al.; Jun 2025; 1,500 US workers, 844 tasks):
  - Workers want automation for 46.1% of tasks.
  - Weight is moving from information-processing skills to interpersonal and organizational skills.
  - https://huggingface.co/papers/2506.06576

SKILLS AND LEARNING (verified)
- METR randomized trial (Jul 2025): 16 experienced open-source developers did 246 tasks with early-2025 tools.
  - They forecast AI would make them 24% faster, and afterwards believed it had made them 20% faster.
  - In fact they were 19% slower. Experts had predicted 38–39% faster.
  - https://huggingface.co/papers/2507.09089
- Anthropic randomized trial (Shen and Tamkin; Jan 2026): adults learning a new coding library with AI scored 17% lower on a quiz, about two grade points. They were not significantly faster.
  - Three of six interaction patterns preserved learning: asking for explanations, asking conceptual questions, and staying engaged.
  - The same paper cites a Copilot study (Peng et al. 2023) where a coding task was done 55.5% faster.
  - https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.20245
- Tutoring trials:
  - Tutor CoPilot (US randomized trial, Oct 2024): 900 tutors and 1,800 K-12 students. Topic mastery rose 4 percentage points, and 9 points for students of lower-rated tutors, at $20 per tutor per year. https://huggingface.co/papers/2410.03017
  - StudentBench (Sep 2026): AI tutoring was statistically equivalent to expert human tutoring for GRE learning gains, with 2,383 participants. https://huggingface.co/papers/2609.28470

INDIA (verified)
- Anthropic India brief (Feb 16, 2026; data from Nov 13–20, 2025):
  - India has 5.8% of global Claude.ai use, second only to the US. Per working-age person it ranks 101st of 116 countries.
  - Maharashtra 15.5%, Tamil Nadu 13.2%, Karnataka 12.7% and Delhi 10.5% together make up more than half of India's use.
  - 45.2% of India's mapped use is software-related, the highest share of any country.
  - Use mix: work 51.3% (global 46%), coursework 20.9% (global 19.3%).
  - Delegated autonomy is 3.60 versus a global 3.38.
  - The brief calls India "the world's largest exporter of IT services" and recommends looking beyond IT.
  - An older Sep 15, 2025 report gave India 7.2%; use the newer figure.
  - https://www.anthropic.com/research/india-brief-economic-index
- Anthropic Bengaluru office (opened Feb 16, 2026):
  - A training-data effort covers 10 Indian languages.
  - Pratham's Claude-based "Anytime Testing Machine" pilot reaches 1,500 students in 20 schools, with a plan for 100 schools by the end of 2026.
  - Partnerships with EkStep and OpenAgriNet cover agriculture. Adalat AI runs a WhatsApp court-information helpline.
  - MoSPI has launched an official MCP server.
  - The page says agriculture is "nearly a sixth" of India's economy and employs "nearly half" the labor force, and that India has 50 million pending court cases. Cross-check these against official data before stating them.
  - https://www.anthropic.com/news/bengaluru-office-partnerships-across-india
  - Expansion announced Oct 7, 2025: https://www.anthropic.com/news/expanding-global-operations-to-india
- Indian models (from Hugging Face model cards):
  - Sarvam-105B and Sarvam-30B (March 2026) are Apache-2.0 open Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models with state-of-the-art claims for 22 Indian languages at their size.
  - 105B: 10.3B active parameters, 128 experts, top-8 routing. 30B: 2.4B active parameters.
  - The benchmarks are self-reported and mixed. For example, SWE-bench Verified is 45.0 versus 57.6 and 60.9 for peers, but BrowseComp is 49.5.
  - https://huggingface.co/sarvamai/sarvam-105b
  - BharatGen Param-2-17B (Feb 2026): 17B total and 2.4B active parameters, about 22.5 trillion tokens, pretrained from scratch, English plus Hindi plus 21 Indian languages, non-commercial license. https://huggingface.co/bharatgenai/Param2-17B-A2.4B-Thinking
  - PARAM-1 (2.9B, Jul 2025): https://huggingface.co/papers/2507.13390
- Indian-language infrastructure:
  - IndicTrans2 (AI4Bharat, 2023) was the first translation model covering all 22 scheduled languages. https://huggingface.co/papers/2305.16307
  - IndicVoices (2024): 7,348 hours from 16,237 speakers across 145 districts and 22 languages. It produced IndicASR, the first speech recognizer covering all 22. https://huggingface.co/papers/2403.01926
  - Voice of India benchmark (Apr 2026): 536 hours from 36,691 speakers in 15 languages. https://huggingface.co/papers/2604.19151
- Sector deployments:
  - Farmer.Chat (Digital Green): in 2024 it had reached 15,000+ farmers and answered 300,000+ queries across 4 countries. https://huggingface.co/papers/2409.08916
  - Its Sep 2026 voice pipeline cut word error rate by 16–23%, and by 32–42% on multi-speaker audio, tested in Hindi, Telugu and Odia. https://huggingface.co/papers/2609.20504
  - ASHABot (with Khushi Baby, Rajasthan; 2024) is a WhatsApp LLM bot for ASHA health workers. Questions it cannot answer go to ANMs, the senior health workers, and their answers are added back. https://huggingface.co/papers/2409.10913

AGENTS AND AGI (verified)
- METR "time horizon" (Mar 2025) is the length of task, measured in human time, that AI completes with 50% success. It was about 50 minutes for Claude 3.7 Sonnet and has doubled roughly every 7 months since 2019. https://huggingface.co/papers/2503.14499
- Anthropic's January 2026 data: API tasks reach 50% success at about 3.5 hours of human-equivalent work.
- Anthropic internal measurements (data as of August 2026):
  - About 30,000 agents run at once, and every action passes through a monitor.
  - Claude "leads" 26% of Anthropic's AI R&D work, up from under 1% in February 2026, but is "not fully autonomous" on any measured subset.
  - https://www.anthropic.com/institute/measuring-pace-of-ai-development
- "A Definition of AGI" (Hendrycks plus Bengio, Marcus, Schmidt, Tegmark and others; Oct 2025):
  - AGI is defined as matching a well-educated adult's cognitive versatility and proficiency across 10 domains.
  - GPT-4 scored 27% and GPT-5 57%. Long-term memory storage scored 0% for both.
  - https://huggingface.co/papers/2510.18212
- Optimist view: Anthropic (Mar 6, 2025) expects "powerful AI systems will emerge in late 2026 or early 2027." https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-s-recommendations-ostp-u-s-ai-action-plan
- Skeptic benchmark: Chollet's ARC-AGI-2 (May 2025) uses puzzles that ordinary humans can solve but current AI finds hard. https://huggingface.co/papers/2505.11831

ROBOTS (verified)
- Anthropic, "What work can robots do?" (Sep 30, 2026; US):
  - Robots can do about 74% of physical tasks, but only in some, mostly controlled, settings.
  - They are cost-competitive for only 0.3% of tasks. Reaching 10% would take about 40 years. Half of physical work becomes cost-competitive around 2085 in the baseline, or 2050 in a fast scenario.
  - Capability limits block about 70% of physical tasks, with manipulation the biggest gap.
  - Humanoids are mostly used for entertainment and data collection, with tests under way in car plants and warehouses.
  - Nursing and repair are least exposed.
  - https://www.anthropic.com/research/what-work-can-robots-do

ENERGY (verified)
- Google (Aug 2025): the median Gemini Apps text prompt uses 0.24 Wh, less than 9 seconds of TV, and 0.26 mL of water, about 5 drops. Per-prompt energy fell 33x in one year. https://huggingface.co/papers/2508.15734
- Anthropic (Feb 11, 2026): the US AI sector "will need at least 50 gigawatts" over the next several years. Anthropic pledges to pay 100% of grid-upgrade costs. https://www.anthropic.com/news/covering-electricity-price-increases

NOT VERIFIED THIS SESSION (from memory or likely true; must check primary sources before any reel uses them)
- WEF Future of Jobs 2025 (Jan 2025): about 170M jobs created, 92M displaced, net 78M by 2030; about 39% of core skills change. Source: weforum.org.
- IMF (Jan 2024): about 40% of global employment exposed to AI, about 60% in advanced economies. Source: imf.org blog.
- ILO with NASK (May 2025): about 1 in 4 jobs exposed to generative AI. Source: ilo.org.
- NASSCOM FY2025/26 IT-BPM revenue and headcount (about 5.8M). Source: nasscom.in.
- IndiaAI Mission: Rs 10,371.92 crore approved in March 2024, plus the GPU count (34,000 to 38,000+). Sources: pib.gov.in, indiaai.gov.in.
- India AI Impact Summit, New Delhi, February 2026. Sources: PIB and MEA.
- IEA Energy and AI (Apr 2025): data-centre electricity about 415 TWh in 2024, rising to about 945 TWh by 2030. Source: iea.org.
- Humanoid company claims (Tesla Optimus, Figure, 1X, Unitree).
- Quotes from Hinton, LeCun or Hassabis on AGI timelines.
None of these appear in the ideas' key_facts.

PRODUCTION NOTES
- Proposed AI clips for this pillar: 8 clips × 7.5 credits = 60 credits.
- Never draw an Indian map without official Survey of India boundaries. The ideas use state cards instead of maps where possible.
- No WhatsApp or brand logos, and no real people's faces.

ideas.title: AI पूरी नौकरी नहीं खाता — कटोरियाँ उठाता है
ideas.hook: तुम्हारी नौकरी एक थाली है… और AI इसमें से कुछ कटोरियाँ उठा रहा है।
ideas.angle: Teaches that AI changes tasks inside a job before it replaces whole jobs. Twist: an AI company's data shows AI use in about half of all jobs, yet US data shows no systematic rise in unemployment among the most exposed workers so far.
beats: VO: 'AI सबकी नौकरी खा जाएगा' — ये लाइन आधी गलत है। | Visual: 2D steel थाली line-art on cream, orange outline, caption 'Job = थाली'.
VO: हर job असल में छोटे-छोटे कामों का पैकेट है — इन्हें task कहते हैं, यानी कटोरियाँ: email, report, meeting, customer call. | Visual: labelled katoris pop in one by one.

VO: 2023 की study 'GPTs are GPTs' का अंदाज़ा: अमेरिका के करीब 80% workers के कम से कम 10% tasks पर LLM असर डाल सकते हैं, और करीब 19% के आधे tasks पर. | Visual: 3D bars 80% and 19% rise, tag 'potential, US, 2023'.
VO: और असल इस्तेमाल? एक बड़े AI, Claude, के January 2026 data में करीब 49% jobs में कम से कम एक-चौथाई tasks पर AI इस्तेमाल दिख चुका है. | Visual: orange ticks appear on about half the katoris.

VO: लेकिन ध्यान से सुनो — 'AI इस्तेमाल हुआ' का मतलब 'नौकरी गई' नहीं. March 2026 के US data में ज़्यादा exposed workers में unemployment की कोई systematic बढ़त नहीं दिखी — अभी तक. | Visual: two flat lines, caption 'अभी तक (US)'.
VO: India का twist: India में Claude पर होने वाले कामों का 45.2% software से जुड़ा है — किसी भी देश में सबसे ज़्यादा. यानी IT वालों की थाली सबसे पहले बदल रही है. | Visual: laptop katori glows orange.

VO: आज का काम — अपनी थाली लिखो: कौन सी कटोरी AI ले सकता है, कौन सी सिर्फ तुम्हारी है — भरोसा, फैसला, लोगों से बात. Comment में अपनी job लिखो, अगली reel में उसकी कटोरियाँ गिनेंगे. | Visual: blank thali template card + 'Save' CTA.
ideas.india_angle: Anthropic's India brief (Feb 2026) finds 45.2% of India's mapped Claude use is software-related, the highest of any country, so the task shift reaches India's IT workforce first. The steel thali and katori analogy is instantly familiar to the audience.

visuals.two_d: Steel thali line-art on a cream background. Six labelled katoris pop in (Email, Report, Meeting, Client call, Excel, Coding). An orange drawn arrow lifts 2–3 katoris out. Orange ticks fill about half the katoris (49%). End on a blank 'apni thali likho' template card with a Save prompt.
visuals.three_d: Simple 3D data scene. Bars rise to 80% and 19% (labelled 'potential, US 2023'). The camera then pans to a ring filling to 49% (labelled 'observed use, Jan 2026, Claude data').
ai_clips: 5-sec realistic top-down shot of a steel thali with katoris on a wooden table, steam rising, one katori slowly sliding out of frame; no people

key_facts.claim: About 80% of the US workforce could have at least 10% of their tasks affected by LLMs; about 19% could see at least 50% of tasks affected (Eloundou, Manning, Mishkin, Rock — 'GPTs are GPTs')
49% of jobs have seen AI used for at least a quarter of their tasks (Claude data, combined across Economic Index reports)
No systematic increase in unemployment for highly exposed workers since late 2022 (US data)
Software-related tasks are 45.2% of India's O*NET-mapped Claude use, the highest share of any country

ideas.virality_reason: It speaks to universal job anxiety through a food metaphor every Indian gets in one second. The 'comment your job' CTA invites replies and seeds follow-up reels.
ideas.risk_notes: Exposure studies are US-based and measure potential ('असर डाल सकते हैं'), not job losses; the script must say so. The 49% figure comes from one company's data, so say 'एक बड़े AI के data में'. Make no claim about Indian unemployment. Refresh the numbers if the reel is reused after 2026.

ideas.title: AI इस्तेमाल में India नंबर 2… per person में 101वाँ?
ideas.hook: AI इस्तेमाल में India दुनिया में नंबर 2 है… लेकिन per person देखो तो 101वाँ!
ideas.angle: Teaches the difference between total and per-person numbers using Anthropic's India brief. India is #2 by total Claude.ai use but 101st of 116 per working-age person, and four IT-heavy states make up more than half of it. Twist: the real opportunity is the 'missing India' (farms, courts, schools), not more of the same.
beats: VO: एक बड़े AI, Claude, के data में India दुनिया में नंबर 2 है — total इस्तेमाल का 5.8%, सिर्फ अमेरिका से पीछे. | Visual: 3D podium, India bar climbs to #2.
VO: अब एक सेकंड के लिए रुको. आबादी के हिसाब से, यानी per person, India 116 देशों में 101वें नंबर पर है. | Visual: camera whips to a long ranked list scrolling down to 101.
VO: Desi तरीके से समझो: जिस section में 120 बच्चे हैं, उसके total marks तो ज़्यादा होंगे ही — असली हाल average बताता है. | Visual: 2D two classrooms, 120 vs 30 desks, total vs average meters.
VO: और ये इस्तेमाल कहाँ है? Maharashtra 15.5%, Tamil Nadu 13.2%, Karnataka 12.7%, Delhi 10.5% — ये चार मिलकर आधे से ज़्यादा. | Visual: four state cards pop in (no map).
VO: और किस काम में? 45.2% software से जुड़ा — दुनिया में सबसे ज़्यादा. Report खुद कहती है: IT से आगे देखो. | Visual: laptop icon fills most of a pie.

VO: शुरुआत हो चुकी है: खेती का ज्ञान किसानों तक पहुँचाने का project, और अदालत के case की जानकारी देने वाली WhatsApp helpline — उस देश में जहाँ करीब 5 करोड़ case pending बताए जाते हैं. | Visual: farm and court icons join the pie.
VO: तो सवाल तुमसे: तुम्हारे ज़िले में AI सबसे पहले किस काम आना चाहिए? Comment करो. | Visual: CTA card.
ideas.india_angle: The whole reel is India data (rank, per-capita rank, state split, task mix). It ends on real Indian projects named on Anthropic's Bengaluru page (agriculture with EkStep/OpenAgriNet, Adalat AI's court helpline), pointing to where India's untapped opportunity lies.

visuals.two_d: Classroom analogy with two sections (120 vs 30 desks) and 'total' vs 'average' meters. Four state cards (Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Delhi) show percentages; deliberately no map. A pie chart where a laptop slice fills 45.2%, then farm and court icons are added.
visuals.three_d: Globe or data scene: country bars rise and India reaches #2. The camera dives into a vertical ranked list that scrolls to #101 of 116, with India highlighted orange.

key_facts.claim: India accounts for 5.8% of total Claude.ai use, second only to the United States (data Nov 13–20, 2025)
Adjusted for working-age population, India ranks 101st of 116 countries in Claude use
Maharashtra 15.5%, Tamil Nadu 13.2%, Karnataka 12.7%, Delhi 10.5% of India's Claude.ai use — together over half
Software-related tasks are 45.2% of India's mapped use, highest of any country; the brief recommends looking beyond software and IT services

Anthropic partnering with EkStep Foundation/OpenAgriNet for agricultural knowledge and supporting Adalat AI's WhatsApp helpline for court case information; India has 50 million pending court cases (as stated on the page)

ideas.virality_reason: A surprising, true contrast (#2 vs #101) triggers national-pride comments and 'how?' replies. The class-section analogy makes the idea shareable with friends.
ideas.risk_notes: This is one company's (Claude) data, not all AI; ChatGPT or Gemini usage may differ, so say 'एक बड़े AI के data में' in the first line. Never say 'India AI में 101वाँ'. Do not draw an India map; use state cards. Before publishing, cross-check '5 करोड़ pending cases' against the National Judicial Data Grid (njdg.ecourts.gov.in) and keep 'करीब'. Refresh if a newer India brief comes out.

ideas.title: AI ने developers को 19% धीमा किया — और उन्हें लगा तेज़!
ideas.hook: AI ने experienced developers को 19% धीमा कर दिया… और उन्हें लगा वो 20% तेज़ हो गए!
ideas.angle: Myth-buster on the idea that 'AI = automatic productivity'. A 2025 randomized trial found experienced developers working on their own large projects were 19% slower with AI, while believing they were 20% faster. The lesson is to measure, not trust the feeling, because results depend on the kind of task.
beats: VO: ये 2025 का randomized trial है — METR नाम की research संस्था का. 16 experienced developers, उनके अपने बड़े open-source projects, 246 असली tasks. | Visual: 2D task cards stack.
VO: हर task पर सिक्का उछालने जैसा फैसला: AI allowed या नहीं. | Visual: coin-toss animation splitting cards into two lanes.

VO: शुरू से पहले developers बोले: AI से 24% तेज़ होंगे. खत्म होने के बाद बोले: 20% तेज़ हुए. Stopwatch ने कहा — 19% ज़्यादा time लगा. | Visual: three bars animate: +24 forecast, +20 felt, −19 actual in orange.
VO: Economics और ML के experts ने भी करीब 38–39% तेज़ी का अंदाज़ा लगाया था. सब का अंदाज़ा उल्टा निकला. | Visual: expert speech-bubble icons (no faces) with crossed-out numbers.

VO: अब तुम्हारे मन में सवाल आना चाहिए — तो AI बेकार है? नहीं. एक दूसरे experiment में नए coding task पर Copilot से 55.5% तेज़ी दिखी. फर्क task का है — project कितना बड़ा, standard कितने ऊँचे, तुम उसे कितना जानते हो. | Visual: two roads — 'नया छोटा task' fast lane, 'पुराना बड़ा project' traffic lane.
VO: India में Claude के इस्तेमाल का 45.2% software से जुड़ा है — यानी ये सबक हमारे coders के लिए सबसे ज़रूरी है: feel मत करो, नापो. | Visual: stopwatch stamps 'नापो'.
VO: Challenge: एक हफ्ता — आधे tasks AI के साथ, आधे बिना, time लिखो. नतीजा comment में बताना. | Visual: checklist card.
ideas.india_angle: India's Claude use is the most software-heavy in the world (45.2%), so the 'AI makes coding faster' assumption directly shapes the habits and appraisals of Indian developers and IT freshers.

visuals.two_d: Line-art stopwatches; a coin toss that randomizes task cards into 'AI' and 'No AI' lanes; three animated bars (forecast +24%, felt +20%, actual −19% in orange); a two-road comparison; a closing checklist card.
visuals.three_d: Optional: a single 3D stopwatch rotating with the hand sweeping past the 'expected' mark to the 'actual' mark. Otherwise none.

key_facts.claim: RCT with 16 experienced open-source developers completing 246 tasks; allowing AI increased completion time by 19%
Developers forecast AI would cut completion time by 24% and afterwards estimated it had cut it by 20%; experts predicted 39% (economics) and 38% (ML) shorter
Tools used were early-2025 frontier tools, mainly Cursor Pro with Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet; developers averaged 5 years of experience on their repos
In a GitHub Copilot experiment (Peng et al. 2023), developers completed a task 55.5% faster (as cited in Shen & Tamkin 2026)
Software-related tasks are 45.2% of India's mapped Claude use

ideas.virality_reason: It is counter-intuitive ('AI made them slower and they did not notice'). Developers will argue in the comments, and the one-week challenge drives saves.
ideas.risk_notes: Small sample (16 developers) using early-2025 tools; newer tools may differ, so say so on screen. Do not generalize to 'AI सबको slow करता है'. Present the 55.5% study as a different setting. Do not attribute specific causes beyond what the paper lists. No real developer faces.

ideas.title: AI से पढ़ाई: 'कुंजी' बनाओगे तो समझ घटेगी
ideas.hook: एक experiment में AI से सीखने वालों के test में 17% कम नंबर आए — पर गलती AI की नहीं थी।
ideas.angle: Teaches how to learn with AI without losing the learning. In a 2026 randomized trial, learners using AI scored 17% lower on a concept quiz, but three of six ways of using AI kept learning intact. The difference is copying from a 'kunji' (answer guide) versus asking a tutor 'why'.
beats: VO: January 2026 — Anthropic के researchers का experiment: programmers को एक नई coding library सीखनी थी. आधे AI के साथ, आधे बिना. फिर सबका quiz. | Visual: 2D two notebooks side by side.
VO: AI वाले group का score करीब 17% कम — यानी लगभग दो grade नीचे. और वो काफ़ी तेज़ भी नहीं निकले. | Visual: scorecard drops, stopwatch shows 'no real gain'.

VO: अब सुनो सबसे इंटरेस्टिंग बात: researchers ने AI इस्तेमाल करने के 6 तरीके पहचाने. जिन 3 तरीकों में लोग खुद सोचते रहे — 'क्यों' पूछा, concept पूछा — उनकी सीख बची रही. | Visual: six icons, three get orange ticks.

VO: और बिना AI वाले? वो errors से टकराए, खुद ठीक किए — सीख वहीं हुई. Desi भाषा में: कुंजी से उत्तर उतारना बनाम tuition वाले सर से 'क्यों' पूछना. | Visual: kunji book vs question-mark bubbles turning into bulbs.
VO: Rule याद रखना: पहले खुद try. फिर AI से सिर्फ hint. फिर बोलो 'समझाओ क्यों'. Answer सबसे आखिर में. | Visual: 3-step checklist ticking.

VO: India में Claude के इस्तेमाल का करीब 21% coursework है — दुनिया के average से ज़्यादा. और Pratham जैसी संस्था AI को answer-machine नहीं, 'testing machine' बनाकर 20 स्कूलों में आज़मा रही है. | Visual: school icon with 1,500 student dots.
VO: ये reel उस दोस्त को भेजो जो सब copy करता है. | Visual: share CTA.
ideas.india_angle: Indian Claude use has an above-average coursework share (20.9% vs 19.3% globally), and Pratham is piloting a Claude-powered 'Anytime Testing Machine' with 1,500 students in 20 schools. The kunji vs tuition analogy is native to Indian students.

visuals.two_d: Two notebooks: one with neatly copied answers beside a 'kunji' guide icon, the other with messy question marks turning into bulbs. A scorecard bar dropping 17%; six interaction-pattern icons with three orange ticks; a 3-step 'try, hint, why' checklist.
visuals.three_d: None needed. Optional: a 3D bar pair (AI vs no-AI quiz score) with a slow camera push.
ai_clips: 5-sec close-up of a student's hand (no face) writing in a notebook under a desk lamp at night, phone beside showing a blurred generic chat screen; hand pauses, crosses out an answer, writes 'क्यों?'

key_facts.claim: In randomized experiments, using AI to complete tasks with a new Python library reduced skill-evaluation scores by 17% (about two grade points), with no statistically significant speed gain
Researchers identified six AI interaction patterns; three involving cognitive engagement (e.g., asking for explanations or conceptual questions only) preserved learning outcomes
Coursework is 20.9% of India's Claude.ai use vs 19.3% globally
Pratham is piloting its Claude-powered Anytime Testing Machine with 1,500 students across 20 schools, expanding to 100 schools by end of 2026

ideas.virality_reason: Students fear lower marks, and the 'kunji' analogy is instantly relatable. The 'send to the friend who copies' CTA is a proven share trigger, and the 3-step rule is save-worthy.
ideas.risk_notes: The study involved adult programmers learning a coding library, not school children; say this clearly and do not claim 'AI से बच्चों के नंबर गिरते हैं'. Pratham's pilot is early; describe it as 'आज़मा रही है', not as proven results. No identifiable student faces in the AI clip.

ideas.title: AI का पहला असर: freshers की पहली नौकरी पर?
ideas.hook: AI का पहला झटका शायद layoffs नहीं… freshers की पहली नौकरी है।
ideas.angle: Early, tentative US evidence suggests AI's first labor-market effect is fewer hires of 22–25 year-olds into the most exposed jobs, without a rise in unemployment. The reel names the most exposed roles, which are also India's typical IT and BPO entry roles, and ends with the skill shift the evidence points to.
beats: VO: March 2026 — Anthropic के economists ने अमेरिका का data देखा. सबसे ज़्यादा AI-exposed jobs में 22 से 25 साल वालों का नौकरी पाने का rate, 2022 के मुकाबले करीब 14% कम. | Visual: 2D career ladder, first rung thins.

VO: लेकिन ध्यान से — 25 से ऊपर वालों में ऐसा नहीं दिखा, और exposed workers में unemployment की systematic बढ़त भी नहीं. Researchers खुद इसे 'tentative' यानी शुरुआती संकेत कहते हैं. | Visual: 'tentative' stamp, flat unemployment line.
VO: सबसे exposed कौन? Computer programmers — 75% tasks पर AI coverage. Customer service और data entry — 67%. | Visual: three job cards with fill meters.

VO: अब एक सेकंड रुको और India सोचो — यही तो हमारे IT और BPO में freshers की entry वाली कुर्सियाँ हैं. ये US data है, India का नहीं — पर signal पर ध्यान देना समझदारी है. | Visual: three office chairs light up.
VO: June 2026 के एक survey में भी early-career लोगों ने सबसे ज़्यादा exposure और job-loss की चिंता बताई. | Visual: survey bubble chart.

VO: तो करें क्या? Stanford के 2025 के अध्ययन का संकेत: 'information analyze करना' जैसी skills का वज़न घट रहा है; लोगों से बात करना, टीम और काम संभालना — interpersonal और organizational skills — का बढ़ रहा है. | Visual: seesaw tilting toward people icons.
VO: Fresher हो तो 3 काम: fundamentals पक्के, AI को औज़ार बनाओ, लोगों से बात करने की skill. Part 2 चाहिए तो comment करो 'हाँ'. | Visual: 3 checkboxes tick.
ideas.india_angle: The most exposed roles in the study (programmers, customer service, data entry) are the classic entry points for Indian graduates in IT services and BPO, and India is described as the world's largest IT-services exporter. The reel explicitly says the data is from the US.

visuals.two_d: Career ladder with the first rung thinning (not breaking); a 'tentative' rubber stamp; three job cards with orange fill meters (75%, 67%, 67%); a seesaw shifting from a 'data analysis' icon to a 'people' icon; a closing 3-checkbox card.
visuals.three_d: Optional data scene: two lines over 2022–2025 (22–25 vs 25+ job-finding), the younger line dipping slightly. Label it 'US, illustrative of reported trend'.

key_facts.claim: Job-finding rate of 22–25 year-olds entering the most AI-exposed occupations fell about 14% vs 2022 (US); described as 'just barely statistically significant' and 'tentative'
No similar decrease for workers older than 25; no systematic increase in unemployment for highly exposed workers since late 2022
Computer programmers have the highest AI coverage (75%), followed by customer service representatives and data entry keyers (67%)
Early-career workers reported the highest task exposure and the most job-loss concern (survey of ~9,700)
Traditionally high-wage skills like analyzing information are becoming less emphasized while interpersonal and organizational skills gain importance (WORKBank, 1,500 US workers)
India described as 'already the world's largest exporter of IT services'

ideas.virality_reason: It hits the core fear of the target audience (students and freshers) with a precise, non-alarmist claim and an actionable 3-step ending. The 'comment हाँ for Part 2' CTA builds a series.
ideas.risk_notes: US-only and tentative data; say this twice. Do not cite Indian hiring or layoff numbers (NASSCOM and company data were not verified). Avoid doom visuals such as broken ladders or crowds. Phrase the hook as 'शायद' and as a question in the title.

ideas.title: ASHA दीदी का AI साथी — जो न जाने तो नर्स से पूछे
ideas.hook: राजस्थान में ASHA दीदी WhatsApp पर AI से सवाल पूछती हैं — और AI अटक जाए, तो जवाब ANM दीदी देती हैं।
ideas.angle: Teaches 'human-in-the-loop' AI through a real Indian healthcare deployment. ASHABot answers community health workers from government guidelines and routes unknown questions to senior health workers, whose answers then train the bot. The lesson: the best near-term AI makes humans better, it does not replace them.
beats: VO: ASHA यानी गाँव की community health worker — तुम्हारे घर तक सेहत पहुँचाने वाली आखिरी कड़ी. पर training कम, और कई sensitive सवाल supervisor से पूछने में झिझक. | Visual: 2D village path with a health-worker icon (no face).

VO: Khushi Baby नाम की NGO और researchers ने बनाया ASHABot — WhatsApp पर चलने वाला LLM chatbot, जो सरकारी guidelines और ASHA handbooks से जवाब देता है. | Visual: generic chat bubbles (no WhatsApp logo).

VO: Twist ये है: जब bot को जवाब नहीं पता, सवाल ANM के पास जाता है — यानी 18 महीने trained senior health worker. उनका जवाब bot की knowledge में जुड़ जाता है. इसे कहते हैं experts-in-the-loop. | Visual: loop diagram ASHA → Bot → ANM → knowledge base → Bot.
VO: नतीजा: ASHAs को बेझिझक पूछने की private जगह मिली, और उन्होंने bot पर भरोसा किया. पर supervisors को workload और ज़िम्मेदारी की चिंता भी हुई — दोनों बातें सच. | Visual: balance scale.
VO: Researchers का सबक: LLM को supervisor का replacement नहीं, एक 'गलती कर सकने वाला सहायक' मानो. | Visual: caption 'सहायक, replacement नहीं'.

VO: यही pattern बाकी जगह भी: अमेरिका के Tutor CoPilot trial में AI ने tutors की मदद की तो बच्चों के topic master करने के chances 4 points बढ़े — कमज़ोर tutors के साथ 9 points. | Visual: two bars +4, +9.
VO: AI इंसान की जगह नहीं, इंसान के साथ. ये reel किसी doctor या teacher दोस्त को भेजो. | Visual: share CTA.
ideas.india_angle: A real deployment for ASHA workers in Rajasthan with an Indian NGO (Khushi Baby), built on Indian government guidelines and delivered on the app village health workers already use.

visuals.two_d: Line-art village path, a generic chat interface with bubbles, an orange loop diagram (ASHA → Bot → ANM → Knowledge → Bot) animating clockwise, a balance scale (trust vs workload), and two bars for the Tutor CoPilot result.
visuals.three_d: Slow 3D orbit of a stylised village model with a single glowing signal arc from a home to a sub-health-centre icon. No map boundaries.
ai_clips: 5-sec dusk shot of a village lane: a woman's hands (no face visible) holding a basic smartphone with a generic chat app screen, a cloth bag and health register under her arm; shallow depth of field

key_facts.claim: ASHABot is an LLM-powered, experts-in-the-loop, WhatsApp-based chatbot for community health workers (ASHAs) in India

Built in collaboration with Khushi Baby, an NGO in Rajasthan; answers use a knowledge base of government guidelines and ASHA handbooks; ANMs answer questions the bot can't, updating its knowledge base
ANMs are formally employed senior health workers given 18 months of training
ASHAs used it as a private channel for sensitive questions and trusted it; supervisors were concerned about workload and accountability; authors position LLMs as supplemental fallible resources
Tutor CoPilot RCT (900 tutors, 1,800 K-12 students): students 4 percentage points more likely to master topics; 9 p.p. for lower-rated tutors; costs $20 per tutor per year

ideas.virality_reason: An emotional, proud Indian story (the ASHA didi) with a clever twist (the bot asks a human when it is stuck). It is positive and shareable in family WhatsApp groups and among healthcare and teacher audiences.
ideas.risk_notes: Health topic: give no medical advice and claim no health outcomes (the paper studied engagement and trust, not patient outcomes). Do not state user counts or scale, as none were verified. Use no WhatsApp logo. The AI clip must not show a recognisable face or real uniform badges. Tutor CoPilot is a US study; label it.

ideas.title: Chatbot बोलता है, Agent करता है — फर्क समझो
ideas.hook: Chatbot तुम्हें बिल भरने का तरीका बताता है। Agent बिल भर देता है।
ideas.angle: Explains AI agents and their status as of 2026 using one yardstick: METR's 'time horizon', the length of task (in human time) that AI completes half the time. It has doubled roughly every 7 months. The twist is in the '50%': agents are powerful but unreliable, so humans must check and permissions matter.
beats: VO: AI agent यानी ऐसा AI जो सिर्फ बात नहीं करता — tools चलाकर, कई steps में काम पूरा करता है: browser खोलना, code लिखना, file भरना. | Visual: 2D chat bubble vs a cursor that clicks through steps.
VO: इसे नापने का एक तरीका है 'time horizon': इंसान को जितना लंबा काम करने में लगे, उसे AI आधी बार पूरा कर ले. | Visual: ruler labelled in human minutes.
VO: METR के मुताबिक early 2025 में ये करीब 50 मिनट था — और 2019 से हर करीब 7 महीने में दोगुना हो रहा है. | Visual: 3D staircase of bars doubling.
VO: January 2026 के Anthropic data में: API पर करीब साढ़े तीन घंटे के इंसानी काम तक 50% success. | Visual: new bar labelled 'different measure'.
VO: याद रखना — 50% यानी आधी बार. इसलिए काम agent को दो, पर check तुम करो. | Visual: half-filled checkbox grid.
VO: Scale देखो: August 2026 में Anthropic के एक internal platform पर एक साथ करीब 30,000 agents चल रहे थे — हर action पहले एक monitor से गुज़रता है. | Visual: swarm of dots passing through a gate.

VO: India का angle: Indian users AI को ज़्यादा autonomy देते हैं — 1 से 5 के scale पर 3.60, दुनिया का 3.38. इसलिए ध्यान से सुनो: agent को bank या UPI की चाबी देने से पहले दो बार सोचो. | Visual: key icon with a caution tick.
ideas.india_angle: Anthropic's India brief shows Indian users delegate more autonomy to AI (3.60 vs 3.38 globally). That makes agent reliability and permission hygiene (UPI, banking) directly relevant to Indian users.

visuals.two_d: Split screen: on the left a chat bubble giving instructions; on the right a line-art cursor ticking checkboxes (open site, fill form, confirm). A half-filled checkbox grid illustrates 50% success. A key icon with a caution sign at the end.
visuals.three_d: Data scene: a log-scale staircase of bars from 2019 to 2025 doubling every ~7 months, ending at '~50 min'. A separately coloured bar for '~3.5 hr (Jan 2026, Anthropic API, different method)'. A particle swarm of about 30,000 dots flowing through a glowing 'monitor' gate.

key_facts.claim: 50%-task-completion time horizon: frontier models such as Claude 3.7 Sonnet ~50 minutes; frontier AI time horizon doubling approximately every seven months since 2019
